Better to bring your own food and water The beach was pretty... But this month of August, the waves were too big for swimming and there were too many rocks and coral pieces all around for comfort. The coral pieces are all along the beach, which makes for a nice thing to look at but bad for walking on sand.  Not soft sand. Not a good swimming beach. I went in and the waves crashed me down and my foot hit a rock. Got some big scratches. There's a few places there to order drinks and food, but are bloody expensive. The benefit is that there are chairs to sit and lounge on. Wouldn't come back to this beach.
This serene beach is surrounded by a strip of vegetation and rock formations. There is a 5min hike through a jungle area where at the end we are presented with this mesmerizing beach.

We came here in the morning in the second week of July. There were few other people around and so it was not crowded. We saw several large monitor lizards. The water was calm and refreshing for swimming. We took a tuk tuk to the top of the hill and hiked down from what the driver called the "tourist entrance" which came out at the little restaurant. Then we went to the left of the restaurant over some rocks to a little cove to swim. We did not find this area dirty. There was a path up the hill from this area to the pagoda where we caught another tuk tuk back to our villa.
Very small beach with a lot of rubbish on the sand - even a needle!! Only one eating place on the beach.

This is a nice sheltered cove that avoids the pounding from the big rolling waves of the Indian Ocean. There's not a lot in terms of facilities but there is good natural shade and safe bathing. Makes a nice place for a day if you are in the area although coach loads of tourists turning up for a quick gawp does take the shine off it
Need to trek down the hill a bit to get to this beach but the views are worth it. Can be difficult for small children and elders. Beach does get crowded a bit.

I've heard of Jungle Beach, the secluded stretch of beach just west of Unawatuna, for awhile now. I eventually made my way one afternoon and couldn't help feel a bit uncomfortable. In the offseason, there's fewer tourists everywhere and being 1 of only 3 other tourists after walking down a long jungle path to the beach was a bit eerie. Staff were eager and the water was not as clean since it's now in the bay with the Galle harbour. If you're visiting from April to October, best just stay on the Unawatuna main beach area. It's much nicer anyway.

I liked this place, just the small road to the beach..you need to walk there carefully. The waves there was pretty big and it is getting deep very fast. Anyway it is beautiful place where to take rest and seems that that place atract those who like to play some music instrument. During my stay there 2 big groups of people came and were playing music instruments..so it made the place look even better.

It takes some effort to reach Jungle beach but it is an amazing experience down there. Sea is calm in the morning and as you swim, you will get to see amazing views. There is a small stall where you can buy refreshments and snacks. Just bring your towel and some change, you will be good to go.

This is a secluded beach front remote to Galle. To reach there, half of the way you can hire a Tuk Tuk, next half you have to trek though forest pathway. Place is good for swimming and snorkeling as well.

It's a private beach and a mini trek to get there. Recommend going there in the morning or before 6:00 pm as the jungle to get there has no lights in the evening. If it's dark while returning, I suggest the traveller to carry a torch light. A must visit while you are staying in and around Cantaloupe Levels and surrounding resorts.

Too much PR of this place but as for me nothing special . Just nice beach but not more then this . U can try 1-2 times . To go there cost like 200 rubies on tuktuk. Ask discount usualy they Agree for 200..

I had to do some figuring before I could reach this place. My tuk-tuk driver was not aware of this beach so I used google maps to finally reach there. I visited this place in early morning. The trail is easy but full of garbage. It’s not often you get to wander a empty beach. The waves were crawling gently to the shore. There was only one empty boat in the sea which completed the view. One can smell the fresh air of ocean. Its best to avoid this place after weekend parties as garbage compiles up. Also this it gets over crowded easily as it is a small beach. Best time to visit is early morning.

Worth the little walk to find the place! There are actually two beaches connected and both are worth checking out. I loved that it was less tourist oriented and there were lots of locals hanging around. Such a lovely little oasis.

We were there on the low season. Quiet place, some bars to get fresh fruit juices or cocktails. But I even preferred the way before the beach, to reach it, in the middle of the jungle with the possibility to see monkeys. We saw two.

Place is quite remote. It'stake some time to get there. There is bit of climbing to get there and back. At the time of visit there was no restaurant on the beach. Just a couple guys selling coconuts, water and beer. Have a feeling place become popular and bit overcrowded at middle of the day.
Delicious food and coctails, very reasonably priced. Nice and friendly staff. Lovely unspoilt beach, soft white sands and very clean, sea was clean and clear. Highly recommend
Lonely Planet says it's a hidden pearl that everyone knows about, and it's a pearle indeed. When we were there, it was still quiet, and that's what it should stay.

Jungle beach is small and a small trek away from Unawatuna but worth the effort. We walked along the path from Unawatuna visited the Japonese Peace Pagoda and then on to Jungle beach. Jungle Beach is smaller than expected but picturesque and great for snorkelling or swimming or just a nice place to relax. The waves are small and a walk into the sea is nice and easy. Take a picnic and your camera and you won't regret it.

great place to experience a touch of wilderness with close proximity to the ancient city of Galle A 15 minute climb down a Forrest pathway will lead you to a beach secluded from the the hustle and bustle Ideal location to relax caution: there is no lifeguards so you are on your own..
Amazing clean beach with comfy sand! Jungle beach is in a bay so there are no huge waves. At the beach you can find sunbeds and bar with cold drinks and snacks.
Disapointed! Dirty beach and water.  I just say one thing. Dont bother go here. Go to Unawatuna beach instead.

This place is unreal. It is a postcard beach. Hidden through a steep jungle entrance you can enjoy a day basking in the sun and snorkelling in the sea. (ask the tuk tuk driver to take you to the entrance by the Japanese peace pagoda, its more the locals beach so less people) simply delightful. 1 person selling drinks. Take food with you or up the hill is a few places to eat.
Paradise beach! No constructio only trees. In the middle of the jungle. Really quiet sea and calm beach.

If you are visiting Galle, this is a beach that you should not miss. This beach is usually not crowded as the Unawatuna beach. Ideal location to have a swim in the sea. There aren't any beach restaurants available at the site but parking facilities, few shops and places to have a shower are available near-by. Please make sure you don't litter in the beach. This is a clean beach comparing to some other beaches around. You also can have a visit to the temple nearby which offers some great views of the Galle city and the sea.
Beautiful place to be at, theres no much to do around or in there but to enjoy the precious view of the jungle.
Beautiful place still but shame it has been found. Was pleased to see that I was bein cleaned of rubbish when we were there as this is obviously a problem.
It is a very small beach accessible from the peace pagoda. A walk of 10 minutes downhill. Nice to see if u go to pace pagoda

We walked to Jungle Beach  from Unawatuna based on the Trip Advisor reviews. It's a very sweaty arduous walk on a very poor trail.  When we finally got there it was a complete anti climax. The beach is small, unremarkable and overcrowded. It's a good hour of my life I will never get back! Skip it - you're not missing a thing.

Really nice beach but weird local guy was following me some of the way and randomly asked me is I wanted to have sex with him. I got out of the situation well but it got me scared since I was on my own.

Nice beach. Would be rather happy if the water was more cleaner. Once we stepped in to water, there were lots of polythene bags and dirty stuff which fouled our legs. Environment was so beautiful. Be careful if you are going with kids as the tides are little stronger.

Central part of the beach is okay and has a nice bar, however rest of the beach is covered in rubbish and we met a girl who got her stuff stolen. Nice jungle hike up to the beach. If interested visit but be carefull and keep your expectations low.

Ifv you want a day away from the bustle of Unawatuna, this is the palce to escape to just around the bay from Una. A secluded beach that is easilly accessible by boat and to have a BBQ fish lunch and fantastic day out.

Not a bad place to go with your mates and have a cold beer.only downfall is that this place is very dirty .polythene bags and plastic bottles were all over the place .if someone could clean this up that'd be great.and cmon guys please don't litter this place.its a gem of a place !!

This place is a bit off the main road, you can google it for the directions so it was easy to find. You have to walk down the hill to get to the beach and first the path was a bit rocky but half way there was some steps to go down. We went there around 5 in the evening and most of the people were going back at that time so the beach was fairly empty with just few locals and foreigners. Which was great because we were able to enjoy the beach leisurely. But I heard from a local that the previous week it was packed up and there was a huge traffic. We had the chance to see the beautiful sunset which was amazing. Overall it was a great experience but wish there was some changing rooms so that we could easily change clothes.

Wouldn't recommend this beach, the water feels "dirty", the beach is crowded with locals which is fine, except that the local women can only get into the ocean with clothes on, so the few tourists in bikini are starred at. It's nice with all the green surroundings, but not the beach I prefer

If they cleaned it up it would be a definite 5 Would have been a beautiful walk through jungle if it wasn't for the small piles of rubbish along route and the bits of rubbish on sand and rocks. It could be amazing

Jungle beach is about 1,5 km from Unawatuna beach, you can walk or take a tub-tuk. It is definitely the best beach for swimming, quiet and lovely water. There are two Jungle beaches, the first is  small, but also the nicest. The other is bigger. Very crowded on week ends and holidays.Bring your own food and water, there are pedlars who sell seafood, but don't count on it.
Could be a beautiful beach with a nice view to Galle, but it's full of rubish. We needed to walk in the jungle, which was interesting but not worth it if you are planning to swim. Disappointing 😕

This beach is beautiful, but takes a little bit of getting to for those who are not the most mobile. For those able to scramble along a jungle path, they are rewarded with a wonderful, peaceful beach, with gentle waves and great snorkeling potential.
It isn't worth to go there, especially for beaching or swimming. Very small and DIRTY. I won't never go there anymore

A Beach , Surrounded by jungle. I have visited few times. and some times back there was no any shops or seller mens on the beach.That was very beautiful. Need to careful while bathing on sea. Because it is SEA. Still the beach is in clear condition and we need to be careful not to litter.
I belive that idea of jungle beach was good but nobody took care about this place. It's very small area which looks like garbage dump. Absolutely not worth to see.
The long trek to this beach is not worth one's while! It is a busy beach frequented by the locals with a few tourists. People are bathing fully clothed.Security is an issue.

Beautiful nice clear water. Coke 300 rupees but hey it was cold and glad I didnt have to lug stuff up and down that hill.  500 rupees for a tuk tuk there and same approx back. Quite a steep hill from where you are dropped at the top of the hill - and of course if you go down you need to go back up!  Cocktails available and food (but I didn't try. Loungers available I think covered by purchasing drinks. Take sunscreen and plan to spend a few hours.
Great beach. Beautiful view. Clean and secluded. Bit tricky to get to and from. Would visit again. Can spend the day there relaxing easily.

Love the beach, there is shadow from the plants. Many monkeys hanging around ! You can reach by foot 20 min away from Unawatuna cross the jungle. Many tourists go on the small path. Amazing experience !
Set on the small coast at the beginning of Unawatuna, this spot is a great swimming zone with good fun people. We also took a catamaran Cruise that set sail from here. Very pleasant. Recommended!
Nice, but you need to be able to get there ... steps or a bit of climbing ... but the reward is exceptional.
Really good beach. It was a little dirty once because there was alot of plastic trash in the water. But the next time I visti it was clear water with nice fish to see. Nice to see!
Friends recommended this place but it was nothing special at all . The beach is quite small and there is lots of dirt swept under the bushes. We went once only .
Really small but beautiful beach. Frequented by locals and tourists alike. Calm, clean water. To access it, you'll have to go up a hill (via tuk-tuk/car), and then walk down an easy 'jungle' path.
Dont bother. Small, crowded, polluted water with trash floating around. Wouldnt even consider swimming here.
The most overrated spot on the Beach. After walking a long Walk from Unawatuna We came to this little Beach. To Many people.
Go early! The walk there is lovely and well sign posted. The beach is small, but beautiful. There are shady spots too. The water is stunning and quiet, no waves.

This is an especially good destination if you're staying on Unawatuna Beach. The jungle walk to Jungle Beach is charming and rewarded with snack bars on the way. Much gentler beach than the big surf at Unawatuna
We went to snorkel however the water wasn't clear enough to see anything. The beach is cute but small in the little cove we went to but it didn't offer much.

I advise walking down to get the full experience (it only takes 15 minutes) but this is a lovely little hideaway with gentler currents than elsewhere in the bay. A bit of rubbish floating round but the water itself and beach were clean.

The beach has the potential to be beautiful, unfortunately there is quite a lot of litter that gathers near the trees so you're unable to sit in the shade that they provide. The walk down wasn't for the weak but we stopped and admired the monkeys playing in the trees and posing for the cameras. It is a nice beach but if you're planning on making quite a journey to it I wouldn't suggest you do. However if you're close I don't see why you shouldn't go for a few hours.

I had the really nice walk from Unawatuna to get here. The beach is nice but small and get crowded quickly. I went here on a thursday morning... Arriving there another 5 was already on the beach and 30 min later a Schoolclass and a couple doing there weddingphotography with a crew of 10 made the beach less serene. Actually Unawatuna beach is less crowded 😂 I might have been just unlucky - the place is nice so well worth a visit.

At jungle beach you really have to earn your swim with a hike up the hill and down the forest path to the beach. And what a swim it is! I love that the water is so calm that it's actually possible to swim quite far out to sea, which is rare in this area. Nice, shady trees, sun loungers some picturesque boats dotted around as well as lunch facilities make this a truly great beach. It's perfect to round off the beach time with another short hike to Unawatuna.

Lovely beach to wander down to if you have time. It's small and we went at sun set and it was fairly quiet and a lovely spot to see the sunset from. We walked from Unawatuna beach, up to the peace pagoda, and then down to Jungle Beach. Was a fun little afternoon adventure.

Spent here half a day and whilst it is a nice beach in terms of landscape and an area with clear water / rocks / corals to snorkel, the shore is truly dirty and full of rubbish (bottles, food packages etc.) There is not much shade either and to get there, you have to go up a hill - not too bad, just bear in mind the heat!

The beach is no longer a secret and while it is pleasant enough the water was a bit murky and the coral has been trashed. We walked there from Unawatuna in half an hour but tuk-tuk is an alternative. We only stayed a couple of hours since it was a Saturday and was beginning to get crowded. There are better beaches in Sri Lanka such as Mirissa.

We loved this beach. You take a tuktuk from town. Walk down to the beach about 10 minutes and you have a gorgeous secluded beach with a little restaurant. Great for swimming, lounge chairs and have a restaurant open until 5pm. Great view across the bay to Galle fort. We have already returned again. Go visit it's worth it
Jungle Beach is small, but beautiful. There are beach loungers to use. There are restaurants that serve food and drinks. This beach is a great place to spend an afternoon!
this is a nice beach in down south sri lanka good for relaxing and reading we stay over 3 days in this beach swim and diving prefect activities @ here
It's about a big beach erea divided between sands and rocks with calm ( low waves) waters surrounded by jungle trees and a nearby Buddhist temple.

Jungle Beach is not very far from Unawatuna (just a bus ride away if you're taking local transport - you can also walk if you're up for it). It's very secluded. You have to climb down a hill to access it. In 2016 there was only restaurant serving food at the beach and was overpriced. The food was just average. It's a virgin beach. Go there to get away from the crowds.

Had a great time there. Waves aren't rough so had no problems to swim. Safe beach as well. The outside areas have been corrupted by tourists with rubbish hence its not clean. But a good place to go for a swim and relax.
This can be termed as one of the virgin beaches of Ceylon and a beautiful location and a real gift of nature
great place to swim and hang out with the locals.   you do have to climb down a hill to get access to the beach

My experience here was awful.  Lot's of garbage. You could fill 20 large rubbish bags easily. Theft. Met a tourist who caught Sri Lankans trying to steal $80 USD out of his wallet.  They'll try and be your friend and distract you for n hour or so while their other friends find an oppurtunity to go through your belongings.  You've been warned.
Nice for picnic and snorkeling. Only 30 minutes walk from the lovely Simon's House you go through shadow little lane to this wonderful little beach!

Supposedly 'hidden' beach, at the end of a v heavily wooded, rocky downhill trail. Heavy with tourists when we went. Good bar serving drinks and food. Be careful with belongings though: a couple had their money (not the wallets, just the cash) stolen while in the water.

Visited 1st time this beach 2 years ago in March 2015 and that was a very good experience with positive feelings. So today we were there with the expectations that if it will not be better at least it will be the same beach. But ... its a disaster. Its only my opinion but I'm writing now about my feelings. The water was dirty with some stinky smell. The beach itself its smaller than it used to be. 3 times smaller area. The place is dirty. The little cafe that was there its gone. Some strange people walking around. The beds on which we used to take a nap ;) are gone. The only good thing that is left its the view onthe jungles from water.

We walked to the beach, scrambling over rocks, having been told it was worth visiting. The sand is good, but it is a narrow strip of land, with hard beds and a poor cafe. Better to stay in Unawatuna beach where the facilities are better.

It's a nice beach but there's a fairly off the beaten track journey to get too the beech. Plenty of sandbag steps to negotiate. Once down on the beach it's fairly small and surrounded by nice scenery, the beech is used for partying in the evenings so it can be a little noisy / busy especially at the weekend. Very nice if you get your timings right !!

We took a TukTuk from Galle to this hideaway which is located between Galle and Unawatuna. We paid around 400 Rupies from the fort. Don't expect a total secret place, but a nice beach with a bar, sunbeds and less people than in Unawatuna. Pro: + close to Galle (you can see the lighthouse from there) + small beach without mass tourism, but convenience like sunbeds and one restaurant with food and drinks + ever Wednesday a beach party during night, probably just in high season + almost no waves Con: - sunbeds without mattress - some parts of the beach have stones in the water - some locals don't keep it 100% clean Please mark helpful if you like the review. Thanks.
Very beautiful place, a lot of monkeys on the way to the beach. The water is very clean, there are not so many people there.

Do you remember <The Blue lagoon >( Brooke Shields 1980) well this was our secrect Blue lagoon in late 70s and early 80s. so beautiful and unspoilt. it still has that charm to some extent but not lonely and deserted any more. but compared to a packed Unawatuna beach just other side of the Rumassla mountain which seperates  strip, this is a breather
Nothing special about this beach. It's ouy of the main road, so not that crowded. However its quite small and not that nice. Hikkaduwa us better.

Nice little beach with a bar but beware, while we were there a couple left their bag unattended under the trees while they went for a swim. A man then used a stick to drag their bag from their towel and stole a camera. I caught him doing this and and he ran away up the hill never to be seen again. So a nice as it is here and in Sri Lanka as a whole, please ensure you look after you belongings wherever you are. Also please don't let this scare you off it's a lovely little beach:)

There are two sections to jungle beach and we went hoping to see some interesting things snorkelling, but to no avail. The water was murky and there is not much live coral left in the area. The beach is very very small and busy even on weekdays. The water is calm and great for swimming and it is clean. It is a bit of a walk down, but do-able in flip flops and even with kids. There was a vendor selling coconuts and small drinks and there was a restaurant at the top of the beach.

Not the best place. Lots of noisy drunk locals on the beach so do take care of your items.  The walk to the beach is pretty difficult so I wouldn't recommend walking there if you're less able than others -

There are two beaches linked by a rough track. One has (overpriced) food and drink. The smaller one is great for snorkelling, but gets crowded, especially at weekends. It,s a long hot treck from Unawatana.

Whilst visiting unawatuna being driven by srilankanishatours and not wanting to stay too long on the beach there as a solo female traveller, my driver Nisha suggested this beach.  We hired a moped (many options to do so in Unawatuna for 1000 rupees (approx £7) and Nisha took me to Jungle beach.  So happy that I was able to spend the afternoon here, mainly local people there and although only a small bay it was perfect for some relaxation time away from the crowds.  Most definitely worth a visit if your in unawatuna.

A small beach with view to Galle Fort with a small restaurant/cafe. The beach is very nice. Beware of many and steep steps to get down from the road. Best to go there in morning. Only a few wooden sunbeds avaliable

We read about this hidden small beach, you can get there by tuk tuk easily. Although the beach was cosy and nicely located, we had some trouble with a group of men. These men took photographs of me and my friend in bikinis without asking, and when we told them to stop, they started filming us. Made us really uncomfortable and we left. Besides that experience, there was nothing wrong with the beach.

Large expanse of beach and calm bay for getting into the water, after uphill drive on narrow roads; very crowded on weekends.  The beaches just below the Galle fort walls looked much more interesting and easier to access.

Quaint beach surrounded by the jungle. Acces is difficult. Recommend you wear sturdy closed toe shoes for the walk down the track to the beach. No need to take supplies with you...there was a mobile drinks station with a local selling cold drinks and snacks at very inexpensive prices. There was the option of taking a boat trip from jungle beach to the bay and other areas but we didnt take this option up. It makes for a goo afternoon. Recommen ded!!!
We went there by tuktuk. Really nice no garbage and the bar offers beds If you Order a Drink. Afterwards we walked to unawatuna beach. On the way we saw a lot of garbage lying around.

Walked to the beach and got there about 10am. It is a tiny crescent of sand with a bit of vegetation behind it. Even at 10am, the beach was full and there were boats everywhere. There is nothing remotely special about this place.

This is the place to go to if you want to avoid tour groups and just get away at a small, peaceful resort on an isolated beach. In fact, the whole hotel is so peaceful that my wife and I found ourselves unknowingly speaking in whispers all the time. The hotel was built to blend right in with nature so only 2 trees were cut down during its construction. The private cabins are huge, amazing and right on the beach (although the beach itself is obscured by trees). The staff is extremely helpful and amazing although it would be nice if hotel had a naturalist on staff like many other eco hotels in country. As good as the hotel is, the beach is the best part. The hotel is small and is the only one on the stretch of beach so it is extremely quiet and peaceful. If you're looking to get away and recharge this is definitely the place for you. Heads up though: the hotel is very isolated so you should plan on eating all your meals there. That being said, the inclusive "board" options are extremely expensive and not worth it. I strongly recommend buying the bed and breakfast option and then paying for lunch and dinner a la cart.

Walked to Jungle Beach via the jungle walk that was enjoyable. Two separate beaches we went to the second one and headed for the quieter area. We split our swimming but still were unfortunate to encounter thieving western swine who emptied our wallet. Heard that Jungle Beach has a bit of a reputation. So if you visit take very good care of your money!

We were looking for a different kind of beach after a hot day in Unawatuna beach under direct sunshine and right next to dozen beach restaurants. Reviews and snorkeling options lured us to choose Jungle beach. Our hotel reception told us that the beach could be reached by walking from Unawatuna, but it was too hot day for a random walk. We hailed a tuk tuk and our driver chose a route that diverts from Matara road (main road). Route was surprisingly steep, so I´d recommend a tuk tuk anyway - or you'll swelter in the sun. We found out that the beach splits into two sections. We went first to section that is closer to Japanese pagoda and then also tried the other one. There is a small path connecting both beaches, but it was badly maintained. My companion swam from first beach to another :) Notes: - "First" beach near the pagoda is easier to reach - less steep walk. Ask your tuk tuk driver to drop you off in front of the pagoda. - This beach is small but more relaxed than the other one. There was a guy selling sodas, no other services. - Snorkeling is possible but there is nothing to see. Some dead coral and few fishes. Local glass boats make tours here - I don't know why... Anyway first beach could be a bit better for snorkeling if one insists to see whats below the surface. - Second beach has more tourists but also more space. - Entering and leaving requires a walk trough steep stairs. - Second beach has also a small restaurant. Medium priced simple dishes. Beer available (but if I've understand right, last can was sold out even it was still early afternoon). - Second beach had monkeys in nearby trees which amused kids. Anyway we enjoyed both beaches, but I´d prefer the first one.

Jungle Beach is next door to the Japanese Peace Pagoda.  It is a bit of a climb down to the beach but once there you have safe current free water, clean sand and a few kiosks selling basic food and drinks.  A nice place to chill out and safe for young children.

We walked there from the Unawatuna railway station (Around 2km) to take a clear look around. If not we can easily hire a taxi to reach the starting of the road through the jungle. While walking we met some sort of a snake on the road. So it's better to keep eyes open while walking there. If you are planning for a night time visit don't forget a torch. After an interesting walk through the jungle we reached the beach. As we went there on a week day the beach is crowded with foreigners & there were couple of local visitors too. The beach is very safe to take a swim even for a kid. No waves at all. And also the beach is covered with the jungle and very scenic. I can say this is the best beach I've ever visited. But some visitors left wastes like plastic bottles, polythene etc and it make some untidiness. Please don't do that if you are planning to go there. Water is very clear & the bottom is clearly visible up to a certain level. Boat rides are also available & the bottom of the boat is made by glass. When we were heading towards Galle town while returning we saw the beach & couldn't figure out a way to reach there. I guess this is only one hidden beauty in Sri Lanka & there could be more places like this. If you are visiting southern area of Sri Lanka don't forget  to spend a day on this calm scenic beach.

We took a tuktuk to the Peace Pagoda, and then walked to the jungle beach; on the way we saw a female monkey with a baby clinging to it! The beach is gorgeous; good for snorkelling, and with amazing views. We also enjoyed the entertainment of groups of young men with drums having a singsong!

Bit of a steep trek to get to it but very different. Some tuk tuk will take you further than others but always some steep climbs if going via Pagoda. Visit Peace Pagoda on the way with Tsunami monument.

We walked to this beach from the centre of Unawatuna. It's a longish walk given the heat and some of it involves climbing over large rocks. When you finally arrive at the beach there are no facilities at all. Some snorkelling opportunities and quite often a party in full swing. You can get a tuk tuk from the centre of Unawatuna to drop you above the beach but you still need to climb down to it. Food is available and drinks at the tuk tuk drop off point.
Just a perfect place. Nice walk to the beach throughout the jungle and than a small walk along the beach.

We were told how 'beautiful' this beach was and this reassured us that there was something in Unawatuna worth exploring, seeing as Unawatuna beach is also quite poor. We were disappointed. It's overcrowded (perhaps all the people trying to find somewhere a little more private than Unawatuna?) it's littered, it's local (nothing wrong with this but it means everyone comes there for their weekend hang outs) and there are few places to put your towels. Not worth the trip.
Jungle beach is very scenic, but the long 20' walk to get there diminishes its allure. There are restaurants at the second beach.
Maybe we waited something else but this was tiny, crowded and not even very clean beach. Not worth to go.

Had expected more fish and clear water. Unfortunately the corals are still lacking due to the tsunami although they have started to grow, but the place is very close to Unawatuna beach and can be reached in 15 minutes by boat.

Unfortunately there was no party going on, on Wednesday . We got there at 6 and the kitchen was closed. Got back around 9pm and there was no party going on. So people go there its beautiful and really good for a swim. Even at night..

Few kilometers away from the main city (Galle).You can even take a tuk (Threewheel) from Galle to this awsome place.One of the best place for snorkeling in Srilanka.Have some great restaurants nearby as well.Trust me Do not miss this place if you ever come to Srilanka. :)

Jungle Beach is a short Tuk Tuk ride from Unawatuna, and I suspect Galle. It is a small beach with no real facilities. It can get overcrowded but when it isn't it is very beautiful and tranquil. It is not easily accessible. It is at the bottom of a single track stony road. There are steps down from the parking area, please be cautious when you take this path. It's a good place to snorkel.
Needs a little bit of cleaning up. But it is quite nice and probably the nicest beach in the area. Has a couple of restaurant with food that is overpriced

Don't book a boat or a taxi form Unawatuna, the best experience is to go through "the jungle". It takes you about 30 minutes to walk from andour kids  (age 6 and 9) managed without any trouble. In the beach the beach chairs are for free, if you order something from the restaurant. Food was ok, and not too pricey. One meal with rice  was extremely salty... The beach is safe for the kids to swimm (waves weren't too high) and you can see quite many fishes, we even saw turtles and an octopus. There is fine sand to play with and enough shadowy places. BE aware that the monekys may steal your cookies! ;)

- You need to take the small road down the Japanese Peace Pagoda and walk down the hill for 5-8 mins - Super clean and neat beach - Damn good if you can make it before 8 am - ideal place for snorkelling - Local have littered the place with post-party thrash

Visited once on holiday. kids loved the sea and waves. short walk through jungle with monkeys in trees. A handful of cafes on beach and a rope swing for the kids. Out of the way but not a quiet beach. overlooked by Galle on opposite side which was less beautiful than ocean view however still beautiful

Jungle beach located very close to (2.5 km from ) Galle bus-stand. You can take a Tuk Tuk from there to JB area for maximum 200 rupees. JB is geographically isolated bay with high vegetation cover. You can park your vehicle closer to the access point and from there to beach side you have to walk for maximum 500 m. Parking area to beach there is a gradual slope with dense vegetation cover. Open area of JB has nearly 700m sandy and shallow beach line. Morning low tides will be favorable for swimming. At the evening JB is a good place to enjoy sunset. Foods and cocktails are available in beach site but if you can take foods and drinks it will be much cheaper. Also visitors can have boat rides for affordable prices. JB can be bit crowded on weekends & holidays and locals are also attracted to this location. Please be responsible and try not to pollute that beautiful location.

The jungle beach was named as the best beach in the world in 2015 by FOX news. The beach is so amazing.Shallow waters. Crystal like blue waters. There you can explore coral reefs, the Bonavista coral reef. The beach is so nice. You have to go through a thick forest to reach this beach.Nice experience.

the walk to the beach is down a steep hill so make sure you have good foot wear, we went on a Saturday I would not go here again on the weekend as it gets very noise with the local's, maybe  go on a week day

We travelled down south from Hikkaduwa on the moped looking to explore new beaches. This is a good 40 minute moped ride away but totally worth it. It is difficult to find at first up long windy roads and in the mountains for a long walk down through the jungle and trees. We were greeted by many monkeys and the scene and views along the walk down are breath taking. When you get to the beach it is not overcrowded, a good selection of drinks and people chilling out. A great place to go away from the rough seas in Hikka.

There are two ways to reach this beach one is by hiking which takes around 20-30 mins and other way is by tuk tuk. I did both hiking to this place is not so worthy. Dont expect this beach to be secluded serene paradise beach but its good for swimming, swimming here is better than any beaches of this island country. Every wednesday they have beach party we too went there arrived at 10.30 pm that time there were half a dozen people and left ar 11.30 that time too only 7-8 person were there. I found this party not entertaining as bad choice of music, people smoking weed. Also night time its not safe to go this area, on my way going back up to road i almost landed my feet on snake, luckily it was a small and i was few inches away. Better to carry good flashlights while going there and be alert.

Being Greek I'm spoiled with beautiful beaches. Jungle beach is nice cause it's not wavy as many of the close by beaches. However don't expect a paradise. It's quite dirty and the water visibility is also not good. There's a small restaurant there so you don't need to bring your water and food. It's kind of basic but what isn't in Sri Lanka. I would recommend it if you want to swim without currents and waves.

You have to be fit to get through "the jungle". The beach itself was OK but there were big piles of trash. Not very comfortable. Swimming was nice and there were lots of monkies hanging around in the trees. If you get thirsty there is a small bar (no coffee) I wouldn't go there again. The japanese peace pagode made the trip worth.
Best place with a greate view in unawatuana its a cozy good beach the acess road is different from the yademulla road
Actualli clean and secure beach I ever visited. But the approaching road is little bid harder. Totally nice place...

I walked 8/10 mins to jungle beach from Jungle hostel. The beach itself is small and quite secluded. On this particular day, it was cloudy and had rained so the views weren't great but the beach itself is nice. However there is a fair amount of litter on the beach; bottles, wrappers and plastic bags which are visible on the shore. Still, I would give this place a go as it's a lot quieter than Hikkaduwa and Unawatuna beaches.

We walked here, unexpectedly longer than we thought. We spent around 20 mins here after deciding it was just too busy, not the prettiest and was stifling hot due to the lack of breeze with it being enclosed. Unawatuna main beach was much better in our opinion.
The beach has rubbish, cleaner and less crowded compared to unawatuna. The sea is calmer and good for swimming.

Being a Sri Lankan it's rare that you stumble across a beach as beautiful as Jungle Beach  ..looks like something straight out of a magazine I would suggest you take down some snacks and drinks because it's hard to get any good food and drinks down there because the goverment took down most of the eateries and restaurants at the beach ...they were over priced anyways . But remember to take back the litter with you because at the moment it is a spiritually beautiful calming spot.oh and avoid weekends.the locals come in droves to the place
A short tuk tuk ride over the from Unatwatuna, secluded and relatively deserted place for a secret swim and to watch the sunset.

the lonely planet guide mention this beach and since we were in Unawatuna, we decided to go. It is a good walk (better by bike, although you need to walk part of the way) from Unawatunna. Once you are in the beach, it doesn't have a lot of space, and there are plenty of shadows (a lot of coconut palms and trees, that's way they call it jungle!!). It was plenty of locals, and just a few tourist. it was Sunday and the locals were mainly drunk. There was an issue with locals and tourist and we decided to leave. In general terms, the place is nice, but nothing special.

We went there in the morning. The walk was nice and we did some nice snorkeling right at the beach. Our toddler also loved liked the beach as the waves were not strong. There is also the bigger 'white jungle beach' further north but this was more crowded and also had a bar. So I recommend to stay at the smaller jungle beach.
Very nice beach to visit, but mostly if you go by boat and can visit the coral reef and snorkel or dive there.
Supposedly a secluded beach, this has in fact turned into a hipster version of Una beach. Longish walk for nothing.

This is a lovely beach with a little restaurant - very organic with jungle behind. I went snorkeling, and there were a few lovely fish, but coral all dead which was a bit depressing. Nonetheless - worth a busy for a lunch a relaxation.

Even though staying just a couple minutes from Unawatuna Beach, we ended up at Jungle Beach every afternoon. The kids loved the small hike from the tuk tuk drop off spot. The beach itself is small and definitely not private, but with plenty of shade provided by the palm trees swaying gently over you. The water is way more child friendly than at Unawatuna Beach. There are hardly any waves but you need to be careful because the water depth increases quickly. Great place to go for a swim.
Highly reccommended beach! Lots of locals around and safe, clear water! Very close to the shops, great to stay for a few hours and relax with a book to get away from the hotel.

The first time we visited this beach it was late afternoon and we couldn't find a spot to sit let alone relax. Luckily we tried again just after sun rise a few days and had the whole beach to ourselves, which was amazing! The water is great for young kids and is ideal for snorkelling. Plenty of fish, crabs, lizards and monkeys to be seen.

Its quite a nice beach , but just a beach I went very early morning so there were only 3 or 4 other people there and its nice and peaceful. TBH I enjoyed the walk down the path to the beach a lot more, observing the local wildlife, birds lizards snakes etc. The place can get very busy later in the the day, as its one of those places tourists like to tick off their lists, so I wouldn't pay a visit to Unawatuna especially for this beach , but its may well be worth a stroll there to pass the time, like I said its just a beach, and there are far far better one in Sri Lanka

How did you end up here?  You saw pretty pictures on the internet and booked it didn't you?  I already did my rant on Unawatuna beach.. this place is the same.  It's a hike to get here and you think you are going to find your secluded paradise spot from the movie "the beach" but instead you find an average beach full of others who thought the same thing.  The snorkeling was scary.. so much sand and silt floating around rendering you blind and then BAM, a huge rock is in front of you a and then another.. then you are boxed in trying to find a way out.. not many fish to see.  Perhaps I am wrong and it's simply a matter of timing.. maybe the water is clear in the morning or during a different season.. We were here in February. We were here for an hour.. moved on pretty quick, no time to waste on sub par activities.

Jungle beach was about 40 mins walk from our hotel, Thambapanni Resort, but worth walking to. The walk itself was really attractive, through native jungle. We could have got a TukTuk but preferred the peace of the walk. Because it is tucked out of the way there are very few people on it. From here there is snorkelling and trips on a glass bottom boat. We did neither as found it a bit late and had organised other excursions.

This was the sister hotel to Cantaloupe Aqua hotel. We visited for the day and it's a stunning hotel is a great location, having the jungle wildlife and the sea all in one. The room were stunning. The restaurant offered a wide range of food. The pool surrounding had a chose of double and single sun bed. The staff were great and very friendly.if you want a place to unwind this is the place to be,

We visited on a Sunday so there were a lot of teenagers there getting drunk and dancing around. Not a terrible thing to witness but it did hamper our experience somewhat. The walk to the beach is pretty difficult so I wouldn't recommend walking there if you're less able than others - take a tuk tuk to the top and then try to walk down, it's still pretty difficult though. The beach itself is beautiful but there were a few spots where rubbish had gathered that was pretty disgusting. There were also stray dogs that looked as if they were dying! One was breathing so fast and I could see his ribs I thought he was going to keel over. I gave him some food and water (not sure if you're supposed to though!!) which he seemed pretty happy about but as an animal love, it wasn't the most relaxing experience I've ever had! Probably would go back but it'd have to be a week day when it's less crowded and rowdy.
Ok but from oz so no comparison to our beaches Steep walk to beach. Not good if you are not into walking. We were

Gorgeous beach, a bit too many ppl for my Liking and quite a trek up and down the hill Water is beautiful!!! Like paradise!!! Downside is there are a fair few rocks disguised under the water so watch for banging / scraping feet and toes!

The beach is nice one. If you would like to snorkel it is a great one: it worth to swim along the rocky part of the beach as the water is quite calm and the visibility is cool. The road from Unawatuna is picturesque with some possibilities for drinking king coconut. You should be aware that the signs direct you to the parking place and only to the southern part of the beach which is a bit separated from the other parts. That was the positive part. Unfortunately we had a quite bad experience with local people here (I should say the only bad experience in Sri Lanka, but quite a significant one). Second time when we were at the Jungle Beach it was a Hindu religious holyday. Well we thought that it cannot influence our stay or safety. But yes. The beach was crowded with drunken locals who at first just kindly inquired about our home country, after then still kindly asked for cigarettes (several times), after then not so kindly insisted on drinking arrack together with them (we kindly resisted) and after then really not so kindly they surrounded us and they wanted us to go with them to Colombo (for who knows what reason) with a completely drunken driver. As we were surrounded escaping from this situation was quite challenging. The solution was a not drunken local guy (thanx to him) who asked the guys not to bother us, so for the second try we could leave. So to sum up the Jungle Beach was not our favourite one.

A lovely beach. Less waves and better for small children than Unawatuna beach. Stay away from the sun bed if you don't want too eat/drink there. The staff is aggressive selling from the menu, and the price is higher than in Unawatuna. The best way going there is by tuk tuk and walking down the step path. If you have a map you can walk home through the forest.  Both beaches is good for bathing, sunbathing and ok for snorkelling.

We took the 25 minute walk following signs from Thambapanni Retreat to what we thought was Jungle Beach, certainly walked via a Jungle to get to it. Small beach, one drink seller, glass bottomed boat floating off shore, snorkel and masks for hire. Lovely water so I swam about 150 metres around the corner to what I guess is the main Jungle Beach. There is a way to walk from one to the other, across some rocks and path. Main Jungle Beach with small bar, eating facility, sun beds for hire has more room, a view of The Galle Fort and the same great water to swim in ... with my swimming goggles I was able to see some colourful marine life so snorkelling would be safe and rewarding. Not the easiest access from the road, one poor lass on crutches literally had to shuffle on her bottom down some of the route ... but beach is reward for your efforts- and we got to see two local eagles soaring about to boot! Helps if it is sunny - we are in Sri Lanka at a time when it is experiencing much, well needed rain!!

The beach is hidden in the outskirts of Unawatuna. We reached there first through the jungles then by tuk tuk. It's very beautiful there. There is a bar with tables to sit and eat there. We had a tasty lunch just on the beach. It was funny when a group of school children with a teacher appeared on the beach. I still wonder what was that interesting with that place that a teacher took the children to this place for an excursion)) Recommend to visit at least once.

Lovely spot. Just let down by poor service at the one and only beach bar (two days running it took them 40 minutes to serve a pot of tea!) If you enter from the track leading down from the Japanese Peace Pagoda, beware that the first stretch of beach is only half of it, You need to turn right and go along to end of beach, clamber over rocks to a pathway and walk around to main beach where there are loungers and a bar
It may have been nice, clean and secluded place once but now is dirty and overcrowded. Too many loud people ruined the charm and beauty - Jungle beach is now the place to be avoided.
this very small beach, accessible by foot is cute but.. no privacy since you are standing on each other's feet

Jungle beach is a small secluded beach just on the outskirts of Unawatuna. The walk from the main Unawatuna Beach area is approximately 1.5km however it may take 30 minutes due to the steep roads. Several reviews have commented on the snorkelling and beach popularity which is true. Get there early we left at 1030am and the beach was starting to pack up with Russian Tourists and local playing music and drinking the local rum. If you are going to snorkel low tide is generally 0830am and high tide midday. Having arrived and 930am and reading reviews we snorkeled the rocks on the left hand side of the beach. The visibility was a little difficult as it had been raining the previous night thus saying the fish that we saw was similar to Nha Trang in Vietnam (which we paid to see) indicating the reef is starting to recover. Snorkelling satisfied my personal needs saw a tone of various fish including a  Lionfish and accomplished my goal of seeing a Blue Spotted Stingray venturing on the seabed which really made my day. Jungle Beach is a must if you are in Unawatuna however don't judge the reef on arrival swim out to the outer edge of the left cliff and you will see plenty underwater creatures.
Nice beach. A bit difficult to get down to and go walk back from. Lovely view, not too crowded. Give it a try
One of the unique places in the world. You have to go through the mountain and will find a best beach Not much crowded in weekdays and weekend get visitors

I was so excited to go to this beach after reading the reviews and to be fair, the view/beach is beautiful but it's like that in all of Sri Lanka. Would I specifically recommend this place? Not really. It was very small and crowded and there weren't any services offered. Not even a small kiosk selling water for dehydrated sun bathers. Basically, while the beach is beautiful, don't go out of your way to see it. There are plenty of gorgeous and more spacious beaches in Sri Lanka.

We walked from our guesthouse (Three Shades Villa, not on TA as quite new but best place we stayed in SL, see booking.com) over to Jungle Beach on a weekday morning and whilst there were people there it was by no means busy. Quite a cool decent through trees with the obligatory mobkeys chattering away. There are piles of rubbish at points at the back of the beach hidden in the trees but this didn't put us off at all as they are out of sight. Nice mix of tourists and a few locals enjoying the cooling sea. We walked around to the smaller connected beach by a rocky path round the small headland that was slightly more crowded but still pleasant. Guys selling coconuts and cans of lion lager for ok prices.
We visited the 2 beaches several times and enjoyed the crystal clear water very much. You can snorkel, relax and see monkeys from time to time. A must visit place when you are at the neighbourhood.
Nice little beach with own privacity. Good to swim. Good food in a restaurant on the beach. It was a little bit difficult to find the beach.Better sign to the beach would be necessary.

A nice short stroll to a small picturesque beach. Popular with locals and the water was beautiful. A little bit of rubbish around but not too bad. My visit was a little bit ruined by a group of young men who appeared to be drunk and were yelling at me to remind me that I'm fat. This caused us to leave, otherwise would have loved a swim at this beautiful spot.

I have heard of Jungle Beach which was described to me as a small, very quiet and peaceful area for relaxing and swimming. What I found was a small, dirty (partly even filthy) beach crowded by noisy Russian tourists which made approx. 95% of all the visitors (approx. 50 people) on that morning when I was present there. The later the morning the more (Russian) tourists showed up so it was time for me to leave. If you are looking for that tranquil and special beach, look further because this isn't it.

Unfortunately we visited on 'full moon' day when it appeared half of Sri Lanka had also descended on the beach that day. Would be a tranquil spot if we're not for the fact that it is part of the tourist thing to do whilst in Unawantuna. Firstly it was quite dirty with litter and secondly lots of Sri Lankans drinking spirits on the beach with large families spread over quite a tight space. The beach at Tangalle was twice as good this one. Not for me and a waste of four hours.

The beach is not very big, but it has a really nice, tropical vibe. You have to descend there about 200 meters from the main road through the jungle. The beach is all sandy, there are a few small rocks in the water you can step on (nothing dangerous, just not comfy). You can watch for stripes of sand where you can easily walk (or watch the locals playing in the water and follow them). There's a small café that offers some food and cold drinks (expensive, given the location and the lack of competition). Last but not least, you can have a good swim in this beach, waves during our stay were vers calm (beach is located in a small semi-open bay). There's no fee or anything. It was not crowded, but there were a few dozen turists and locals (weekday in January). You can easily visit nearby Japanese Peace Pagoda as well (it´s 15-min walk from the along the road, bring something to cover your shoulders).
There is a steep walk down to the beach from the road, but it is worth it for the fine sands and sunset views over Galle. Lovely luscious green background on the beach too.
Just a small beach but ok Worth going to as a break from Una We walked, takes at least 30mins to walk Nice japanese pergola nearby
Great place to relax and get away from the busy sun-chair beaches. Some days they have food/drinks for sale but do not count on it. There is hiwever a restaurant a few minutes away.

If you go to the Japanese peach pagode, Jungle beach is easy to find. Follow the path down to the beach. If you walk further over the rocks you will come to white beach. It's very nice with beach beds. You can buy foods ands drinks but it's expensive. 400 rp for a small can of beer.
We were told this beach was wonderful but were a bit disappointed... very dirty and crowded, don't think we will go back

After a 10 minute hike down along a mostly unmade path you come upon this wonderful treasure of a beach! Great for the children to play in the warm water, the waves were not as strong as other local beaches. Beautiful jungle setting, a beach bar/restaurant and nothing else other than the sound of birds and the lapping waves! Our favourite beach. If it wasn't for the hot 10/15 min trek back up to the road we would have returned every day!
Amazing beach hidden by undergrowth, lovely ocean to swim in a little rocky, great walk to white beach over the rocks close to jungle beach

A lovely little secluded bay with breathtaking views. We went in the morning and did not experience any of the overcrowding mentioned in other reviews. This is not a place to surf but is a great place to relax.

Having read mixed reviews about jungle beach, I was happy I made the visit myself to make up my own mind. I could see that numerous bags of rubbish had been collected so although the beach was clean when I went I can see how others would be correct in complaining about the state of it at other times. There is a beach party in Thursday nights and my guess is a lot of rubbish accumulates after that. Also walked through to white jungle beach in the next bay along. I imagine it could be good to snorkel here. A popular beach with the locals due to the water being a lot calmer.

The walk to beach from Unawatuna is nice, and the beach is pretty enough with it's forest background. However, it is way to much litter for it to be enjoyable. We also tried to snorkel but saw absolutely nothing.

Secluded and tucked away on the other side of Unawatuna beach lies Jungle Beach. Aside from a few sunburnt Germans, stray dogs, one umbrella shaded couple and a boat or two offering glass bottom tours, there isn't much to see here. I could see this place thumping during a beach party, though. If you're in the area and wanting to see the peace pagoda or natural park headland to the west, then stop by here for a bit. Someone in the water mentioned colourful fish floating around, but I'm sure there are better snorkelling places.

It's quite a nice beach and the walk to it is also kind of nice.  It's nice to swim in (except occasionally painful due to dead coral in the sand) and very pretty with the rocks and trees right next to the beach. I actually quite enjoyed it. Water is calm. There's two parts of the beach that are separated by rocks so you can walk over to the other side. There's a little Cafe where you can get food and drink and there's also sun beds. A downside is the beach is quite small and crowded and also there's quite a bit of rubbish. Actually I saw monkeys climbing down and into the bins and taking food /wrappers /bottles them throwing them on the ground afterwards. It was very cute but then again maybe that partially explains why there's rubbish scattered everywhere
Quite calm beach, not so crowded than other beaches nearby. You need to travel there by tuktuk or trek through some jungle. We did some snorkeling, but it was not that special.

There's a Jungle Beach and White Jungle Beach which are located side by side on a quiet bay behind the hill Did some snorkeling and saw some fishes but the water wasn't so clear that I would have expected!

This beach is very crowded ( I went on a weekend so that probably didn't help). Majority of people around are locals not tourists. Did not find it very comfortable to relax or swim. Very nice view though.
Recommended to visit the place with a group of friends. Lovely view. Get pretty crowded but still good enough for a visit.

Took a short tuk-tuk ride to get here and we took a boat back to Unawatuna beach. Many rocks on the beach underwater, so swimming was rather exiting. Also some garbage dumped behind the sand area (not nice). Not my favourite.
This place has great potential to be nice quite spot hidden from crowds of tourists, unfortunatelly in sri lankan style it was turned into dirty beach where u feel like on garbage dump.

Lovely spot...and definitely worth checking out! But wouldn't bank on hanging out there for the day as it can get quite cramped with people because it is so small...but if you're lucky enough to catch it on a quiet day...you could easily spend hours there.

The setting is spectacular, looking back from the water to the small beach in the 'jungle'. It is just across the bay from Galle Fort - about Rs 600 by tuk tuk. Water was clean and there were no waves to speak of. On the Sunday we visited, we were among the few white tourists standing out among the friendly locals. It was busy but not absolutely crowded. It was fun chatting to some of the locals, although one didn't know when to stop. A great place to visit!
Nice beach at the end of a small trail. Take your beachwear and insect repellant. Nice place to hang for a few hours!

white jungle beach - This beach is perfect as its quite small but perfect. There may be times when its busy, but we went there twice and it wasn't that bad, plenty of space to sit, only a few sunbeds though so bring some stuff to sit on the sand with. It is surrounded by a jungle so there are fire ants etc, you have to be careful where you sit. The water is different everyday depending on the tide, one day it was calm and beautiful soft sand, another day it can be slightly stronger waves, lots of shells, and lots of rubbish in the water and beach. There are a few shacks selling drinks and food. Definitely recommend visiting this beach! Just be ready to climb back up the rocky path! its only about a 10-15min walk though to wear you can take a tuk tuk back to wherever you want to go so its not too bad. Please note: There are 2 jungle beaches. Ask the locals or tuk tuk driver, depending on which beach you want to go. White Jungle beach - access from the bottom of the hill opposite the cement factory on the main galle road, or if you google where the hotel cantaloupe levels is, its on the same road, probably about 100m before that hotel. (great hotel by the way!). Tuk Tuk up this road from unawatuna beach is probably about 400-500 rupees as they dump a lot of petrol trying to get up this massive hill! Jungle beach - is the smaller jungle beach which is beyond the rocks on the left hand side of white jungle beach. You can swim from white jungle beach to this small jungle beach. This one isn't so great, and the trek is longer too. To access this small beach, you can go from the end of wella dewala road (the unawatuna beach road), and the path has clear signs to jungle beach and locals will also help direct you.

It is only a 10 min tuk tuk from unawatuna which cost 400rupees then a downhill walk down to the beach. The beach itself is nice and hidden away with lovely views. However we went on a Sunday morning and it was very busy. There are only a few places selling food and drinks which were quite expensive. It is a nice change to the big unawatuna beach but nothing special.

It was nice to visit this beach but there wasn't much down there and when we went it was really busy (a Saturday). I'm not sure you could spend the whole day unless you take supplies with you or if your requirements are minimal! :) There are a couple of beach shack bars which could probably do great drinks but food options may be limited. We didn't stay long....

it's a place where you can relax without much distraction surrounded by a small jungle. Its good if you take what you want before you go to the location such as snacks and water.. small crowed always will be there but ave to leave the location before 06.00PM. its a good place for couples who needed much idle to be closer more to get the business done ;-) Better to take a local tuk tuk from where you stay which will cost you less than you expect.

We set off from our hotel in Galle to spend a relaxing morning on the beach. We had been recommended to Jungle Beach for a week day visit and swim but not at the weekend apparently when it is very crowded. It has a simple beach bar and sun loungers but there is a lot of rubbish at the back of the beach in the undergrowth.  It was OK - there are a nicer beaches.

This beach is very touristy, I had Images of a hidden beach at the edge of the jungle but you can see gale from the beach, also it's a 20 min walk from unawatuna, plus you get all the tour groups going. We had a struggle to find a place to put a towel down and it's not a very relaxing place

Jungle Beach is hidden from view down a half mile meandering track. The beach itself is great with coral sands and one shack restaurant. There are very few people here and it is very peaceful. The only thing that let's it down is the piles of rubbish dotted about.
Beautiful small beach it is fabulous.one beach shack.good for surfing a couple of sunbeds good for children quite quiet.
20 minutes trip by boat from Unawatuna. Excellent beach quieter than Unawatuna. Small restaurant, -not very good-...
Lovely jungle safari and amazing water sports .... Guide and trainers are helpful . We covered this through Unawatuna beach Must visit

It takes about 30 minutes to walk from Unawatuna beach to Jungle beach and it's not an always more than a thin path that goes up and down the hill. The beach is very nice and doesn't have the big waves as Unawatuna.
The place was packed with the Sri Lankan navy playing volleyball. Even so we found a old jetty which was great for snorkeling from.

Except for the plastic bags and plastic bottles that float on the water, this place is a must visit. We really enjoyed going there as it is a great secluded beach with awesome scenery. There is a place were you can buy drinks and food and is very convenient. It is a steep climb up and down so be warned. The trip back yo anawatuna beach should cost you no more than 400 rupees. Don't let them charge you more.

The only somewhat different thing about this beach is that there is no hotel in sight on the beach itself. Other than that it does not feel secluded or private or is in anyway particularly nice. It is tiny and packed w people. That being said, there's not much to do in Unawatuna so if you want to walk a bit it's as good a destination as any for a few minutes.
Take the 30min walk over the hill to jungle beach, and you will not be disappointed Beautiful sandy gently sloping beach, perfect for kids and adults alike

Convenient location near Galle however lots of broken coral making it a bit unpleasant for swimming. Bit of a trek (10 mins) to get to it, which I guess is half the appeal, but that didn't stop it being quite busy
We were able to cross "drink beers on the beach in paradise" off our bucket list thanks to jungle beach. So beautiful, calm, and warm waters. Can't wait to come back.

Went there by tuk tuk. The beach was crowded and while it wasn't really dirty, I wouldn't call it clean either. It's small, there are some stones in the water that allow some snorkeling but the visibility was not exciting when we went. When crowded this beach is not special at all. The only positive I see is that you get a view of galle fort from a different perspective. Don't go by tuk tuk or if you want to do a walk. If you have a scooter or motorcycle, the trip can be nice. But the beach is not really worth the journey.

lovely beach away from city. But the place is infested with crowds in the day time. sad to see the litter everywhere, there was a man cleaning them in the morning so we also helped. Visit in the morning to avoid huge crowds..

The beach lies hidden. You have to ask for the road. It is a small, cosy place. Depending on the time, you are alone or among other people. Last time I visited the place, it has been just my husband, me and few (five) other people spending a great afternoon over there. Sometimes it is possible to order meals and drinks from locals that do some magic and organise it somehow to the Jungle Beach =)
Two hundred of locals on a very very small beach, friyng their food on a fire. Lots of garbage in the water. No place to sit. Dont go there.
Dirty, crowded and noisy made this beach trip particularly unpleasant, and we left after a quick swim in the crowded sea.

Short version: don't go. Longer version: it was described as paradise, but it is far, far from that. There was litter absolutely everywhere. Mounds of it. And we went during school holidays so it was very crowded, though most of the other visitors appeared to be having a good time. Perhaps it's better at other times, though I doubt it. Without the refuse it might be sweet little beach, but it was hard to see past it (almost literally). Ignore the sign that says there is a beach cafe 100m along the beach - there isn't one. The only place we could find was up by the road.

Gyönyörű kis öböl ,nemkönnyű megtalálni de remek hely csak egy kicsit szemetes. Beautiful small beach ,but a little bit to many litters, please don't leave behind any garbage . not to easy find it,not to easy find it,but worth it.

After a 5 min walk through a lovely jungle, what greets you at the bottom is not as reviews suggest! Rubbish all over the beach and in the water, extremely crowded. Would not want to swim in the sea at all. Spent 15 mins here and walked back! If you want a quiet clean beach with plenty of space, I would go to KOGOLA BEACH.

This beach is so special, the walk through the jungle was fun as you come across monkeys and wildlife, only a short 10min walk and then you come to the amazing view of the beach, it's quiet and secluded, highly recommend visiting this hidden treasure
Beautiful secret beach in Unawatuna. Not too crowded. Water, coconut water and snorkel gear available for rent. You can either get tuk tuk (we were quoted 500ruppees) or walk (~30 min).

We walked here from the main beach of Unawatuna- took a small half hour at a leisurely pace through nice bit of the nature. The beach itself has lovely soft sand which is great for building sand castles but was quite busy and small. It was nice not to be pestered by sellers on this beach. There is only a small cafe at the top of the last descent which has fairly standard prices for the area but otherwise you need to bring your own food and drink

The beach it self is not much. Cozy but small. I really enjoyed the walk from Unawatuna though. A bit of an adventure. Bring good shoes. If you have small children take a tuk tuk. We found a small pond of Hanuman on the way, visited the Japanese peace pagoda and Buddhist/Hindu temple.

Nice beach with a view of Gaulle Old Fort. Isolated, not crowded, beautiful colours and place. You can walk from Unawatuna from a small road, about 20 minutes, through coconut trees and nice jungle atmosphere or take a tuc tuc that takes you really close to the beach. Sundays are for locals, so better go another day as usually they party a bit more than usual... Scenery is really beautiful! There is a small cafe reastau close by for a drink or a meal. Also, you may visit the Japanese Peace Pagoda on your way or when leaving. A worth visiting place all in all if you stay on Unawatuna beach 😃

Popped here after what seems a well trodden path of the temple and the Japanese pagoda. Parking a pain at the top and then a steep track down to the beach a few hundred feet below.  Last section has steps  watch out for the monkeys on the way down! Small shack selling juices and drinks - think some lager there as well.  They do fish on a small grill as well but we didn't try. Sand itself is nice with a few wooden loungers.  Sea shelves gently but the water has lots of rubbish in it - real shame but hardly surprising in Galle bay.
Worth visiting ! A nice beach, great for group activities with friends ! Had a good time there and will go again !

Worth a visit. Me and my family went on Friday (it was a poya day in Sri Lanka) so it was very crowded. Beautiful sea. Better to walk from Unawatuna because way to the beach was amazing. But please take your garbage when you leave.

Don't go by tuk-tuk! One of the best things about jungle beach is the way from Unawatuna. About 40 minutes to go, jungles around, monkeys on the beach. The sea is quite dirty, so not the best place for swimming. However there are no waves. The beach is very romantic and beautiful.
To reach this beach you need to walk a nice trail in the jungle, and at the end you're rewarded with a small beach with scenic views.

First you're perfectly able to go & return without Tuk-Tuk by public bus. Second poor visibility (less than 5 meters) doing snorkeling, a lot of garbage (inside/outside the water) and the food options I don't recommend them. Maybe the weather conditions that day, in fact I have to get out of water because thiny jellyfishes (I'm not overreacting, I'm a diver Open Water). It's much better Koggala beach (you could walk through Wijaya beach)
Worth a visit . We went on sunday when the place was full if locals having picnics, enjoying the sea, playing the drums   and dancing on the beach which was cool.Nice cafe at the top

I walked from Unawatuna. It way to the beach is well signed. More crowded then Unawatuna. But then again, it is a small beach. Surprised about the amount of rubbish and plastic people left behind. Please take your rubbish when you leave. And take some of the other rubbish as well to keep this place special (-:

I understand what this place used to be. Its a nice little beach which the jungle comes right up to. We even saw a snake dining on a frog. Sadly, the beach is also full of rubbish now too. Which ruins an otherwise good swimming beach.

We liked jungle beach. The walk through the jungle and seeing the monkeys was great and the beach itself was lovely. The water was clear and the view was great. It certainly isn't a quiet empty beach but not that touristy compared to some of the others in the area. We did go to both jungle beaches  (there's a second smaller one just further on, accessible via a track near to the Japanese Pagoda) and the second one definately felt a bit more untouched. We also liked that the locals obviously enjoy coming to these beaches. The sea was pretty gentle so no surf great for a swim.

Located close to Japanese peace pogoda this beach has backdrop of forest.  Relative small beach compared to unawatuna. But it is peaceful& clean. It is very crowded on weekends as many local tourist visit.

You have to go by tuk tuk, I then go on foot through stairs for 5 minutes. It's easy, except if you are very old/young. On the way we saw several little monkeys. We took snacks fto eat has it has only 2 bars montly with drinks. Great place, quite, clean, beautiful. However, there are corals there, lots of shells in the sand, so it hurts a bit in the feet. I spend a morning there, I think it's enough, or 1 day.

Takes a long descent through jungle to get here so if you're unfit, don't bother! It's worth the walk though - we met a bunch of monkeys going through a pile of rubbish for water - they all knew how to open the water bottles so that was cool. This is quite a wild beach but there is a place to buy drinks and palm trees provide natural cover. Didn't hang around for the sunset as the mozzies come out early here.
Gives the feeling of calm sea side with thick jungle around it. good place for friends to party, please do not pollute the environment, area will be endangered,

Sadly, as with anything, when word gets out the masses visit and destroy it. We last visited here only 5-6 years ago, and we were shocked to see how this beach was covered with litter and that there were many, many people winding their way down to the waters edge. It is just a tiny beach, that you used to have to walk through jungle to get to it, and now there is a small road leading to it and masses of people throwing their rubbish everyone when they come. Its not worth visiting anymore. Save yourself the trouble.

Not that secret as you might think. .. the first time we've been there we felt like in a very special place cause we were almost alone.  But the nixt time we were surrounded by so many families that the place kind of lost its charme. Snorkeling equipment to rent for 600 rupies; you can see a lot of colorful fish but sadly the reef itself is almost completely dead. Still worth a visit.

Jungle Beach is a popular spot and it does provide a small Bay Area to swim and sun that is away from the busier, touristy areas. The entry into the water however is limited and you must navigate carefully around rock. The propose of my review is more directed to OW swimmers who seek training areas when they travel. I wouldn't recommend Jungle beach as a safe spot for early OW training in case you seek this as the area is solitary and visibility is not good to navigate safely the rock formations on the bottom as you head out to open water and bear right to "coast" from there. Best to OW train in Unawatuna.
Not sure why this is rated so highly on trip advisor, but the beach itself is dirty and depressing. The walk to jungle beach is  more enjoyable than the beach itself.

Went for the walk from our hotel. The beach is a walk of 2km. Takes about 40 minutes from the village. You walk through the jungle. Or a little part of it. Beach looks nice and everybody gives me directions. Arrived around noon. Lots of sun. The water wasnt really clear and has lots of plastic waist floating around. Snorkeling with some black coral and fish go to the far left side when you enter Jungle beach. Conclusion its a nice walk but for the beach only I can't recommend it
It could be a really nice beach but there was a lot of plastic trash. After our visit we still felt it was a good idea to visit because the nature is beautiful there.

We found out this when we were leaving our hotel one of the service persons told us it's a good place to go. It was easy to find as  the Peace Pagoda was close to it. If you are going avoid paying for parking at various places with placards and drive straight as there are enough parking spaces right next to the beach. The beach is clean and secluded although not very big. It's a great place for a coupe to retreat and spend some time. The water looked clean and inviting but I was too lazy to go in. Take your own food and water as there are no shops around for some distance. Also take some decent clothing so you can go to the Japanese Peace Pagoda. The view of the ocean from it got to be one of the best I have seen anywhere in the world.

It's location is lovely, you need to walk through wooded jungle to get here, and can get here from two sides.  It's  a cosy bay but if you want food or just a drink from the establishments that provide them you'll pay a premium as there are only two cafes there.  So take your own stuff and enjoy the little cove

You can see crowdes of people here, but most of them are locals. Place is nice and surrounded by jungle, you can just walk here from Unawatuna, it wouldnt be more then 2km. Also you can take tuktuk for maybe 300.
A very small & sweet beach literaly in the middle of jungle. 15 mins walk from the top to bottom, beautiful views.

It is not very easy to reach (at the end you cannot go with scooter anymore), however there are still quite some trash on the way and near the beach. It is also just a very small spot, nothing too special about this hidden beach. There is no restaurant there. But if you stay at Unawatuna for some time, it is not bad to take a look at this place. 我們是騎機車去的，到後面只能用走的。本來以為蠻隱密應該會比較乾淨，但是還是看到不少垃圾。整體而言沒什麼特色，就是一個非常迷你的海灘。
It is private and beautiful. The sea was a little rough but it is still definitely worth a visit. Lovely little bar and a restaurant if you need refreshments.
