Not having any idea of tide times my friend and I arrived at Jungle beach and the tide was high and still coming in. The beach itself would be lovely if it was still a secret spot. It there was 3 other couples there and it felt crowded due to the high tide. The Jungle Beach In restaurant is definitely worth a trip to though with lovely staff, great food and clean, modern rest facilities.

My wife and I went to Jungle Beach hoping to do some snorkelling. Nope! It looks like a recycling centre with all the plastic bottles on the beach. The water is dirty too. It must be because it's on the port side of the harbour. Unawantuna Beach although commercialised as .... with all the bars and sun beds the beach it's so much cleaner and generally nicer. It wouldn't take too much to clean up Jungle beach. Like 60 mins with 10 people. I know being from Australia we're blessed with amazing beaches so I have high standards but I've seen much nicer beaches already in the week I've been in Sri Lanka. Do yourself a favour and go to Unawatuna. Trust me. I ignored the reviews on TripAdvisor...going to Jungle beach...there 40 minutes of my life I'll never get back.

It is hidden paradise. You need to walk down from path through the forest and once you reach down to the beach you will not believe your eves. It is amazing. They have bar there and they are preparing very nice cocktails. It is top of "to do" list.

Awful place ! (1 beach, north) While we were expecting a nature beach, we actually found this place all dirty (looks like an Indian place...), with rude people from the bar, noisy... We didn't even try the 2nd beach (south)... may be better?

There is an extremely treacherous descent over large boulders and rocks though part of it has steps. Anyone with joint issues or back problems should not attempt this as one has to climb back up the same way. It was late evening so was unable to see much but the lights of Galle and the Fort were very pretty. Very peaceful and quiet but the access is a negative.

Quiet place with a superb view of the vast ocean Have a couple of juice bars and can order supper as well The menu is limited though Superb place to have a sun bath. Nice place to have chill in the evening Small part of the sea covered by the hills and trees. Can have a boat ride if you prefer. There another small beach connecting, it's better suited for locals than foreigners. There's plenty of tuk tuks to get there from the main road . Not far in,about 3 km from the main road. Overall best at sunset
Extremely secluded and private beach ruined by its patrons :( bottles and plastics thrown everywhere in the beach. really sad.

The road from Unawatuna passes thru the Jungles and looks a little wild ending with this small beach. Good place for swimming and snorkeling , even when the ocean was rough, there were no waves. If you will be lucky , u will be along there. Disadvantage: clearness of the beach might be better , that should be provided by local authority.
Nothing special really. Has views of galle but not a lot else. Better off staying on Unawatuna beach.

Lovely setting for these small white sand sheltered coves (if you ignore the view of Galle) and an antidote to the commercialism of Unawatuna but spoiled somewhat by the accumulations of rubbish at the back of each beach.

Don't bother going to the trouble of going here. The walk from Unawatuna is okay but the beachside is filthy with loads of locals partying and leaving all their rubbish just lying in heaps, a real shame.

The walk from Unawatuna Beach to here through the small jungle is absolutely stunning! From this secluded beach you have a beautiful view of the sea and the city. There is also a beach bar here where you can get some snacks and drinks. Would recommend visiting to anyone who is in Unawatuna or Galle!
Nice beach but the water was not very clean. Nice though that its not a lot of people. If you go more to the left there is one more small beach that is even more nice!

Low season,good athmosphere,and tranquil place at this time.some places are overprized,somehow all Lanka seems a bit overprized compared to other asian countries.lots of budget options of sleeping,go to buffet place for dinner,at mati gedara (or almost the name),or coconut hut for cooking class!😊

It's a tiny beach with a hut selling refreshments in a nice shady 'jungle' location. The walk down to the beach is nice, but honestly it's not all it's made out to be. Worth a visit, but don't get too excited.
There isn't much jungle about this beach, only garbage floating around and a not very charming bar. Tanning beds provided, but not really nice to stay on since they are hard wood and no cushion.

Take the lane going down besides entry to Japanese peace pagoda and in 800 m downhill u hit one of the most amazing clean private beaches in Sri Lanka. Parking available but no food options (few restaurants are there but due to less crowds not sure if they serve food ). Worth a visit ,watch out for langurs who snatch away any cover having food .

Bit of a trek down a rocky hill to reach it, bit once there a beautiful, but small beach.  One food place on the beach, prices a bit high for choices and quality, but with lack of competitors, the world is his.   Saw lots of Monkeys in the trees and a few hermit crabs scuttling around.  There is a coastal walk, but a bit rough and very dirty with litter.  Lots of locals use the beach and I felt safe enough, but uncomfortable slightly with the gaping at my teenage daughter.   Don't think there is anything to be concerned about, but be wary if you are trekking through a jungle as can be remote  and I think some single females may feel uncomfortable.   Lots ot Tuk Tuk waiting at the top of the trudge back up the hill to transport you onwards.   Be wary of the water though.   Strong currents and waves when I was there and I saw two local boys getting pulled from the water after going under.  They both got resuscitated, but scary to see.  Keep a watch out!

After spending several days on Unawatuna Beach, we heard great things about Jungle Beach and decided to spend a day there.  The walk down to the beach was lovely.  However, the beach itself was a great disappointment.  There was rubbish everywhere!  There were quite a few people there on the day, so we did not venture into the water at the safer & cleaner end of the beach. Not worth the tuk tuk fare to get there

Visited jungle beach last week & found it relaxing but get there early as it does become quite busy later on in the day. Also care is needed on  your way to & from the beach as the area is quite rocky & can be rather tricky. Unfortunately there's no where on the beach to purchase refreshments from so remember to bring your own, although there's a rather nice restaurant at the top of the hill close to the Japanese peace pagoda with stunning views over the bay.

Nice walk down to a quiet beach with small cafe selling drinks and local fish. Friendly locals directed us to swim on left side of beach to avoid rough coral on feet. Only pity was the rubbish that blows in from the sea probably people throwing rubbish off boats and the ramparts at the fort. The locals sweep the rubbish off the sand which is nice but up into the bush which looks dirty. Needs to be buried or taken to the dump. Otherwise lovely. I think they should ban plastic water and those little plastic bags  bottles in srilanka . It's a beautiful county with beautiful people trying to cope with too much plastic

This is a lovely, little beach that's off the beaten path. You have to walk through a small area of forest to get there. Once you arrive, you're welcomed by an amazing, secluded beach. Perfect for relaxing in peace.

I was told that Jungle Beach was a little hidden gem. What I found out is quite the opposite. Small cove, murky sea and way too overcrowded for a secluded beach. I was also told that there is a little restaurant that provides drinks and food. Well... not any longer (beginning of September 2016). If you decide to go there, bring everything you need with you. There are no facilities, not even rubbish bins - but there is a sign advising you to keep the beach clean. But expect that you'll be charged for the parking or whatever. I did confirm twice with locals that that place was indeed Jungle Beach. I should have read more reports before deciding to go there.

It's a bit of a walk to get this place from the Japanese Peace Pagoda, it better to walk it still, adds to the fun of travelling. Its not a beach per say, but a secluded bay with good waves and decent place to find some sun and to sit under the trees. It felt safe and the locals gave it a party environment it. You will be able to spot monitor lizards around the area, which gives it the jungle feeling. Good to spend a few hours and there is a lovely restaurant at the beginning of the climb as well.

A lovely little beach that needs a mini trek to reach. Completely worth the walk. Compared to the other beaches in the area, this one has much calmer water. There are a mix of locals and tourists. You'll see a lot of locals sitting around in groups getting drunk and singing baila to drums and a number of sunbathing tourists as well. The water is warm and gentle and perfect to relax in. Like the rest of the beaches, very salty water and so very easy to float and just relax. There's not much in the way of a sea bed view if you want to snorkel here but I hear there is a reef about 500m off the coast of this beach to the west. There is one restaurant on the the way from the road which is good stop for a beer and eats. Worth the visit for a relaxing dip in the sea.
Secluded beach, warm water, nice way to get there (jungle). The guy on the way ho has a parking and sell coconut really helpful and nice to talk to

We parked at the top of the entry road (had to pay when leaving) and walked down the hill past some cafes and homes. The walk is fairly easy going down, uphill coming up. Not fun in the boiling hot weather. There is an amazing view when you reach the end of the road however the water is just crashing on the rocks, we found no beach. You can take a track to your right through the 'jungle' to take you to another beach which looked popular with the locals

First of all, don't go by the signs in Unawatuna thay say "jungle beach this way" as it's waaaaay further away than one would imagine. We followed them and ended up at the other end of Unawatuna beach  and had to walk all the way back as well since we could not find a tuk tuk there. Secondly, it's dirty (beach and water), hard to get to, and the beach is full of broken coral that make it a very very unpleasant 2/3m entrance in the water. (The is the tourist jungle beach not the one for the locals. You don't want to go to that one trust me, it's far worse).
Hidden away in Unawatuna is a place called Jungle beach. You have to embark on a small hike through jungle to get to it. Upon arrival we found only locals, it was a cool spot and worth a trip!
After a short walk through the jungle, this great beach waits for you! Unfortunately swimming is not great because of rocks.

We were there out of season and it was pretty quiet, just a handful of tourists. We walked there from Unawatuna which was a pleasant 40 minute stroll, nothing too strenuous and better than taking a tuk tuk. The beach is a nice one and the sea was beautiful but the view of Galle wasn't particularly picturesque for me. We didn't stay long, we like the beach but soon get bored!!
Disappointed once I made the steep decent to jungle beach. Small area crowded with tourists and back packers. Many other easier accessable beaches in the area with more room to move.

Definitely need a tuk tuk to the top of the access walk as it is uphill and quite a distance.   Walked down the hill and disappointing to find a commercial operation has the prime spot on the beach.  However we have now discovered there are 2 Jungle Beaches.  Enjoyed swimming but off putting having odd bits of litter floating around and the beach also littered.  Loved watching the monkeys including cute babies playing.  There is some sharp coral so be careful.  Relaxing place to spend part of a day and a short walk from here to the Japanese Peace Pagoda which is worth a visit.  Shade trees are available.    We rang tuk tuk to pick us up at Peace Pagoda afterwards.
This is really nice hidden place in unawatuna its a paradise btw..you can see lot of things in here Its a hidden beach btw
It was full moon when we visited the beach, really nice day with the lovely locals. Go here to relax a bit, sun and shadow both available

Lot of locals come to this beach, but a proper life-guard was not seen, beach was not clean with lot of lunch left overs and sheets thown under trees, wish authorities would take more action to keep such a popular local destination clean.

20 minutes walking from the main Unawatuna beach you will find this beautiful small beach full of local people, it's very easy to get there. There is also a small restaurant if you're hungry, but there's not much to do there, only lay on the beach, swim and relax ;)

Beautiful beach, couldn't fault it. Really picturesque and hidden from the hustle of people selling stuff to you at nearby Unawatuna. Trek is worth it and you get a chance to see monkeys on the way! Only downside is the sea shore is full of broken coral which isn't nice when getting in/coming out of the water.

Since it was shown just 1-2km from our hotel ....We thought of going there in the evening. But it was an isolated place & the route also....while going here & there ,you can see Jungle Beach (way Finder Arrow)....Some  how we trek down reached some where a part of Jungle beach...It was really scary because we saw no 1 else ....other than a foreigner who was also searching for the way to reach the jungle beach.... Since we felt it may be a place for anti -social activities , we went back half the way.... It is really hidden place...If anyone going, I suggest you to go in group....
Really out of way bay which means quite quiet -when we got there really sheltered bay with small bar on beach which was very pleasant
Bit off the grid but not worth the effort to get there. Mostly dirty and poorly maintained beach with tons of non degradable plastic waste that the locals toss around with impunity.

Place is very near to Japanese Peace temple, Place is quite peaceful, and no other activities to do, just a restaurant and sun loungers, place is quite overrated by the local guides and tuk tuk drivers. Just a place for people looking for peaceful sun bath.
Its good to go for 1/2 day just to see, its busy as many locals go here as well, no beds, no bars, no restaurant but fantastic views and sea.

We reached the beach at 8.00am which was good because it gets crowded. The beach could have been cleaner but the experience for kids was great. They enjoyed the walk down through the trees and steep precipice.

There are actually 2 jungle beaches; one with sunbeds and a restaurant and one without. You can enter the one without sunbeds near the japanese peace pagoda. This beach is quite peacefull if there arent any locals making noise. The water here is also more calm. Near the rocks you can go snorkeling, everywhere else the water is too muddy. The beach with sunbeds has a more rougher entrypath, but this is a nice short hike trough the jungle. The view from this beach isnt amazing and the beach is not suitable for snorkeling. The water is, altough the waves could get quite big, suitable for relaxing. All together we think these beaches are overrated: the view isnt amazing, the sunbeds are quite hard, no showers, many locals, no stunning underwater scenery, but it is indeed a beach in the middle of the jungle.

A small beach close to Unawatuna and Galle. Make sure to go to the right one. The White Jungle Beach has a lot of dead corals in the sand and it's difficult to pass on the way to the sea. The correct Jungle beach is a better place to stay for families.

we just went there for a stroll, its very nice, you walk down a jungle to end up at a beach, opposite to the galle light house,  its a public beach to expect it to be crowded on weekends, we were there on a thursday so there were only a few people, we didnt swim, but there were sunbeds i think for rent, and a restaurant.

this beach which is hidden behind the lush greenery of the Rumassala mountain at Galle is very much private and not at all crowded. how ever the season is from November to April when the seas are calmer with the onset of the north east monsoons.....this south west beach is almost a swimming pool in the sea after November.

As the name suggests, this beach is accessible through a jungle. The road leading to this beach is in terrible state (mud road). You have to hike/walk another 200 meters to reach the beach. No lights. Nothing great. Pay parking 200 meters before the beach rps50.
My visit of this area my friend advise me. He live in gelle near to jungle beach he is juwler of this area name Handed howlers.

This is not a long beach or not much clean as sand is mixed with rubbish left behind by visitors. But you can find clean spots on the beach and also the view around is very calm and pretty. It is about 5min ride by tuk tuk from main road to Rumassala side and on the way to Japanese Peace Pagoda. There are two beach entrances and I recommend the one before the temple as the other is too crowded and polluted. Surrounding is full of trees and very good place to enjoy an evening.
5' walk in the Jungle and then Jungle Beach. Too much garbage and dirt on the right side of the Beach and in the sea. Water is not clear. But Nice secret but now too we'll known by tourists

After spending the previous day at Unawatuna (great waves, lots of bars and lots of people), Jungle Beach was the perfect compliment to this. We got there about 9.30 in the morning and found an empty beach, a stunning view and calm water that was beautiful to swim in. We had heard a lot of criticism about this beach being over crowded so my best advice is to go in the morning!

The beach itself is beautiful and very relaxing, bar staffs are friendly. But i was disappointed with the sight of left garbage at the  far end of the beach. trash are being washed off to the sea and are floating all over. Sri lankan Government should clean up this mess.
Overrated place, many rubbish on the beach, quite expensive bar however good place to take nice photos and you can see some monkeys when you will go by jungle to get into beach.

As an Australian I tend to have high standards when it comes to beaches. Mostly the standards revolve around cleanliness because all beaches and coastlines are beautiful. I enjoyed swimming here looking out towards Galle, and back at the secluded surrounds of coconut palms and jungly cliffs with a beautiful white dagoba looming above the greenery. However, walking between the 2 small bays and also back behind both beaches was the seemingly inevitable and disappointing piles of rubbish - plastic and glass bottles, straws, styrofoam food containers and plastic bags. If the groundskeepers/beach rakers were to focus on picking up the rubbish (which wouldn't take long) it would be so much more enticing and enjoyable and invite more people. I don't understand the mentality of those who trash such a gorgeous and sacred environment. And I don't understand why raking leaves takes such precedence over picking up rubbish.

it looks great but try find space is impossible, but it is crowded by the locals so you can be joined by a family from Colombo where your playing cricket with the lads and getting forced to eat there mothers extremely hot food.
A super beach with a steep stair climb through jungle . We saw lots of monkeys. Had a good lunch at the beach cafe and a fabulous day. Highly recommend .

It's a beautiful beach but have to hike long to get in there. Me & my friends enjoyed the swimming up there but the locals can be little disruption to other tourists. I think if they could develop this beach further will be a paradise
So disappointing, yes the location is great. We got told it was great for snorkelling, but the visibility is so poor

I visited this much recommended beach during the stay in Unawatuna, or at least I thought I did? I followed all the signs although I had to walk/hike/scramble for a small distance after parking the car. One can reach it either from the side of Galle or from Unwatuna. Reaching from Galle appears the more suitable if you do not want to risk slipping and falling on rocks, especially when its wet. Once there, the general view is pretty however, the dreadful piles of litter, plastic bottles and generally unkepmt nature of this place is a tragedy. IF this was THE jungle beach and you wish to hike the hard way, do it ONLY in proper shoes, or trainers NOT flip flops!

Only 20 minutes walk from Unawatuna Main Street and the shops and restaurant.. And also on the way to the Peace Pagoda for an amazing sunset! We did a trip around Sri Lanka for our honeymoon and wanted to cover the south coast towards the end of our travels... being monsoon season, it was difficult to find anywhere to snorkel or less crowded with white sands and lush water... This was just the place!

Great beach for children, small beach bar but amazing what cocktails and food comes out of it. Has some shaded area plus wooden loungers and a toilet. Take a tuk tuk ride and walk down the last bit to the beach. There's 2 parts to the beach and the other is smaller and more local with no facilities.

A nice small beach were locals and tourists are spending good time, having fun in the waves or sleeping on the wood deck chairs, or enjoying a coconut or,a cocktail at the bar. This is a simple and friendly place that you will find after a little,walk in the jungle.

We got there early with a three year old.  Up until 10AM everything was fine and then they said we needed to pay 1000 Rupees for each sun bed.  Whatever, we packed up and left.  There was a small beach restaurant here but did not see any toilets or showers.  Totally, not worth the hassle but we were happy to at least go on a tuk tuk ride.
very nice and small beach and its full of locals, dancing, singing and barbequing and playing beach balls.

Jungle beach was a bit rough the day we went. So we sun bathed and took in the view instead of swimming. Lots of lovely coral on the beach with a handy bar not to far away, which also sells food. A good day out and your surrounded by nature and lots of trees

Good please to relax and enjoy..Jungle Beach used to be quite isolated. You'd need to go up the Peace Pagoda, well off the main strip, and then hike in a circle round a peninsula before you arrived. Now you still need to get to the Peace Pagoda but they've cut some stairs straight down the hill and once you get there there are beach beds and a little restaurant. We're not sure if this is necessarily a good thing, but it does make access easier. Nice economic friendly please to be.

There are 2 ways to get to Jungle beach from Unawatuna centre, you can take a tuk tuk via the main road or you can do a 30 minute walk. We preferred the walk as it was nice and quiet but also it gets you ready up for a dip to cool off once you arrive. The beach is off to the side of a larger bay/inlet, as a result it does not get the strong waves of the pacific. The calmer waters make it a great destination for swimmers of all abilities. The Japanese peace pagoda is also adjacent to the beach which is worth a look.

Definitely a hidden beach and far nicer than the main beach in unawatuna, but because of its size and amazing views it can get fairly busy at times. Forget about any chance of enjoying a remote, quiet, getaway spot as at certain times of the day this beach can be packed full of people. During these times it can also get a bit tricky getting in and out of the water as a mass of bodies often blocks the only sandy access into deeper waters.  Families with elderly and small children should also be cautioned that the walk up down and up to the road can be quite steep and due to the heat, not suitable for all beach goers.
It was an adventure to get to Jungle beach. first you climb up the road then you climb down the jungle to the beach. Definitely had a great time here!

We went with the intention to spend an hour to an hour and a half there, ended up spending about 30 mins.. there were many locals which is ofcoarse ok as it's there land after all, but it was a huge group of ppl so we didn't feel like swimming. It's relatively small .. but if it's not busy, then it would be a beautiful little romantic spot.. and a nice 5 minutes walk in the jungle to reach it
This beach is defiantly one to visit, it was one of my favourites on my hole trip to Sri Lanka. Great drinks on the beach too, would return back.

It was a bit of a walk from the main road, but boy was it worth it! If you equally love the serenity of a jungle as well as a vast spread of the sea, this is a must visit. A pristine beach which is not very crowded (on a weekday). One of the few beaches in Sri Lanka which has not been polluted with people and man-made things too much.

You can go by a tuktuk, but you must walk after a point which is great, because you have to go through the jungle and can hear birds and monkeys in the trees. After a short walk you walk into a small beach. It is fascinating to have the ocean on your one side and a jungle and on the other. unfortunatelly the beach was polluted by peoples litter because there was a festival the da before. As told, the BEACH is perfect and must see on season. but there are also local people, some starred the tourists -very uncomfortable. We did not stay there too long but glad to see anyway.

We went to Jungle Beach on 1st August. Actually there are two beaches connected by a short easy path on the cliffs. The second one has got a restaurant too and some facilities such as chairs and umbrellas. Jungle beach is known to be a very good place for snorkelling with living corals but that day the sea was very rough and visibility was very very bad. Besides the beach was rather dirty with a certain amount of rubbish such as paper and plastic bottles left by people. The beach and the path need certainly to be cleaned. Maybe we have been unlucky but anyway we decided to move away after one hour. No reason to stay there.

This is in no way a deserted spot. Was once probably enchanting, but over crowded and quite dirty. There seem to be two parts to jungle beach and I refer to the one  closest to the peace pagoda without the restaurant.
Nice beach located in the jungle, avoid saturday and sunday local crowd. Great hidden spot to visit. No restaurant or sunbed on the beach.

Jungle beach is actually two beaches instead of one. If you - while on the beach with the bar - take the time to walk the path left (facing the sea) you arrive on a smaller beach. Here the water is clean and you can actually swim! Also this beach has   stairs to the street on the hill.

We hiked through the jungle to reach this secluded part of the coast.The hike is more interesting than the destination, found some really good sceneries around. I was a bit disappointed when we reached the place, quite crowded and the current was quite strong so I wasn't able to take a dip. Most folks were chilling out with their kindles or getting a tan. Along the way,as same with the whole of the country, rubbish is all over the place.Its a bit disheartening to see such trash in the middle of such great views.

Walking down a path covered with waste you will come to a small area called beach. There are some big rocks in the bay and there is hardly any sandy area. The creek mouthing the sea is completely polluted and you wonder in what you will be swimming. Furthermore there are tons of tourist coming to the area as the reputation is apparently good. There are no toilet and other services available.

This place would have been nicer if it was more spacious. It's a place with a beautiful view. The day we went there it was pretty crowded and hardly had a place to keep our belongings. Would have been better if they don't keep tables and chairs for large groups to make more room.

Very difficult to get here. We followed a short cut route which we got from the net and tripadvsior, but it was hellish as we had to walk through a jungle which was going nowhere. Better to take a tuk tuk to this place.

It's hidden away literally through the jungle and you feel like you've stumbled onto a little paradise. It's only a small stretch of beach but it's got a more local feel and people aren't hassling you to buy anything (although there is one restaurant if you want to get something). Leave before it gets dark because it gets dark so quickly and it's a scary climb back up to the road.

Away from the larger beaches of Unawatuna, this hidden gem has character. Even locals will spend their weekends here. A cafe also here but service is very slow. Worth the 30 min trek from central Unawatuna
Hang around, get a drink, eat some fish, get your feet wet, spot a monkey. Just a nice place to relax.

The way to the beach is nice. Cool trees, cool rocks and a fun side road that leads to a rocky beach with giant waves. Jungle beach itself is a bit of a downer. We went on a Saturday. Lots of locals with prying eyes on our bikinis. The beach looks like a dump. Waste everywhere, bottles, debris, you name it, we've seen it. Don't go.
An unusual beach in the jungle with lots of monitor lizards (don't worry, they are really shy) and very good sand. A bit difficult to get to, but definitely worth it!
Would definitely choose Jungle Beach over Unawatuna beach. You can either take a TukTuk there or just walk (it's a nice walk through the jungle).

Dont think of attempting this one if you are with elders in the group, with a bit of a steep walk down without a lot of support. But if you do get there eventually - grab a beer and sit in the shade and enjoy the view :)
Small secluded beach with great sand, view and small waves for swimming. It is quite a walk down so only down side is walking all the way back up after a relaxing day at jungle beach!

We came and visited this beach after visiting the peace pagoda, we fancied a little down time and thought it would be a nice place to do so, we stayed 5 minutes and left. The beach was filthy and there were a lot of wild monkeys which although very cute, we are concerned about flees and being bitten, obviously something to be avoided. The cafe which apparently used to be there is no longer and the tonne of rubbish there put us off hanging out there at all. Also to note, steep hill to get there.

This is a warning to any women travelling alone( or with partners) to jungle beach. I visited the beach alone 2 days ago and was almost sexually assaulted :-( it was the middle of the day, I was fully clothed walking down the steps that lead to the beach and was approached by a local Sri Lankan man who exposed himself to me and then proceeding to attempt to assault me, half way down the steps. I felt extremely threatened but managed to wriggle free luckily and ran down to the beach to get help, by this point the man had got away. Please be extra careful in this area and do not go down unaccompanied. I was very lucky that nothing happened but was extremely shaken after the experience and would hate for anyone else to have to go through this!

We walked here over the hill from Unawatuna beach. The walk was fun. The beach is not as good as the one at Unawatuna, in my opinion. There were lots of rocks/coral fragments that swept in and out with the surging waves so that my feet were scratched all over. It's a beautiful location and a fun place for a drink on the sand.

It was a good place to get the tropical warmth in a pristine beach. It's a pubic beach and no charges apply. The tuck shop nearby provides required juice and beer. It recommended visiting this place during the week days to avoid disturbances from excess crowd. The by road is not maintained properly, however it's less than 100 meters.
It is a long walk down, but jungle beach is worth it. Idyllic setting in lovely bay you find a basic beach bar, but fish is fresh and rest of food very good

We really liked jungle beach, way more cosy then Unawatuna beach. You can get there by tuktuk and a hike down some rock. People around will point you in the right direction, just ask around. I think you can get there by walking as well.
Litter everywhere, rocks in the water, small and crowded. Overpriced restaurant with no beer and bad food. Go to another beach, this one isn't worth your time
Native people were seen throwing rubbish into the sea i.e... beer cans and cigarette ends, Boats were polluting beach area with diesel and the air was polluted too, never recommend it to any one.

When we were with my son in Sri Lanka, Unawatuna, in the end of 2014 for a great week, we spent the best moments here on this beach - you can enjoy walk through the jungle, to see trees, animals, people living there, to listen to many birds, to have a great feeling of the nature. This beach could be reached in 40 minutes walk through the jungle. When you get there, the reward for your effort will be a beautiful view to the ocean, trees with monkeys and many birds, nice food served in small buffet, blue water, quiet atmosphere.... This is really right place for your relax, swimming, snorkeling and thinking about the life.

When we arrived at the Jungle Beach, we were just the two of us and one (huge) lizard. There used to be a restaurant which was removed but there are a lot of trash around which is a shame. Later on, many tourists and people came by which made it less special. Still a place to see.
Great beach, a short walk down the mountainside but worth it There were a few people there but there were also enough sun beds and a cafe that provides beverages and food. We enjoyed it

Quite a bit of a drive to get there with Tuk Tuk, then a relatively steep walk down to get to a relatively overcrowded short stretch of beach with old, wooden sun beds without any cover, a small bar offering some drinks, and otherwise nothing that I would call spectacular, or worth going there. Difference to Unawatuna Beach: The waves are a bit less vicious and therefore better suited for smaller kids; but then a lot of rubbish floated around us in the water which we don't find at the, much bigger, beach around the corner. Interestingly enough the 'Manager' requested a young group of tourists to buy drinks from the bar, or otherwise to pay 1000 (!) rupies for using those sunbeds...

My tuk tuk driver took me here and I'm so pleased I said yes!! A great little beach hidden away. Very pretty and a great beachside cafe serving food and drinks. I had a fresh pineapple juice which was 10/10. Lots of sun loungers and wasn't too busy when I visited. Would definitely go back. Pack a swim suit and enjoy the water!

We were encouraged to visit being told the beach was stunning! After a fairly long trek down to the beach (you need to be reasonably fit to get down and more importantly back up from the beach) we arrived to find a smallish beach area packed with people. Not my idea of something special! I can imagine if it was deserted, it would be worth a visit, however, there are far more beautiful beaches along the coast without clamouring down/up a number of steps to get to it!

After nice walk through nature reached nice little beach area. It's a kind of paradise where you can swim , snorkeling and specially relaxing. Avoid SW monsoon season, In SW monsoon this not a place to swim, sea bath or any activity with sea!!
After a great walk through a magcal jungle you will reach a wild, beautiful beach! A desert paradise that you can explore yourself.

Nice small beach in front of a small jungle. The route to the beach through the jungle is like 10 - 15 mins walk but thrilling. You will get a fill like going through a jungle. I heard if you are lucky you may see some monkeys though I didn't see any. On the beach there is one nice small restaurant where I can order some seafood or drinks.

We have visited Jungle Beach 5 or 6 times and enjoyed the cafe and facilities there,ie sunbeds, snorkel's and masks, plus good food, but after 6 years the authorities have closed it down and all the buildings including the toilets have been pulled down and completely cleared, including the sunbeds. It is a complete shame when the people organised the facilities did a great job, now what will happen, who will keep the beach clean?? Whoever decided on this ridiculous decision needs to rethink their plans or allow someone else to take over the running of this beautiful little bay. What a shame for the area.
Pretty and secluded beach. Not so much so anymore but a fun and beautiful place to visit in Unawatuna nonetheless.
This is quite a rough beach which has been unspoilt and not made just habitable for tourists. Locals and tourists alike come here.
not so much to so there , the waves are very high and dangerous but it's nice to be there just one time
Walked here and was very disappointed very dirty and small beach maybe better in season but out. Of season not worth it. I've from peace pagoda nice though
We were very excited about the view. had a sea bath. very clean and nicer beach. there are two roads to go to the Jungle beach. make sure use the road near to Japanese peace Pagoda.
From unawatuna, it's a 30 min walk. The beach is divided by rocks into two parts, but you can walk from one side to the other. There were only some sri lankan people, so it was very quiet.

A nice calm sea but polluted. Have a bit of walking to reach the beach.Has great views. But highly polluted with broken bottles, plastics and waste filled with drunken people. There was no proper restaurant in the beach for us to take lunch and when we asked the only restaurant  it had, they refused to give lunch saying they are only serving foreigners.
You know it's a great beach when the locals are using it. Beautiful calm water. This is a must see if you enjoy snorkelling.

went here because my auto driver suggested it.   You have a bit of walking to get to a small beach, filled with drunk locals, broken bottles and cans... we were out from there the moment we arrived there.....there were more junglies on the beach than Jungle !

It was a nice one hour hike with beautiful views of the Mirissa Beach and Rumassala peak. You can go on top of the mountain by a vehicle and then you have to go down by foot.  On your way you can visit the Japanese peace pagoda as well. The place was not much crowded. Make sure you go there in the morning so there is not much sun.

We found this beach to have a great vibe, very laid back feel. Only downside is that it is a very steep rocky walk to get to it and get back up again! Most tuk tuk drivers will pull over just before you get to the entrance as there is a great view point and photo opportunity !
Small beach  but needs to be protected from the onslaught of visitors. Nice place to take a dip as the sea is not rough here

The entrance to the beach is a wonder! You walk in through a mini jungle to find your way to a gorgeous beach with crystal blue waters! Sight for sore eyes! One of the must visit places to go to if you're in srilanka and in unawatuna!

The best thing I liked about this beach was that it wasn't too crowded. It has two small hits serving drinks and food. The walk to the beach which is through a jungle is great too. It's like a secret hangout which is just perfect for a lazy day out!

My friend and I decided one day to hike up the road from Unawatuna beach and then take the trail down to Jungle Beach where we could snorkel. Hike was pretty enough and when we arrived at the beach it was a decent size with lots of friendly folk around, and a small makeshift restaurant renting snorkling equipment for exploring the reef just offshore. Our first hint was the recalcitrance of the equipment renter to confirm what could be seen offshore.  when we got out the water was so murky that it was hard to see anything. I'm spots where visibility was better we could see that the reef was in very poor shape, so there was very little visible marine life. Big disappointment compared to Trincomalee and we soon decided to ditch the snorkling equipment and have a swim instead. The water in this spot is so warm as to feel truly like body temperature.

Very cool beach. There were approximately 20 people in total on the beach when we went, so it was quite quiet. Sea was relatively calm as it was sheltered from the waves. 2 bars on the beach which serve alcoholic and non alcoholic drinks. Prices are a little higher, but not ridiculously so. Definitely worth a visit.
Very interesting relaxing time, excellent service.... Very interesting architecture of the hotel, everything was just perfect. Relax, romance, enjoy ... Food just amasing

Nice enough beach, but the claim to be the best beach in Lanka...probably written by the guy who owns the bar there! Absolutely nice enough, but there are better beaches nearby. Very crowded, with sun beds very close to each other. Loo available.
Off season visit - not much to really see or do... Good night parties with resident DJ's, however There are better beaches around the local area to visit including Unawatuna beach
Very relaxing area with beautiful beach. Nice surroundings with great trees flowers etc. Nice restaurants nearby and great area for walking. A must visit when in Galle area
We liked this beach. Clear and has nice view. Not to hard to find. If you are around you may stop by. You will like

Lovely beach to get away. However you have to avert your eyes from the rubbish that's every where. Make sure you pack your repellant. Steep walk into the beach, but it's short & sweet. Stick it out it's not far.

This beach is quite small and you have to walk down a jungle track to get to it.  Thought it was too small for the amount of people who were there.  There were some people selling drinks and fruit platters on the beach.  Didn't stay too long, but we didnt go to sit on a beach, more to just explore.  its fun to combine the Japanese Peace Temple with Jungle Beach if you are just out and about exploring like us.
Best early in the morning for snorkeling and swimming when the water is calm. On a good day you can enjoy the sunset as well. A true gift Mother Nature has to offer.

I was initially a little sceptical about going here having read poor reviews of this beach. But my family and I were pleasantly surprised. The beach was clean and calm and managed to get in about an hour of snorkelling with my 11 year old and really enjoyed it. Visibility was poor but we were warned. I would suggest bringing your own snorkelling gear though!! I suppose it was the off season and hence the crowds were thin. Overall a nice experience.
Fabulous beach and very clean.  2 beach bars.  Food excellent. Surfing good and sea safe. make sure you spray for bugs and sun lotion, as it is  sun trap.
Lovely little beach away from the bustle of the main beaches of unawatuna.  Go here for a much more chilled vibe with good swimming options for kids as there was no waves.

This is a very nice beach if you want to chill and take a swim. There are two beaches connected with a path, I prefered the White sand jungle beach as it felt a bit more intimate. There is a cantine that offers juices, drinks and lunch.

We stumbled upon this beach after a long and scary drive of our tuc tuc driver and we were pleasantly surprised by the beach. It's secluded less crowded and warm water. Our kids loved it so much that they didn't want to come back.  Getting there would be a little scary since there is a steep and rugged path that goes down to the beach and there is also no facility for anything. You may have to make sure you don't need bathroom for at least your time there.😀

We wanted to see jungle beach in order to make some beautiful pics, but no sunset is seen from it. Anyway, beach itself is nice but the water sometimes is dirty due to the port on the other side of the bay. Worth visiting, but don't expect too much

Access Asphalt road half way, then rocky slippery slope, with some sand bags to create steps. Not available for tuk-tuks. Not wheel chair accessible. If you really want to go, you should be one who likes hiking, this place is definitely not for seniors or people with knee injures. From Unawatuna beach, go west to South Ceylon guest house (hotel?) & keep straight up what looks like the path on Google maps. No tourists, no shops, only locals live there, eventually asphalt will transform into a mud road & then mud & rocks. That's OK, keep straight. Wear comfortable shoes as the rocks are slippery. Follow the "Jungle Beach signs". At some point the path will split. Take the one going down & left. That's your Jungle beach path. If not, you can take up & to the right. You will get to Japanese Peace pagoda. Place Used to be a gem but not is really dirty, the area is tiny & we couldn't see why so many were so hyped about it. Also, if the waves are high, it gets dangerous on the rocks. Other than a few shots, there's nothing to do there really. Unless you love hiking in hell like heat. Otherwise just don't do it. Take a tuk-tuk or a local bus & go to see Galle instead.
Average beach. About 2m into the water the sand disappears and is replaced by jagged rocks. Lots of rubbish. Poorly constructed bars selling overpriced drinks. There are much better beaches around.

Jungle beach, although nice we felt was overrated. It is a small beach, which attracts quite a few tourists fir snorkelling. The day we were there the water was murky with quite a lot of rubbish floating in the water. The guys on the beach were friendly and we hired a sunloungers and bought a drink off them. The juice was good and I did see them bringing in ice made from clean water. The water was safer for swimming than some other beach areas.

The place is nice and potentially wonderful but we went on a weekend and it was overcrowded and full of drunk people screaming and singing and causing a riot in general. Not fun. We left in under an hour.
A beautiful little beach with a friendly restaurant that serves very good fresh fish. You have to walk down a rough steep path for 5 minutes before you get there.
Jungle beach was one of the most beautiful beaches in Sri Lanka. Very few tourists, crystal clear beaches, and a beautiful wooded path to reach the beach.
Bit of a walk to the beach. Pretty small beach and fills up pretty quick.Not private at all. Good for swimming for kids as the water isn't as rough here. Overall an average find

There is a good 10-minute climb down from the road and up again when you're finished. Beach is divided into two sections - one for a small cafe with tables and sunbeds and the rest for sunbathing and swimming. There are shady areas, too. Lots of coral offshore so watch your feet.  Best place to swim is centre area.i

When I visited Jungle Beach for the first time, a few years ago, hardly anybody had ever heard of it, except some locals. We were the only ones here on this Godly paradise piece of beach on the north side of Rumassala peninsula, No restaurant, no beach chairs, only a soft golden beach with a lukewarm sea all for you alone. The place is still nice for a relaxed stay, but during the season crowded with tourists from Unawatuna and in the weekend with lots of drunken locals too. There is a restaurant now, which provides soft drinks and cocktails. The food is far below standard, not fresh and no value for money (Rs. 800 for a fried rice). When you decided to go there you need to take a tuk tuk or make a long a climbing walk, because there is no public transportation. There is a connecting path from Unawatuna to Jungle beach too, about 3,5 km. There is also a possibility to hire a boat at Unawatuna to bring you to Jungle beach.The path from the main road is difficult and steep, not advisable for elderly who are not fit.Take your own picnic basket full of nice items and water and you can enjoy a wonderful time. A visit to Jungle beach can easily be combined with a visit to the nearby Peace Pagoda. Every Wednesday night there is a disco party.

Walked here from our lovely French Lotus hotel , the path was the best bit as what could have been a beautiful little beach has been ruined by rubbish everywhere - plastic , cans , bottles , piles of vomit ! ! Such a terrible shame

It's a nice idea, the little secluded beach, but the amount of beach goers steal its charm. The locals take it over at the weekend (and why shouldn't they?), and don't care much for kicking sand it the face of foreigners - not intentionally, mind you, they're all very friendly - as they kick about a ball or play cricket the length of the short beach. Not to worry, the bar served the purpose of being able to grab a cool cocktail, fruit juice or beer on the sand, and the food is fresh and reasonably priced, and tasty, though service is horrendously slow when the beach is busy. It's just not capable of handling a big crowd. In saying that, a weekday venture - getting there by kayak or through the trees - will throw up a different story.
Went on a little adventure to this beach.  I have to say I was a little underwhelmed.  It's nice but not much to rave about.

The location is great but unless you come at a time when it is inconvenient for the average person, expect to share this hideout with many others. Holidays and weekends I presume would also be crowded with folk drinking plenty of alcohol under the mangroves. Expect amorous company.
Spent a great day at this beach good food at little cafe good snorkelling and plenty of shade would defiantly return

Jungle beach is naturally very beautyful place. The waves are small, good to swimm and relax. Beach itself is covered with trees, so you can take sun in water and then relax under the trees. But... But all the beach area is wasted by different garbagge and plastic waste. There are no toilets - so all bushes and jungle near smells like s...house.
Great for kids and snorkelers. Café does good food and drinks, also has a party night on a Wednesdays if I remember correctly
on the opposite side from Unawatuna in front Galle a small jungle beach good place for snorkeling and swimming quietly. And relax on the beach with a cold beer..

nice beach, good for snorkling and perfect for families with kids, cos water is very calm there. better to go in the early morning, beach is quite small. I recommend to get there by walk, just 30 min  through the jungles from Unawatuna beach. Don't forget to take some bananas for monkeys ^^ also on weekend Jungle beach is  full of locals!
snorkeling just fine beach very crowded not much choice among restaurants more expensive than the other beaches we saw monkeys and the snorkeling was really fun

Walked from our hotel, nooit gedacht,up the mountain so it took awhile- & when we got there it felt well earned!  ( it's also pretty accessible by the road, though you do have to walk down a little ways to the actual beach).  We arrived in morning, which I recommend as it didn't get crowded until later. The water was beautiful & there was a little bar restaurant on the sand.  They use bagged ice, so mixed drinks were fine :)  pina colada not great but beers were cold.  There are chairs, but bring your own towel & no umbrellas either. There are also monkeys on the path & african fish eagles flying overhead.  Not the flash of Unawatuna, but if you want a little more peaceful & secluded, I highly recommend.

Spent a morning on jungle beach - water was much calmer that further up the coast so great for the children to play in. Clear water. Paths to access would cause some issues for people with buggies or wheel chairs but otherwise was fine.
Nice beach with a bar with softdrinks, beer and food. The food where so so. They have sunbeds, tables and chairs. You have to walk down on a hill to come to the beach!

Than when we arrived we were so disappointed. I am not sure what we were expecting but definitely not what we saw. After a long hike, you arrive on a tiny average beach with an industrial complex as the view on the other side of the bay. So do not expect the tropical paradise...

jungle beach is reached by a slightly rocky climb from the main road. The actual beach is very small and quite cramped with sun loungers, but the sea is nice for a swim. There are a few bars serving cocktails. If you follow the rocky path at the southern end of the beach (toward peace pagoda) you can walk round to another beach. Requires a bit of scrambling on rocks but fun

This nice little beach is a few minutes away from the high-way exit to Galle. You travel up the Rumassala mountain and walk down to the beach through the jungle. It is a natural bay and has slow waves during April. Great for snorkeling as well. You need to pick the right time of the year as during certain times, the waves are rough and there's a lot of broken coral that makes it difficult to have a proper dip in the sea.
great location and beach but the litter thrown around was terrible and spoilt what could be a fantastic spot to laze.

If you fancy doing something a little less lazy, then would certainly recommend the walk from Unawatuna Beach to Jungle beach. If you're luck you'll encounter monitor lizards, monkeys and bright birds en route - if you're less lucky you'll get a herd of bulls :) Have seen them all on various trips. Pretty steep in places, and can be slippy if it's been raining but lovely views and you really can hear the jungle all around you. The highlight of Jungle Beach is the underwater action - some wonderful tropical fish - like being in an aquarium! Unlike most of the sea in Sri Lanka it's also really calm at Jungle Beach, without currents so safe for children. The beach isn't huge but is nice, you can get cheap no frills eats and beers at the cafe, and you can see enormous lizards and wild monkeys in the trees, so all in all a pretty good day out.

Great place! A very nice and secluded beach. Small but with a little beach cafe, restroom and shower. Nice shallow clear water - good for kids and elderly. The path to the beach is steep and difficult to walk/climb.
Overcrowded, its a beautiful beach but so so crowded. Not worth going there. One restaurant/ bar but not very nice. Some sunbeds but no umbrellas
Great beach to go for a little dip and then have a sip of a nice, cold drink served by super laid back staff. It's easy to get to and great for swimming.
Calm seas for swimming, unlike the main beach.  Do not walk unless very fit as quite a climb. Get a tuk tuk to just above the beach and then it's only a five minute climb down - 500 rps each way.

As seen by other people who reviewed this I believe they are correct, as beaches go this is just ok. However, when comparing to other beaches in Sri Lanka it is pretty good then. We took a small boat ride through the mangroves saw Birds monitor lizards so it was rather interesting to see. The locals do not quite understand trash and litter everywhere is something many tourists do not want to see. On really hot days traveling in it took took for an hour is Harsh

What a dump! This was hyped up by the well known guide books used by travellers for decades but PLEASE don't waste your time. The hour long walk from the town was fun for us as we like to exercise but could be very hard work for some, as its rocky and steep in places. The sunset was spectacular and it was totally by luck we timed it right for this, as it was the only saving grace for what was basically the last stop for all the locals litter from beer cans and plastic bottles to food wrappers and fag ends and loads of floating plastic junk from the sea. I don't understand the total disregard the local seem to have for what could and probably once was a unique and very pretty hidden beach. Suffice to stay we took one look at all the rubbish which is EVERYWHERE!! and walked straight back to Unawatuna.

There's a main road along the beach and it's easy to take bus there. People also take bus to Mattana, Colombo or  Hikkaduwa there. We have 2 days walking along beach to catch stick fishing, but it's very expensive for taking photos. We spent time for walking along the beach, waiting sunset and talk to locals.

Very sheltered beach, meaning the water is calmer than the more popular tourist beaches in the area. Many locals, who are incredibly friendly and welcoming. Only a small shop, and it's a bit of a walk down a broken path to reach the beach. But definitely walk, a tuk tuk would be insane.

It was a great night, the drinks where okay, I had a few of the local whiskeys. The music was a little repetitive dum dum dum! The fire dancing was awesome and watching an feeling the waves wash over my feet was soo nice! The event is free entry...however the guys at the front did try to charge! But eventually he let us in.

If you love small beach coves with clear blue water and fantastic marine life then Jungle Beach is your place. If you continue to the Japanese Temple and turn down the side of it, you come across a small car park. Walk down the steps and there is a little restaurant that serves lots of food choices and drinks. You can also rent snorkelling equipment from them too. Lovely relaxing beach. Nicest beach in Unawatuna. Well worth a stop!!

Up and down a hill in (near Coco bay hotel) you find a small beach hidden in a jungle setting. Water is calm and good for swimming. No waves! There is a good priced restaurant and free sundbeds. Come early to get hold of the ones placed under the palm trees. Well worth a visit if you like to hang out on the beach.
it's a unique place surrounded with spirit of freedom and space.One is likely to feel in a fairy-tale..
Not one of the more attractive beaches around. Lot of watersports going on and not a particularly great view. Not worth the effort to get there.

It's a beautiful and interesting place for nature lovers. Amazing combination of forest and beach. Trees are very close to the seashore.I think it was a much more better in the past but for now unfortunately it's not pristine because of tourists and destruction by human.
Very disappointing  - totally overrated, crowded and felt dirty with all the boats coming in. Sad because it's a unique spot.

We left tangalle to visit Galle on the natural course of heading back to Colombo and we were sad to leave the beach. There is a lot of litter sadly on the beaches around the fort and there are a lot of beaches. So finding this golden Sand beach was brilliant it was busy with all the Sri Lankans on the right side of the beach- partying away playing drums singing and dancing. And all the tourists on the left hand side. There is even a small bar offering chilled drinks and food. You have to get a tuk tuk here and then walk done through the shade of trees. Worth a shout to get away from the fort when you have already walked round it 20 times. There are a few rocks here in the shallow water which are hard to see so be very careful as even I got thrown into them and hurt my leg. Just tread carefully don't let that put you off

From Unawatuna beach were we were staying, we took an early morning hike up the mountains through Yaddehimulla road then through a small walking trail to the tip of the  nose jutting out to the sea (from where  you can get beautiful views of Galle fort) and then down climbing over some rocks into Jungle beach. The bar (Jungle beack disko!) gives refreshing fresh fruit drinks to make your senses come alive. From there a trail goes over a few more rocks to the second part of jungle beach where there are some more small restuarants. There are steps going up from this beach up to the tarred road, from where you can either get a tuk-tuk back to the beach or walk back down by the side of the Japanese pagoda and take the trail to Unawatuna beach.

We went with family to that place. It's was very relax and the surrounding was superb. There is small restaurant with  junk people . Do not trust them they ruin our day . There food portions are really small and prices are higher than a five star hotel. We were spent more than 5000 rs just for the snacks and when we were ready to leave they force us to had lunch . And they were insulting us in front of our relations and kids. Really poor experience ever we got. It is so sad to know, in a such nice peace in Sri Lanka we couldn't enjoy our selfs because of these people . 😂😂😂😂😂😁😁😁

We visited Jungle Beach 15 years ago and then it was an amazing place. We were afraid to go back to spoil our memories, but still decided to go. That was a wrong decision. The small beach was filled with too much people and a small restaurant. But that was not the main problem. The main problem was the garbage, it’s really amazing how they polluted something so nice this way. It looks like a garbage dump. Our opinion: Don’t go until it’s cleaned.

We went to this beach by boat and it was so much crazy and fun.our Guide said this jungle was a very famous among the local as there is a creative story is behind the this Madol doowa. We walked around that and return with the boat again which was so noce

One of the nicest beaches we discovered on the south coast. No waves and the water is clean. There were free beach beds and not crowded, little bar provides refreshing drinks (although the alcoholic ones were more like a parody :)
Popular with the locals and families.  It is a stroll from town (or tuk tuk) Cove beach would be great to watch sunset.  Free beach beds.

At the bottom of a hill with rock stairs. If you're attentive, observe the trees above and you can see monkeys and squirrels The sand is soft. There are sun chairs under leafy green jungle trees. A must visit. The hike back up is great leg work.
This beach is lovely however it is where the locals hang out. Very packed aswell. Be prepared to be surrounded by lots of people.

Very charming small beach! There are no waves on the beach that makes it very comfortable for swimming! Snorkeling is not really interesting there especially comparing with Hikkaduwa. No umbreallas on the beach. There are some sunbeds and several restaurants.
It is adventurous since we had to climb down through the jungle. Not polluted and the waves were calm.

there is very little here apart from a little café/bar,but lovely clear water for swimming,and glass bottom boat trips - not a lot to see though.Try a Lassi - buffalo curd and fresh fruit juice - delicious.
Beautiful is the word to describe this beach. Clean and serene and one if the best beaches in Sri Lanka.

We decided to visit jungle beach and i have to say it was amazing.. The sea was so flat and clear.. Beautiful sand and it wasn't too busy which it was nice but i do understand some comments saying that it was too busy., the beach area is not that big.. We also went to have some food at the bar which we found really good and cheap.. The staff was really friendly and service was quick.. I personally think is worth a visit

We were a bit worried about visiting Jungle Beach after some of the reviews but I am so glad we did. The beach was not crowded, although we took the advice of our tuktuk drivers and came by 10.30 in the morning. We brought along a beach mat and avoided renting the sun loungers, all looked taken in any case. The beach was not polluted at all but there was the occasional smell of diesel when a boat arrived- certainly not enough to worry us. The cage looked good, you could get fried rice and cold drinks etc readily. Behind the cafe looked dodgy, I did not investigate that too much but could have been a bit of a rubbish dump. The tuktuk drivers dropped us at the top and it was an easy walk down (& up again). The snorkeling was great, OK it is not the Maldives but you could see lots of different types of tropical fish really easily. Perfect for kids. Water was calm and safe. I would really recommend having a look. The path is easy to navigate if you don't have mobility issues, and is 5 mins walk, maybe 10 coming up. Well worth it.

Very near Galle, a nice undeveloped beach with just one cafe doing food and drink. Lots of sunbeds to lie on and shade provided by the trees. Not so easy to get to as no bus goes all the way, a tuk tuk from Galle Fort costs us 400 roupees, then a nice walk through the jungle down to the beach. Lots of tourists there, the beach is clean.
This is a beautiful beach but can get very very crowded and that takes away from the beauty of it. Best to get there very early so that you can leave before the crowds flock.

The beach is quite small and most of it taken over by a restaurant leaving only a small patch free. Given the distance traveled to reach here and the walk to get to the beach. I felt rather disappointed and chose not to stay. Perhaps it was the weekend hence it was also quite crowded. But overall it does not feel very special, it is secluded during weekdays I am told. The Japanese Peace Pagoda made the trip worthwhile.
Amaizing beach nit very big. please go in the morning Coz afternoon gets quite hot. Also Japanese pagoda close by. A but of climbing involved. Regards Warren

We came here early morning as we thought we will take some nice pictures, but the beach was not particularly beautiful. Its quite small, full of rubbish and compare to beaches east of Unawatuna, this one can be skipped
a small quiet bay with a bar and beautiful beach. if you have an hour or two and you are around you must stop here for a drink and enjoy the bay. don't forget you snorkeling gear at home :)

I was expecting a bit more from the reviews. Its an OK beach but nothing more. You have to walk down a fairly steep rocky slope and some steps to get to the beach, and once you arrive it is rather small. One half is roped off, the other has some sunbeds and drinks stalls. The sea is OK where it is very shallow but quickly becomes very rocky. I think for snorkeling it is OK but otherwise there are better and easier to get to beaches.
Jungle beach is an amazing and picturesque beach with great view and friendly staff (Raju is one of them). I definitely recommend visiting it while in Unawatuna

Made the short walk from our hotel to the beach, via a very steep path made for mountain goats. The beach was ok, a little smaller than expected.  It had a small bar/restaurant and toilets.  Unfortunately the beach was lit by the rubbish accumulated behind it and in the jungle trail to get there. There are better beaches.

The place is fine. Very packed and you need to go early if you want to have a sun bed. We rented a boat with the idea of going to the coral reef, we spoke with the guy and after negotiate the prices (he wanted 5,000rps per person and we finally agreed 2,500 rpm - be careful with this) we went to the boat and he took us 300m away from the Beck. This means; boat is not needed. The coral in that area after the tsunami is dead and not much fishes to see. The guy got very angry with us when we said we wanted to go back to the beach after 15 min, he insulted us and we got scared. Don't rent snorkeling or scuba diving in the place that is there
Clean water, good for swimming however it might get crowded. There is a nice beach bar just above the beach level.

Jungle beach is without a doubt the coolest and nicest beach I've ever seen. It is so beautiful! Not to crowded, and not too big. But still a place with people and a good beach vibe! The bar and resturant is really nice, descent food for a good price.

A tuk-tuk (price: 500LKR from Galle fort) brought us here. The beach is a bit secluded, but the tuk-tuk driver usually makes his best to bring you as close as possible. The first beach you encounter is very short (maybe not more than 30m wide), there is a bar with restaurant, offering also wooden beach-chair (1000 LKR for 2 hours!!), in an area full of trees. Sea water is quite transparent. If you like snorkeling you can swim along the reef separating the first from the second beach, which is wider and with more space for people unwilling to rent the costly beach-chairs. On the other hand, if you want to get to the second beach via an internal path, passing through the forest and partially on the reef, you will discover unpleasant amount of garbage, confirming the inability of local people in preserving their natural paradise. In any case we spent pleasant hours, snorkeling along the reef, watching colored fishes, albeit the overall water transparent cannot compete with what I saw in Italy (Sardinia and south of Puglia).

Be aware that there are two jungle beaches. There is a smaller one that is 100 meters wide at most, and a much larger one further northeast. The small one has limited space and the water touches the lounge chairs at high tide. There is more space on the larger beach and both beaches have access to food shacks and lounge chairs. You can go to both beaches by foot by walking carefully across the rocks, or you can take a path along a hilly road for a 15 minute walk. To get to jungle beach, you can hire a tuk tuk. The smaller Jungle Beach is located below the Peace Pagoda. In order for the tuk tuks to get there, they will have to take a convoluted path. They wanted 500 rupees for the ride from Unawatuna. An alternative is to walk from Unawatuna through a mostly shaded path. There is some trash floating in the water at the large Jungle Beach due to the way the wind and currents take the floating debris. However, this beach offers calm waves and snorkeling within easy reach from the beach. Visibility is moderate, but there a few interesting sea life to see. It's worth a visit.

Although the popular spot is the well known bathing sea/beach area of Jungle Beach, a little to the south of this if you can take a small walk is a nice rock wall from which you can enjoy a marvelous panoramic view of the sunset. Love to go there again!

We were not very impressed with unawatuna. We felt it was a dumpy area with nothing in it. Shops were very local and beer could only be purchased at restaurants. There was nothing in the town. This beach however seemed to make up for unawatuna shortfalls. It was beautiful in every sense. A small cove and not over crowed. Difficult to find so a tuk tuk is advised. Come early if you need need shaded cover. There are no umbrellas but some trees provide shade. There is one restaurant which is nice as your not hounded by many restauranteurs to dine at theirs. I wouldn't go out of my way to go here but if your in unawatuna make the trip out.its worth it

My boyfriend and I loved this beach. It was very relaxing and picturesque. We had cocktails on the beach, what better way to spend an afternoon. Got a tuk tuk each way for 400 rupees. Tuk tuks are waiting to pick people up. I would recommend getting dropped off at the Peace Pagoda and walking down to Jungle Beach. The dirt road is rough so tuk tuks don't like to go down.

Nice small beach, actually 2 beaches, you can get to one from one side of the hill and to the other(smaller) beach from the side of Pogoda. Both beaches have free sunbeds and small beach bar with ok prices. It was really nice stay, relaxing, nice place for snorkeling, s take your mask, make sure to take sandals or flippers as corals come very close to surface. You can see many monkeys around. It's a dirty on the sides, but you  don't notice this if staying in the middle. So definitely would recommend to visit this place. If you get there from Unawatuna beach, bargain  with tuk-tuk for 400 -300 rupee.

I'm typing this from the beach. The lonely planet said it was worth a visit, so we have. If it wasn't for the fact you have such beautiful coast line near by, you'd find this little spot worthy of a visit. But... Mirissa beach is ten times better. This is a tiny short beach with no horizon to look out at. The water seriously tastes like diesel from the boats and jet ski. It does have a little bar selling food and beer though. So I'll be sinking a few drinks till my 4pm tuk tuk comes to save us.
A proper jungle beach, small with a restaurant. Too many boats, so is not really healthy to swim in. Everything smell like diesel. Otherwise is nice to stay here for a few hours.
Very small beach with some sunbeds and a restaurant/bar. The beach is clean and the water very clear and calm. You can do snorkeling there, there is plenty to see!

Visited just after sunset to check it out, saw a monkey and some crabs. It was really cool. Quite a small beach. Can imagine it being packed during the day. Lots of mosquitoes, but it was at sunset so kind of expected it. Apparently it is a big party center at night time, but we weren't really interested in that.

It was a nice walk up and down the jungle hill to the beach and we appreciated being able to eat and drink something there. But what made it unpleasant was the amount of rubbish. It was washed up all over the place. I went for a walk along the rocks to look around the bay and it was like a dumpster :( Really such a shame. We won't return.

We went here to visit. Its a nice beach, very small and personally abit over crowded for my liking. Snorkelling is good and you can get shade in the café on the beach. However the sunbeds are stacked all pretty much on top of eachother which is a shame, hardly any room or personal space but was well worth the visit!

A great little beach with calm waters (until about 1 p.m.) and a view of the jungle. Mind you, this beach is small although surrounded by little private coves. The water rises in the afternoon and the beach disappears, so get there early guys and grab yourselves a little magic of clean Sri Lankan waters.

We grabbed a tuk tuk from Unawatuna, which took 10 minutes max. The driver drops you as far as he can drive and then it's a 10 minute walk down onto the beach through a bit of jungle. Lovely white sand, turquoise calm waters which was perfect for swimming. A great mornings exertion. Would highly recommend.
Great for a day trip from cool Galle or a walk from the backpacker central of Unawatuna . Small beach with a cafe seving basic food and drinks

Jungle beach is a hidden cove with access via a narrow trail that winds down the hill. The access road is steep but not difficult to navigate. The cove itself had a beach bar with sun beds. It is not a big beach but not a lot of people either. The sea is mild there and not deep.

Extremely popular with locals and visitors alike. Jungle Beach can be reached down a long rough track (unsuitable for anyone with mobility issues) or by boat. There is a small café where food and drink can be obtained. It's possible to take boat trips and there are other water pursuits. On my visit it was incredibly busy and not a place I would want to return to

You need to take a tuk-tuk then walk down the hill to the beach. It's not large and there are no waves. However, it is a great place to spend a relaxing day. You have the choice of hanging out in the sun, or relaxing in the shade. There is a casual beach side cafe for lunch, etc.

Jungle Beach is a very nice place to snorkel and swim in calm water.  We saw a few nice fish and a sea snake there.  Be aware that you will have use stairs on the way to the beach and back and they would be hard to navigate if anyone in your party has mobility problems.  There are showers at the beach, a small restaurant and toilets.  There are no changing rooms per se.  We  had to use the bathrooms which are very small.  We arrived around 9:30 a.m. and the beach chairs were just about all spoken for.  If you want one, get there earlier.  We were there to snorkel, however, so we found a large rock to use as our home base and off we went into the water. It was a nice morning.

This was definitely a gem worth finding.  It requires a walk down some steps.  The beach is clean and the set up with the Jungle Beach cafe is very cool.  Plenty of people on this beach, but very relaxing.  We had beautiful fresh fish for lunch and refreshing drinks.
this is the best place in Unawatuna to have peaceful sea bath while having a beer :) but keep in mind.. It's get more crowded in weekends and local holidays.

I went there midweek so it was not so crowded. Beds are provided by the only food kiosk which serve amazing fress sea food! As it's a bay you can swim with your kids also. You must walk a little trhough the forest to reach the beach but it deserves it!

We went here twice- once in the day to swim and once at night for a party. Both times it was okay, but nothing really special. It's very secluded so nice and peaceful, and a nice setting, but there is only one place to eat/drink so it's pretty expensive. The party was again okay, but nothing to write home about. Worth a day visit if you've got a bike.

Jungle beach itself is very beautiful and in a seluded location (you have to walk through some kind of jungle). However, when we were there in August it was crowded with tourists with sun chairs spread out over most of the beach. The café/bar serves food (nothing special but overpriced) as well as beer and cocktails.

We made the exciting walk through a jungle trail (that had lots of rubbish dumped everywhere) to come down this, little Bay Area. There were drums banging and lots of locals singing. The beach was divided into two sections. One was full of sun loungers, that you have to pay for and no where to lay a towel down. So we passed the rope barrier to where all the local people were sitting. Fine with us. It was a Sunday so lots of families about and lots of men drinking and singing. The beach is full of broken coral and be careful of the rocks, as you enter the sea. But the sea was really nice to swim in. A lot calmer than some of the other beaches. We stayed for about 3 hours until a local drunk main stated to shout abuse at us about being foreign and another started to make kissing noises at me (no I did not have a bikini on). So we packed our stuff and made our way to the other beach. There are two jungle beaches here. You can scramble across the rocks to an even smaller beach or go back up the main road and walk down to it. The other Jungle Beach was tiny and packed so solid of sun loungers, that, again, you have to pay for. No room for a towel to be laid down, either. Packed full of tourists and local men. So we left, disappointed. The Jungle Beach at Welligama is by far the nicest and more natural.

Found this beach through word of mouth and thought I give it a try. Off I went with my goggles and snorkel. I used the tuck tuck from Unawatuna but you still need to walk down a little bumpy pathway to get there. Jungle beach is an amazing little beach with a cafe that's served drinks and some food. They have some goggles and flippers if you don't have your own too. It is very pretty. They offer beach beds and there is a lot of shade if you want it. I got in the water and immediately saw two amazing large fishes. There are lots of fish around the rocks to the right the middle part of the beach is sand and there are less rocks to the right! Don't miss out on this one if you like snorkelling safely! I loved it. I'll be back next year.

Truly heaven!  You walk through a jungle and then there is a path of steps leading down and by the time reach the bottom you open your eyes to this amazing stretch of beach.  All you see is greenery and brilliant clear blue water.  You get Sun beds around and a little restaurant serving food and drink.
Nice walk to the beach, great sandy beach with sunbeds. The food in the bar is delicious. Nice juices snacks and rice meals.

Tucked away from the usual hustle bustle of the unawatuna beach is a jungle beach.
