U may approach it from sea if you take the boats from the unawatuna beach or you can go from the Galle road and walk up a short distance. It's secluded if you go before 9 and late evenings. You need to pay between 800-1200 sRs depending upon the season. Water is calm  and not very deep. It's food for snorkeling and some coral viewing. There are no lifegaurds. The restaurant there lends snorkeling gear for as cheap as 300 sRs. It's a very good place to have a nice swim.

Tricky to get to, it's a bit of a scramble down the hill side, there's a basic restaurant with prices reflecting the isolation. It's small and gets very crowded with noisy groups, frankly it's really only worth going to, in my view, for a bit of variety from the main beach at Unawatuna. (though the sea can be a bit more enticing if the main beach is dirty, usually after Poya day).
A very nice (and small) beach near the forrest, with monkeys and great opportunity to see nice fishes, and have a snack in the beach bar.

This beach is located amid of the jungle but having a small restaurant offering snacks and lunch as well as basic infrastructure. The water is very calm without any strong currents but offering excellent snorkelling opportunity.

I`ve been to Jungle beach two years ago and it was kinda awesome - quiet, no deck chairs, no music, brilliant. So being in Sri Lanka now again I went there. Soooo disappointed!!! Like you suddenly appear near the swimming-pool hotel. Overcrowded, all the beach is covered with the dozens of deck chairs, the cafe with overpriced menu, loud music, loud tourists. So I left the beach a couple minutes later. I`ve never thought I`ll say it but the main beach in touristic Unawatuna is much pleasant, really
Nice for one day visit. It is quite different from other Sri Lanka beaches. It looks more like Thailand beaches. It is pretty small and can be crowded.
Got to jungle beach and surprised how small this place is. Beautiful beach though, clear water and only one place to eat which didnt feel that clean so was reluctant to order food here.
Loved this little beach! So chill and jungle-esque! Monkeys greeted us on our way down and back from the beach. Perfect if u want a peaceful beach day!

I was here with my gf and our son. Although I have been here before the place has improved a lot. Staff is friendly the charges prices are average. All in all a nice place we will be certainly back again.

I am a big fan of Jungle Beach. It's a smaller, more difficult-to-find, private version of Unawatuna bay. The only downside is that it's often very crowded, which sometimes ruins the feeling that you're on your own private island. It's a small walk/ trek down to the beach, but once you've arrived there is a restaurant and a lot of places to lounge by the beach.

We went on a Sunday and it was VERY crowded (90% locals). We didn't even go into the water and just had a drink instead in the beach bar. If less people had been there, the beach would be alright, but Dalawella or Unawatuna beach are much nicer.
Nice beautiful beach. Involves some trekking to reach the beach but worth the effort. It is very clean and there are small water sports options as well around the beach.

VIEW, ENVIRONMENT, FREEDOM, ENJOYMENT. 1OO/100 GUARANTEE you will get in this place. BUT............ Hospitality, freedom, Enjoyment you don't expect on week ends and long holidays. No place to sit even (reserved for foreigners). Thugs and 3rd class people running the business NO POLITENESS at all (specially man in the fruit stall). Note to the owner of Jungle beach restaurant. 1.Give uniforms to your staff. 2.Produce a price list. 3.Teach them how to treat customers to get more & more business.

Highly recommend a visit to this off the beaten track beach. Beds to lie on with umbrellas, great beach. Nice restaurant, I just got veg fried rice to be safe as it is a bit of a pop up restaurant. Handy to have cool drinks close by though

this is a one of most popular beach in Galle Sri Lanka it really nice and located from remote areas of galle town. very narrow road careful driving will be critical. actually you can find to beaches but different sizes 1st one is small bu you can find a hut which save food and alcohol other one is big it has no shop and less people if you drive to the end of the road , you have to stop vehicle near the temple and you have o work like 200m to reach small beach. other beach entrance is located in the middle of the road , you have to stop your vehicle near small security point you have to work down. two beaches are completely  isolated with each other  and if you want to go to next beach you have to go from road or have to difficult path which has big size rock blocks. this road is short but difficult to to go. But i have seen people coming from this road. nice beach
It was a hot day in Galle and the Jungle Beach was the coolest spot around, with a lovely breeze coming off the water.

It was the loudest beach ever in Sri Lanka. Rubbish everywhere. Many people in a small area. We were there at the  weekend  and  many locals also were there. Swimming with them was enjoying but we had to leave the water after some started to wash their body, clean their ears and throats in the water.
Was hard to get there but worth the hassle.  small beach with nice surroundings. loads of Russians haha.big fan

We we dropped of at Small Jungle Beach by the Tuk Tuk driver and decided to stay for the day and go to the 'real' JB another day. Well, SJB was really nice for an afternoon sunbathing and swimming in calm safe waters. Fairly good for snorkeling too. A very basic restaurant shack on the beach serving really good cocktails! Great fresh fish for an ok price too. It does get busy but not too over crowded. The next day we went to the 'real' Jungle Beach, it was ok but much smaller and crowded. We walked along the overgrown coastal path, back around to SJB!
TukTuk driver would not, understandably, take us right down a steep rough track. The approach to the beach is only for people who are fit and nimble on their feet - we are neither so gave up.

Was reading about this place from many places. Decided to go one afternoon. The way leading to this beach was pretty bad with lots of trash. Took some time to reach there and once there found the place really over priced. Just regret goin there.

While Unawatuna beach is squeaky clean, Jungle beach has too much rubbish laying around (not usual for Sri Lanka...) This might be the results of wild parties happening at night, but unless you are a party animal (too drunk to notice...) it looks bad and stinks. What a pity!

Its nearly 3.5 km distance from the Unawatuna Beach, a drive uphill, better to switch on your GPS for exact location. A little trek inside the jungle leading to beach. Small secluded beach, not crowded at all, however the beach is very rocky and water is not really clean, v coarse sand. Can be visited only to tick off a beach off your to do list.
One of my best spots close Unawatuna if you want to avoid busy long beaches and quite touristic Before Jungle beach its nice to go down from a path and at White Jungle Beach

A very pretty little cove, but we went in the evening for a party and it was very expensive, much more than neighbouring Unawatuna and that's already not cheap! The view was pretty and it wasn't packed which was a bonus, but drinks and entry cost way too much for what it was.
We read about this 'fantastic' beach...but what a disappointment! It was a trash dump....Lots of garbage all over!

Worth the walk there and back if you are a walker and there is a pleasant restaurant for a drink and something to eat if you want (didn't sample the food).  The beach is small and uninteresting and far too busy for us to want to stay.

Too many people on a small stretch of sand. Lots of music and also a restaurant, again on a small stretch. Boats starting their smelly engine while people are swimming close by. The walk from the main beach to the Jungle beach is nice though.

Visited Jungle Beach last week. Loved the main beach at Unawatuna so much that we weren't sure we would get to Jungle Beach but so glad we went. The walk there was beautiful and the beach stunning. We went late morning and still plenty of banana lounges around. Pack some snorkels too!
This little beach is definitely beautiful but it was absolutely jammed packed! Hardly room to move! My husband & I left after about 2 minutes!
Quiet and nice. Access by foot via unawatuna beach takes 15/20min and is nice. Not for strollers. Can go with tuktuk. Decent restaurant on the beach at fair prices.

Enjoyed our morning down on the beach. Wasn't too crowded. There was some locals down there drumming which was nice to listen to while relaxing. Recommend trying the seafood fried rice at the little restaurant on the beach. It was delicious!

Getting here was straight forward, we came with rented scooters. There is a short down hill walk from the parking area. The beach is clean and nice. There is a small restaurant, shower, bathroom at the beach. There is shade. Bring a snorkel if you have one, there are some fish around that could be worth a look. The only negative was that there were a few glass bottom boat guys on the water and they were stinking up the air with their old motors running.
Nice bay close to Galle.  Crowded and only wooden beds.  The beach was ok, But small. A bit of a climb to get there.  Nothing for people with walking problems.
The beach is awesome with a lot of tourists. The sand is clean and white and water also is very clean. A place one needs to visit.....

We were advised to go here as it is a hidden treasure. Unfortunately the treasure has been discovered by far too many people. It was unpleasantly crowded. We tried snorkling, but nothing to see. Best part was the food and drinks from the local "restaurant". Very reasonably priced and huge portiones, and very very tasty. Avoid loking into kitchen and toilets though.

If you like lots of Russians in a small confined space this beach is the place for you. Russians come down and take over the majority of the sunbeds whilsr drinking beer in their speedos and overhanging guts. So if you like that sorta thing then this is a great place to visit. The beach itself is average but a nice walk to get there from Unawatuna beach

Difficult to get to, but it is a good adventure. The beach though is quite small, and feels commercial. It is also crowded, and we did encounter groups of men who catcalled the young women in our group making us feel unsafe.
We walked down from our hotel. Not the easiest walk with younger children. As all beaches on a Sunday it was very busy with mostly locals. It is a beautiful area but slightly over hyped.

We forgot it was Independence Day; but for the very tired party goers who were on the beach til 04.30 we were blissfully unaware why the place was packed. Music in familial groups; young and old playing games and having fun in the sea and sun, food from the restaurant or picnics from home; this was the best way one could hope to enjoy Independence Day.

It's just a regular beach. Nothing special. We stayed in Hikkaduwa and our friend advised us to go to Jungle Beach. They described it as magical jungle beach. But in reality...no thing special. Don't know what people like here.

Got the tip about the jungle beach form the locals so we knew we had to go and check it out. Great beach a little bit away from the tourist trail, not as much waves and great water for snorkelling. I visited Sri Lanka with my fiancé and this beach had something for us both, great sunspot for her sun worship and crystal clear water for my free diving. Lets not leave out the fresh juices, passion fruit recommended, and them moorish coctails...
Few sunbeds. Nice surroundings. Rocky water. Swim between the markers to avoid hitting big rocks on the seabed

its hardly any distance from unawatuna beach.. lots of tuk tuk to ferry u  , u can also hike up to the beach its about 2 km by walk.. the place is happening on wednesday night with drinks, party , music till dawn, the service fro drinks is slow when the places is crowed . ideally reaach the beach at around 10.30 night for party... or if u wanna enjoy the beach go there morning.. altough in the morning the place does get a little dirty ... go with froends, go as couples for the party to enjoy the place.. wednesday night is not to be missed.

The beach itself is ok, there is some sunbeds which are free to use if you buy a drink or two from tje restaurant, but its pretty crowded with other tourists. Going into the water can be harsh since alot of big and small rocks + coral is all over the place which easily can hurt if not very careful. The biggest problem however is all the trash along the upper "beachline", without this it would be a beautiful place, but this ruins the whole thing, it takes away all the charm as it seems no one is cleaning it up. Wijaya beach is better in all aspects and the same price from Unawatuna by tuctuc!
It is around 1,5 km far by walk from Unawatuna beach. Tuk tuk is quiet expensive. Towards to the beach we had a very good wild coconut.

Much better beaches in Sri Lanka. Drinks service was so slow we left. The snorkeling wasn't up to much more than dead coral. We were there on a Sunday and it was packed. Perhaps mid week it would be nice.

There are two of them. I liked White Jungle beach best of all. Very good warm little waves and good little cafe with Sri Lanka tasty food. The only thing that I dislike is that people smoke there a lot right close to everyone but that is a matter of regulations and peoples breeding
Nice beach surrounded by jungle with a small café. I walked there from Unawatuna on my own and got hassled by some local lads en route which was not nice - maybe better to go with others.

Fro my view I prefer the second bigger part of then jungle beach which you access from the main road. Anyway it's not far and you can swim between these two. Nice for hanging out with shadow places and for snorkelling!

I hidden, not easy to get too, yet sometimes crowded beach.  We went on a religious holiday so there were a lot of people there.  It's a small cove with a nice beach, beach chairs, some rocks and a snack shack.  Nice way to spend an afternoon.  Plenty of trees around to find some shade it you get too hot. We walked from Unawatuna beach. The walk is an adventure in inself.  It takes about 30 minutes and you'll meet some interesting people along the way.
It is difficult to get to but it is just another small sandy beach at the base of a hill on the point and the best view is from the hotel on the opposite peninsula closer into town

Much touted 'secluded' beach 30 minutes' walk from Unawatuna, but actually it's also accessible by road so it's to be avoided in the season and at weekends.  Beachside cafes are proliferating.  It was crowded with both local and foreign tourists when I went.  Quite pretty stretch of sand but nothing special, and the view across the bay to Galle town is nothing to write home about.
We went on a Sunday and there were way too many people for us to enjoy the beach in peace. You can hike there from unawatuna, its a short 30 min hike from the north part.

For those who visit jungle beach, the beach is beautiful! Their are two little bays. The first one closest to galle is the most beautiful one. Go their for a swim but DONT have lunch there! The people are super unfriendly, the food is way overpriced, we had to wait for 2h!!! And they won't give a special price to the locals which is super unfair! It was the first time in Sri Lanka that we met such unmannered and impolite people.

Tiny beach, a lot of Russian, which is not a plus, one tiny bar, difficult to go into the water, dirty beach, it supposed to be a good place but was obviously spoiled by a lot of tourists and poor care by locals

We recently snorkelled in Polhena and Mirissa, Jungle beach in Unawatuna is by far the best we've seen yet. Don't bother going with an expensive boat, we hired gear from Submarine Diving in Unawatuna for 300 rupees an hour. 2 hours is more then enough. Swim as far round to the left as you can, the reef is plentiful and there's so many beautiful fish. Enjoy!

Expect a popular beach in a nice environment rather than a secluded beach as the name or the tourist guides might suggest. What I loved was the walk from Unawatuna to the Jungle Beach, which is not difficult at all even with a young child. Besides, you get lots of shade, plus great views once you are close to the beach or the Pagoda (there are several possible roads when you get near). The beach itself is small and generally crowded. Too many sunbeds for such a small beach, but without them it would be pretty impossible to lie in the sun after 11 o'clock or noon, as the water almost washes the whole beach in the afternoon. The water is fine and you can spot big fish even without scuba diving equipment. Galle and its Lighthouse are visible in the distance. After visiting the Peace Pagoda, the way back to Unawatuna was a bit tricky (no proper signs), but we did fine with the help of a local teenager who showed us a shortcut.

We only spent a day over at jungle beach driving over from midigama. We took the boards and had some fun waves in the bay to the left of jungle beach. It is a good beach for everyone with a bit of surf (the locals swear by it) as well as being good for sun baking and swimming. Wish we stayed but seeing the whole coast is so close together it's hard to go everywhere.

We took a tuk tuk from Galle fort to Jungle Beach (600 rupees each way) on a Saturday afternoon that was also a poya day (Buddhist holiday). The beach and small foreshore area under the trees were packed with local families picnicking and playing. It was very busy but a nice scene to see. My 19 year old son joined a frenetic soccer game on the sand. But the water smelled a lot of boat fuel and was not pleasant for swimming. The little restaurant was popular and we bought drinks from it (felt a bit obliged in order to use a wooden beach bed).. So all in all it is a pretty little sandy beach with trees around but it would be best on a quiet day without lots of boats and people.
Good small beach, restaurant. Steep slippery walk to access, so not suitable for unfit. Worth it when you get there.
About a 2 kilometre walk from Unawatuna is jungle beach, small but lovely and the sea is so warm and inviting, nice little restaurant too

You have to trek to reach this beach. It's near the peace pagoda. It's supposed to be quite and decoded but when we went it was very crowded due to Christmas holidays. Otherwise a nice beach to relax. They have sun beds and changing rooms as well on the beach

Most definitely this has to be the best beach in Sri Lanka. Its a calm waveless beach although there were slight waves occasionally. Its in a beautiful location flocked with tourists having a good time

All night beach party on jungle beach. Was great music was not quiet my scene all the time but atmosphere was really chilled and friendly. Locals have to pay to go unless accompanied by a tourist . Evens there were a number of locals at the party too. Don't be fooled into taking tuktuk long way round. From unawatuna beach it is only a few km to get there .

Me and my Husband heard about Jungle beach from others and also from our lonely planet guide book so we decided to go there. It's a beautiful beach ! It's a good 1km walk down quite steep stepping stones . On the way there's a few spots for some good views!
Great beach crystal clear water, nice place to chill around and for a swim. Got a nice a bar and restaurant around. One beautiful place you shouldn't miss if you are around Unawatuna.

Small crowded beach, nice food. Snorkelling is average, life and some corals, but the visibility was not so good. Good for swimming, suitable for children. White beach around the corner is less crowded, but a lot of garbage washes up here.
Beautiful but very busy beach, a short tuk tuk ride from Unawatuna and then a steep short walk down an uneven path to the beach.
Great place to chill and for a dip in the sea. Would come a 100 more times with more people. Wish it was a bit better maintained.
We went To jungle beach. The beach is very small, packed with locals en russian people. Only the walk towards the beach is Nice. No must seeing... Nothing special..

We walked to jungle beach from Unawatuna beach (which takes about 30 minutes). It certainly is a pretty setting and the sea appeared calmer, but every sun bed was taken and there was no other space on the sand to lie down. There are toilets, showers and a restaurant, so I imagine if you visit at the right time and get a bed it would be a nice spot, although you will be very close to other beds. After one visit I prefer the space on Unawatuna beach.

Had a great couple of hours at jungle beach club, only visited as a last minute suggestion from the tuk tuk man, however as Unawatuna is pretty relaxed we wanted a place with atmosphere and music and this is exactly what we received. We only stayed until 130am but worth a trip every Wednesday, the music is turned down when the police come but still at a good volume. Be Careful a couple of things tuk tuk drivers will try ripping you off and charging up to 1000 rupees especially return, we paid 500 which was still over the odds. Drinks are a little higher in price but not much, however if you smoke the prices are double for cigarettes

After spending a few days on the beach down in beautiful Mirissa, I wasn't expecting too much from this place. What I got was a beautiful little beach, great for swimming, an awesome view of the fort and harbour. We got to the beach at about 11.30 in the morning and it was quite busy but we managed to grab quite a large patch of beach for ourselves and later on a couple of sun loungers became free. There were quite a few families with small children as the sea is very calm here. We'll be back!!
a lovely small beech with a bar that serves quality value for money food very picturesque and relaxing sea and beech lovely had a wonderful day here

We have been around the coast of Sri Lanka and in our opinion this is the best beach! We went here a few times and in the week when there are less people it's simply stunning. Clear calm waters (often fair for SL), soft sand and shack with friendly staff.
Pretty beach but absolutely packed the day we were there. Good to have a public toilet block. It would be lovely to have the beach to yourself but I don't think this would ever happen.m

Beach is a beautiful place filled with local next foreigners. Foreigners would come here a lot but I would not try to recommend during monsoon season, because sea waves are quite strong and waves has the potential to drag you to the ocean because of the ocean current. Moreover, it's horrible to visit when it's raining
Lovely restaurant great choices of fresh food & super menu for all tastes it's wonderful  and I'll be back regularly to enjoy this little jem of a Beach with very helpful happy staff

Coming from Unawatuna beach proper its quite a hike of about 30 minutes over the hill and down the other side.  A few industrious Sri Lankans have juice bars along the way to syop if you need a drink.  Great views of the pnding surf along the walk too.  Once you ge to the beach below a Temple you will find it small full of locals and a busy bar resto.  Cash only.  Nice place to swim but its really too crowded to find a place to set up and relax.  Maybe go real early or real late.  Looks across the bay to Galle Fort so has a nice outlook.  Another way to get to this spot is by boat for snorkelling in the relatively calm waters.

Excellent beach for kids, nice entrance to water, so a lot of space to swim and play. Great natural shade under the trees,  which was the key for us. You can watch and feed monkeys when you go down or up. Note: not wheelchair/or stroller  acceasily. Sadly, there's a lot of garbage in the hidden places of the beach,  but that's an overall impression of Sri Lanka,  unfortunately.
Secluded bay with 1 restaurant. Beautifull ocean and small. Little jungle trail leads to it. Different to unawatuna touristy beach
Nicest beach in the surrounding area. Sea is a lot more calm, a nice place to go and relax for the day.

Drive up the Rumasala Hill and then take a 10min trek through some light jungle with little monkeys watching you.....to the beach which is quit nice and less populated than Unawatuna which is quite close too..... there is one place to eat and drink .....so that is good in a way.....Ideal picnic or evening time romantic spot....great location for photography too....

I been to the beach at 30-December. this is a well maintain beach with lots of facilities. The beach have two part with separate entry. at the 30-December, the beach organized a beach party to celebrate the new year. From the Jungle beach you can enjoy a wonderful sunset.

Whilst looking for hotels that accept our well travelled dog we chanced upon this gem of a place but didn't stay.  It looked closed when we visited, being a weekday and not a particularly busy period.  Good for travellers who want seclusion as it is a real hideaway!
This beach was a wonderful time for a day party, it had a fun crowd and has a big bar with a great atmosphere.  The food was delicious too.

Beautiful place with very clean water for swimming or snorkelling. Nice little place to eat and have a few Lion beers, which was a pleasant surprise! The only thing I thought was strange was that it seemed that the locals were on one side of the beach and the tourists on the other side. Would be nice in future to not have that segregation! In conclusion, a beautiful place to visit with a great view of Galle Fort! Don't miss this place and don't forget your camera!!
Way to jungle beach is also felt good . beautiful place.beach is also clean.only bad thing is there is only one shop.beach is not ruff.
Walk for a few minutes down a hill through a Jungle to reach an intimate, idilic beach with a small bar and lapping waves. We arrived just before sunset and had a very relaxing float in the sea.
Go there early in the morning, when it is not busy and you will not regret it! It is good for snorkelling and relax.
Nice place  but too many people,prices in bar bit higher then in Unawatuna good place to spend no more then few houres
Went to jungle beach on basis of past reviews , had a good time , ok beach with a nice view , pl. be carefull of the rocks on white jungle beach side in the water

We stayed at the nearby Cantalouple Levels hotel so this was a short walk and came highly recommended. I found the beach pretty average with quite a bit of rubbish both on the beach and in the water. There were several groups of men getting their drink on and playing drums and singing which was more worthy of the walk down. They weren't aggressive or inappropriate, just there having a bit of fun and keeping to themselves. Apparently this is common.

went to the jungle beach thinking there would be water sports and activities but it was a small bay with a dirty cafe and old wooden sun beds, not what we were expecting, disappointed and a waste of time

We took a walking trip to this hidden beach while staving in Unawatuna. It was a bit further than we thought it would be, but a Great experience anyway. The staff at the restaurant at the beach were friendly and fun. Thanks guys :-) The beach was a bit crowded, but it was fun experience this beach and also have a little exercise while on vacation 😊
In fact it consists of two parts and there are two passes which leads to that places. The one part was really crowded, so we went further, through the rocks and there was much more better

Its still not crowded like a lot of the other beaches in the south of Sri Lanka, in the Galle area. So the time to visit is now - perfect for families with little ones, as the waves are gradual and the sea bed gradient is gentle. You can wade in to the water for a hundred meters and still be on terra firma. There is a lovely little shack by the beach that serves chilled beer and cocktails, and some nice sea food fare. Must do if you are in the area. We spent an entire day on 31st Dec, and just loved the beach - not too crowded, but enough to feel the beach-life vibe.

Lovely cove. Nice warm clean water & a family beach. We were lucky enough to be there for a Bollywood style production being filmed. There is a small bar and restaurant there. It's great fun.. Note then the rain poured down on us tropical style & so we took cover in the restaurant. While others still played on the beach
Jungle beach is nice... and always crowded... but if u go White Jungle beach u have it a bit more calm and decent... aand u have white sand :))
Nice beach with a little restaurant. Good for swimming, no big waves. But it's not so easy to reach...a little hike down the hill.

The sea here is so calm and tranquil. It's a great place to snorkel, or just float about in. Definitely no waves here and there are places to sun bathe. There is a lovely little restaurant with good food and friendly service. The cocktails do take a little while to arrive, but they were good. We also attended a party here one night. It was ok, the music was a little too heavy for us but the location was great!
Visited jungle beach during our stay in Unawatuna. The beach is a bit crowded and the sun beds made of wood without cushions, so incredible hard. The sea is calm making swimming pleasant.

Wednesday nights is party till dawn at this scenic little beach. Any tuk tuk driver is happy to bring you there in a ten minutes ride. And if he is young he will certainly join you to the party and and won't charge you the fare. Yes, and do bring the young staff of your stay with you, they really will appreciate that. They are bored because in Galle Fort there is nothing for the youngsters to go out and have fun. Accompanied with a foreigner the local people avoid the steep entrance cover of 2000 rupees. Foreigners get in free.

We were told about this party by the locals and it being a Wednesday, there literally wasn't much to do either ways. The approach to Jungle Beach is tricky so if your took took or taxi says, they don't know the place... I will recommend you take another one. You do have to walk the last street because its non motor able. Once you are there, its a trance party with fireworks on the beach etc. Mind you, they only serve basic spirits and beer. No wine or anything fancy so don't expect the same. Toilets are dirty so don't complaint because their's no one to respond to. Go on Wednesday for a few hours around midnight if you want to hear good music and dance with likeminded people.

A lovely place for a day out. The food in the cafe was fresh and excellent - one of the best 'on the beach' meals we ate at in Sri Lanka. The waters were much calmer than the rather choppy Umawatuna, and were shallower too - perfect for our young kids to splash and paddle in. Our day trip here is a must for any families staying in the area.
This is a place where you can relax and just near it by walk for 5 minutes there is anothe nice beach.

You can find the place in Google Maps, Jungle Beach, and White Sand Beach is located in the same road, The most awesome beach you could ever find in Unawatuna area. Jungle beach is having a medium size restaurant where you can take you meals and drinks, but the quality and tasty is not there yet. Also the White Sand beach having a very small join, I think you can have meals or drinks from there too. Both of these places are less crowded. You need go down nearly Kilometer through the middle of the jungle kind of area to by foot to access white sand beach, but believe me it's well worth. Jungle beach in the other hand is easier to access.

The way to the beach has a great flair. The beach itself is beautiful. It's just a pity that the Beach is such a mess with much trash in the water. During our stay many locals have been there which was quite entertaining. Unfortunately nobody cares if some people throw trash in the water during daylight...

I visit this place on regular interval to have a sea bath and to relax myself to get away from the urban life. Staff of the tuck-shop is friendly, provides fresh juice and other food items. It evidences that Jungle beach is one of the pristine beaches in southern part of Sri Lanka.

This is one of the most beautiful beaches I've ever seen in Sri Lanka.The colour of the sea is a bit turquoise and the atmosphere is cool. We could take very nice photos with panoramic backgrounds thanks to the surrounding rocks and trees.There were more tourists than locals and everybody seemed to be benefiting from the unspoilt natural beauty which this place is enriched with.Highly recommend.Ideal for sea bathing as well.

It is just a small beach in a cove - extremely crowded and fairly unexciting. Even if it was completely uninhabited it wouldn't be particularly interesting. The views over to Galle aren't great as it is the industrial part of the town/

We had heard of Jungle Beach and were staying close by so decided to go and have a look. We walked about 30 min each way. The walk was interesting with some great views and a bit of wildlife along the way. Once we got to the beach we were happy there was a cafe there to get a drink. The beach was nice with great views across to Galle but no better than many other beaches we have visited.

Legend has it that hanuman got the mountain of sanjivani buti and places it here. Hence d jungle and herbal plants are very similar to the ones found in d himalayas.... good beach and has the famous japanese peace pagoda nearby...

The beach is a small beautiful beach, but nothing compared to Unawatuna beach. Unfortunately there are a myriad of tourists, almost impossible to lay down or to relax. It is in other words not worth visiting.

We got here on a lightly cloudy week day, and it was packed with tourists! Nothing wrong of course,but the beach isn't big, and the water can get pretty crowded. Apart from this, its really a cozy and cool place, worth a visit, and with the heat, worth a swim!

We decided to walk to jungle beach from our hotel in Unawatuna, I wish we hadn't bothered. We hiked up what seemed like a couple of never ending hills, then through bushes, a stream, overgrown trees then bolders and rocks. It was an overcast but humid day and about half way in I thought, no way can the beach be at the end of this. I understand why people either drive or get a boat here as it is pretty inaccessable. As we had climbed and clawed our way through the forest/jungle in flip flops and summer dress, oh dear we were not about to give up now. We arrived at the beach, what beach? There was a restaurant which took most of the flat land before the beach, then a rocky cove with not much sand and lots of people. It was a Sunday so loads of locals and tourists enjoying the sun and shallow water. If the beach had been deserted it still would have been a let down as there is hardly any sand to walk along. The water was shallow but way too many people there to enjoy. The walk back through the jungle was a lot more enjoyable than the beach itself as it was great to say hello to all the friendly locals and see their homes.

We visited the Jungle Beach on a Wednesday night during the weekly party. The beach is nice, a private corner that can be greatly enjoyed during the day and at night for some drinks. Food and drinks are available for a quite reasonable price. Unfortunately you have to walk in a quite sloped and slippery path to reach the beach.

Beach is nice,view is superb. There are long chairs that we can use if any are free. The water was not clear near the beach but we swan 250-300 meters away and we saw nice fishes of all colours. I had a devilled prawn plate with rice and a beer for 1000r (10 cad$), very good and cheap. My girl friend had a chicken fried rice which was tasty. Staff is nice too. I will go back tomorrow! Recommended! Warning: you have to walk down a dirt road to get there. And walk up again. Also, visit the japanese pagoda temple on the way. It is superb!

There are actually two parts to this beach. One is the Jungle Beach, the other is the White Jungle Beach which is about twice the size of Jungle beach but still quite small. Both parts are very private and have little restaurants serving good food at decent prices. Both are very picturesque, clear blue water and golden sand. If you are in to night life, check these beaches out. We went to a beach party on Jungle Beach which occurs every Wednesday evening that was great fun.

This is a very picturesque isolated bay / beach however the beach is only about 40 meters long and was packed with like minded people seeking a quiet beach. We walked there from Unawatuna beach and after rain it is a bit treacherous, muddy and hilly.

The water is calm and it is ideal to swim in. There is a bit of coral, quite close to the shore, so it is a nice spot to snorkel. It involves a little drive and a very short walk, but because of that, it doesn't get too crowded as people tend to stick to Unawatuna. Can see Galle Fort is the distance.
Good pristine beach with lots of water sports option.. lovely place...it was very near to our hotel n great place to hang out in the day...
the best way to come is by boat. the beach is very very small and crowded during the week ends. it could be good for small children but the road is too curved

Very crowded and not that clean. Managed to get a shady spot and had a nice swim, but looking out to the factory across the harbour wasn't too inviting. Watch out for the tuktuk drivers at the top of the path, we got suspiciously short changed... Won't go back.
Nice beach with fabulouse view on Galle Fort. On Wednesday evening there is a party with nice music. Cheap but good food.

Lots of rubbish at one end of the beach. Plastic bags in the sea. The diving was just ok and really not that great at all even tho there were dish to see. On the upside it was very calm there and good for swimming. It's a bit of a hike down the hill and again back up. We didnt go back.

Good things dont come easy. Its true with the Jungle Beach as well. The trek through the woods and down the hill made me a bit apprehensive (walking down a jungle in a foreign land gets you a little worried, especially when its just your spouse and a 5 year old with you)...but the moment you descend through the hills, you get to heaven!!! Yes, the Jungle beach restaurant is like a heavenly discovery - a shack on white sands not reachable by roads....its like being on a private beach!! The food is ok (wasnt very impressed, but then maybe its because I am used to hot and spicy stuff in India)...but this place ....you can spend the entire day just doing nothing!! YOU MUST DO THIS PLACE IF IN UNAWATUNA....DO NOT MISS THIS FOR ANYTHING!!

We stayed at Coco Bay, which is located along the road that leads to the Japanese Pagoda and Jungle Beach. It is a good walk up the hill and down through a forest path to the beach. It is a pretty beach but during the weekend and over special Buddha festivals it is full with locals (mainly men) who like to drink and litter. It is a real shame that in this beautiful part of the world you are surrounded by litter.

It's about a 20 minute up hill walking from Unawatuna. The road changes from tarmac to a dirt path and then a rocky path and then stepping stones across a stream, all perfectly navigateable in flip flops, just. The beach itself was packed and busy. Not a spare inch when arriving midmorning. Setting up in the cafe was the only space left. The cafe staff were friendly but busy running around after the countless beach goers. It was a little slow. But free WiFi in the middle of nowhere is a plus. The beach itself was small. Get their early if you intend to visit. The island did protect from the prevailing breeze so no jelly fish or big waves. Plenty of people taking tourist shots of their partners in the surf which amused the locals no end. I'll give the place a miss next time I'm in town.

The beach is nice and you can pick a few good pics, but is rapidly becoming crowded because it is simply small. There is a bar where you can eat and drink at good conditions. If you are OK with crowd, a good choice.
We only went for a short while but it is easily one of the nicest beaches I have been to. Quiet and a bit out of the way. Clear water and stunning views

Really cool pathway, blue water, but maybe better to avoid on the weekends, massive sausage fest when we went there. Worth going for an afternoon or evening, but the japanese pagoda next door is truly worth it

The Jungle beach was one of the beautiful beaches in down south which was cover by a jungle. This place is a must visit to a traveler who visit Unawatuna. I had an adventurous hiking with my 5 year old son to jungle beach which he enjoyed to the maximum. You get a great feeling when you walk on that rough-stony-muddy road.

Plus points.... nice clean beach with calm water, great for swimming, nice drive to get there with some incredible views. Negative points.... Not a very big beach so can get busy quickly. Other points.... Not very accessible for those who struggle walking.

The Jungle beach was one of the beautiful beaches in down south earlier. However now its wasted by the people who visit the place. They never wanted to protect this wonderful place. Still this place is a must visit to a traveller who visit Galle.

We went here with our 9 month old baby. The water is good for swimming with children. Not so high waves and the beach is good since there is a lot of shade. It is absolutely a place to go to if you think other beaches further east is to far off. It's quite a walk and you will need to carry a small child since it's hard to walk. It's not accessible with a trolley. There are a lot nicer beaches and we don't really understand the hype around jungle beach. There are a lot if dogs wondering around... (as everywhere in SiriLanka) ...but this is not great with small children that want to play with the dogs. The water is not clean. Plastic and other garbage is floating around. The restaurant is a bit "rustic" for my taste...didn't feel so clean. We had lunch but I didn't dare to take anything that hadn't been heated. My husband thought it was fine! (I might be a bit sensitive)

The jungle is there though is not as pristine and unknown as it was a few years ago. It's still a must visit place if you stay around Unawatuna or Galle. Quite good place for snorkeling, nice and accesible bar on the beach. Lots of animals and fruit trees around. We've seen many monkeys, monitors, iguanas, all kinds of birds ;)

A secret patch of beach with calm water, Jungle Beach reminds you a little of Blue Lagoon. Opt to walk your way through Unawatuna for breathtaking views, as opposed to taking the tuk-tuk. The water here is calm and perfect for swimming. We stuck to one area, but there are a couple of stretches in this secluded spot. Jungle Beach is best enjoyed with fewer people around as it tends to get crowded and noise beating the purpose of isolation. Nonetheless, this place is a must visit just for the views.

We thought it would be a nice quiet place to go and enjoy so some sun, like many beaches we've visited in Sri Lanka, but it was far busier. A nice spot, and the snorkeling around the rocks at the north of the beach was good.

We went to the beach in the morning before lunchtime. It's very goods since it often rains in the afternoon. We went back to Unawatuna to have lunch. Ordered great fruit drinks and milkshakes in the cafe.
Great little beach with fabulous sand. Get there before 11 am to get a sunbed in the shade. Great little restaurant on the beach. Quiet, clean beach with great swimming
walkway to jungle beach, great feeling when you walk on that rough-stony-muddy road... bike can go to 2nd level if you have... dont go when its raining... closes little early in the evening...
Nicer than the main Unawatuna beach but got too busy later in the day. Walking there is nice if a bit sweaty!

Actually jungle beach is the name of the open restaurant so they have put sign of jungle beach.  The path going towards this restaurant which has an open beach is between forest like area.  Beware of the stray dogs over there.  They come to close for comfort to the kids.  Be with kids at all times in this area due to stray dogs.  Nice beach.  In case you are not travelling to any other places to Hikkaduwa you can carry your beachwear and enjoy this small beach which has good sand.  Saw a white crab of the size of spider on this beach.

The beach is accessible through a walk way created in the jungle and hence the name.  The beach is not huge but clean.  We went there in the morning for a short time and let our toddler play in the sand.

Very lovely and calm beach. You need to walk a little bit to get there but when you reach it there it is. A small beach made of two parts. It is very idilic and there is a nice restaurant with great staff and very friendly owner. Prices are reasonable and nature is stunning.

Lovely beach. Very idyllic. Saw a moray eel while snorkelling and many fish. A bit of litter has washed up and is in a pile to the back but other than that it is a clean beach. Played volleyball with some monls which was an experience!
The beach was nice and the way to it was beautiful. But its a tiny beach n crowded for that matter... With drunk singing men.
Very nice beach, the trip from Unawatuna costs 350 r. The restaurant offers food and drinks at a reasonable price.
It's a nice place though a hush climbing.. Very calm place and gives you a very native island experience. Nice beach....
Dirty water. Very crowded ( we had the impression that we were beamed to Moscow), we left the location after a short swimming without eating or drinking. Not that what we expected.
Half an hour walk from Unawatuna (on flipflops ;) ). Well worth it, a nice place to relax, swim a bit and read a book. Busier on weekends, as there are more locals.
If you want to see locals having fun, this is a nice place to go. Also the walk to Jungle beach is very nice. Better is to watch the sunset halfway, walking from Unawatuna.
Every turist place try to sell what they have to offer, this is a classic example. The beach is just fine but nothing special. Its worth a visit but not more. Dont expext paredise.
The location is bit hard to access. But the beach is awesome. You can hangout as long as you want. Better if you go in the evening and you can be there until dark.
Nice to have a swim there after walking from Una beach. It gets crowded on a weekend, so we found early was best. There are 2 separate beaches, one quite bigger than the other.

Go with an open mind. Small beach that at night becomes a party place. Walk down through the bush to a small beach - easy to get a tuk-tuk from Galle/ Unawatuna. Suits all travelers and there was a mix of families with small children, couples and friends all enjoying themselves when I visited. Beach loungers are free (no padding) but it is expected that you will use the restaurant for food and drink. The restaurant food simple and tasty and not over priced. Monkeys may show up for added entertainment.
The nature have distorted by people.sorry to see.they should more protect their nature.....too many Russians and naked birds:) not good for a family specially with kids....

Its a marvolous piece f nature , a nice lonely beach is located inside a jungle. It has many rocks inside and nowadays open a small restaurant inside which offers beer and other food beverages. Must try if you are in Galle

The treck through the mini jungle is lovely, the beach itself gorgeous however the day we visited there was an awful lot of coral not only on the beach but on entering the sea for a swim which made it virtually impossible to enjoy.  On the plus there is an excellent little shack style restaurant where we enjoyed a lovely seafood lunch.  A bit of a hike back uphill but still worth it. Ohh forgot to mention the monkeys playing in the trees 😂
The food available is not so great here. Only one restaurant serving. So plan you meals elsewhere. Surrounded by lush green forest, this small beach is a good hideout for nature lovers.
Best guy super music. Fresh food. I just love these place. Olso in day time is good ocean and nice nature around. I racomand it so much

I visit Sri Lanka for 6 weeks in 2012, on my travels around the country we stayed for 3 nights in Unawatuna, and only heard about this "secret" jungle beach on the last day. we got a tuk tuk to as far asthey would take us before we had to walk (about 10/15mins) tru a jungle path, where if you veer off to the left you can see a faboulous view of the Indian Ocean of an average sized cliff coated in palm trees and just jungle everywhere!, on our walk down to the beach we came across a large land monitor lizard, tons of skinks and dragons, walking tru some shaded area we saw what seemed like the ground retreeting, it was what can only be discribed as a hermit migration, they were everywhere it was so amazing. we see the beach in our sights, surrounded in jungle, the orange sand and turquise blue water (oh i wish i was there now) with great coral among the rocks along the way. there was just one restaurant/bar there when we were there, in fact it was the only building/shack on the beach which is what made it for me, we were the only ones there! right behind tthe beach there are steps up a hill where i ventured to see if i could find any snakes or such, unfortunately i didnt find any snakes but i did come across a pink faced leaf monkey i had heard so much about, endigenous to Sri Lanka, and he was just sitting on a branch above me eatting a banana! I love this place, if you are an animal lover you will too, and Sri Lanka in general!, I will definately be back

A short walk from the Peace Pagoda is a little protected beach, with just one bar/restaurant on its shores. The beach is pretty and you have a great view of the Fort and the rest of Galle, but it would be a lot nicer and if it wasn't full of tourists doing the same thing you are! It has the feeling of a secluded beach but is anything but. But it is still a beautiful beach, very chilled out and fairly unique.
While heading to Unawatuna we wanted to take a break and went to rummassala. There you can see this lovely beach. However be careful about the waves/current as the sea can be very dreadful sometimes.
Nice beach which is completely hidden from out side bustles and in a hillside slope. A good beach to relax and rejoice.

walked there from Unawatuna..took about half an hour..nice walk. beach was average...water wasn't clear like other reviews have said - a little dirty too...a CD case & plastic floated past...maybe it was the time of year?? It was a very small beach, one restaurant and lots of local men..being a single female, I was glad there were other tourists around..I would have felt a little uncomfortable if there wasn't (& I've travelled solo extensively).. I stayed about 20mins and left..won't be going back.

A hidden gem in Galle. Great beach but no longer isolated as it used to be few years back. Nevertheless  the beach is clean and the water is crystal clear. There is a small restaurant run by locals that provides beach chairs and huts and their food isn't bad either.
it is very nice place with fine sand and calm sea of fabulous blue colors. definitely worth to go there for couple of hours just to have those "bounty-the taste of paradise" views.

We were there as we saw it was highly rated in this website. We were not disappointed at all! There's a small bar there which has higher prices than other places. If you are looking for a place to eat (and you are not afraid of local, unclean palaces, you must visit a small restaurant in that's almost in front of the second jungle beach "entrance. The lady who cooks is amazing! And her children too :)

Very pretty beach and safe to swim.  Not very easy access as a very steep climb down to the beach and can be slippery if its been raining.  Tuk tuk takes you fairly close before the descent and plenty of them waiting when you get back up!  Small restaurant on the beach but didn't try the food.  Not suitable for people with disabilities or walking difficulties.

Pretty little beach in the middle of the jungle. Access is a little difficult, but our tuk tuk took us very close to the jungle entry, as we travelled with two toddlers, and it is just a 5 minute walk through the jungle. There are sunbeds and a little beach restaurant at the beach,  where we ate very well while enjoying great views! Careful with the waves and the currents Definitely worth a visit if you're staying in the area for a few days. The Japanese pagoda is close by, and it has beautiful views of Galle, so also worth a quick visit

We had been recommended this beach and it is really nice small and pretty but actually much smaller than I had thought and therefore dominated by the restaurant there and the beds. You can swim in the indian Ocean which is nice as the areas is quite protected but we did not feel the urge to stay long
Beautiful lonely beach. Restaurants near by charges high prices than average standards on foods and beverage. Prepare those with yourself.
Lovely small beach. Unfortunately dominated by the shack/restaurant which serves good sea food. Still worth a visit. Not better than Unawatuna beach if you're looking for a proper beach.

A lovely secluded beach away from Unawatuna but there is a large amount of broken coral on the beach and in the surf, although this turns to sand just offshore. There is a restaurant which is a little overpriced but that does decent food and cold beer. The seats were free if you order drinks or food from them. We had some tiger prawns here which were very fresh if a little over-priced. The sea is a little hard to swim in due to the coral and is not suitable for small children, at least it wasn't when we went.
i can only recommend this place! it was not crowded, food was amazing and beach is very nice. its not typical commercial site, so if you are looking for something cozy, this is it

it's a long walk to get there  but it's a must do!!! the beach is really lovely although not big, the little shack on the beach serves the best devilled chicken I've eaten in 3 weeks . we had a great time there! the kids were able to go in the water because the waves were not to big (although it was monsoon)

When we went to the beach it was full of local men, swimming. They were very noisy, shouting across. Sun loungers were cheap wooden ones stacked up and covered in sand. Most of the Tourists looked like backpackers staying in surrounding cheaper hotels. Not a place for older couples as it is difficult to get down to the beach. It is a muddy pathway down the hill. Could be very dangerous and slippery.
one needs to make some effort to reach this beach...but then since it is little isolated, it retains its beauty as its neither crowded nor dirty...
Beautiful beach, less rough than Unawatuna. Guys at the beach bar are nice, however solo female travelers should be careful walking to/from the beach alone.

Jungle beach was one of the cleanest beach I visited in Sri Lanka. It is a small beach but fantastic. Water is clear, sand is light brown. Does not have too many visitors on weekdays (atleast what we made from our visit). Its a 15 min trek from top of the mountain. Must visit.
A peaceful beach where you can relax, sun loungers provided, nice little bar. Safe swimming, interesting nearby Japenese temple and djs/parties every Wednesday night.
This place is pretty relaxing and offers a nice view. Nice to spend time just chilling and hanging out.
This beach makes a great alternative to the main beaches of Unawatuna. In certain weather conditions it's more sheltered. It can be quite busy for a very small beach, particularly at weekends.

Cute little bay with nice beach cafe. Few sun lounges and very busy with locals at the weekends. Sea is ok to paddle/ jump around in the shallow waters. Steap to get to- quite treacherous mud path. Don't recommend for people with buggy/ walking difficulties.

Jungle beach is very nice, small beach. ideal for spending some relaxing time. unlike Unawatuna beach, it does not have too many restaurants or visitors or noise. it is quite beach with calm surroundings, very still water (no rough like all places around) and a small beach cafe to serve food and drinks. sand is very fine and light golden, waters are clear and good for a swim. really nice, worth the effort to climb down the small him via jungle.

I visited this beach in August when the water was very rough so basically i could not do snorkeling or see any fish/coral. But the place itself the sorroundings are beautiful and adventurous.  There is even a little bar there to buy coctails or soft drink and they also have DJs and parties on wednesday.
small but definitly worth making the effort to go to. Nice place to have drinks. Not very busy when we were there. the sea is so warm!!!!! would love to go back
A nice peaceful beach great place to relax, free loungers, nice little bar. Nice safe swimming and interesting nearby temple

A local beach with some great food. The only thing to watch out for is that the beach drops away quickly and so very small children will need constant attention. Our children who are 11 and 12 loved playing in the waves.
Definitely worth the visit . Full of locals , very safe . Take some money . Just avoid the rocks on the left .

We found jungle beach when there was only a few people there, which was quite relaxing - the beach is quite small, but idyllic if it's not crowded. There are appx 12 sunbeds free of charge (but you are expected to buy something in the "cafe" if you choose the beds). Cafe served cold drinks - we didn't try the food. A bit rocky and some rubbish in the water, but still a nice break from the heat in Galle. We paid appx 500rs each way for a tuktuk from Galle bus station. The walk from The road to the beach is a lot less struggle than we expected - but not accessible in a wheelchair. Kids would make this 4 min walk easily. And fridays by sunset the rumour has it that there's a big party there ;)
this is one of the best beach in sri lanka ,its not much crowed and cool and good place to relax in the day

A calm and quiet beach surrounded by a jungle.Sea is calm and suitable for a evening sea bath.Green of the jungle adds extra beauty to the blue of the sea.Two colours are separated by the colour gold owned by the beach.Only negative point is the jungle beach restaurant pollution the beauty and the uniqueness of the beach
Nice beach with a cool walk to it from Unawatuna. For less adventures people you can also take a tuktuk to it. There are some cool animals in the jungle.

An easy walk from the peace pagoda, this little cove is a nice spot to sunbathe and swim. Enjoyed by locals (smart enough to hang out under the shade of the trees) and,predominantly European, tourists alike. There's a restaurant on the beach if you need refreshments, though I can't attest to it's quality as I didn't venture in. They hold dance parties here every Wednesday night - the way is lit by makeshift lights and local djs supply the beats. Jungle Beach is definitely worth a look. I can't help but think it might get quite crowded in the high season. It seemed just right in August, considered to be low season.

Yes go here. It's a bit of a trek to get to and if you're not great with climbing and scrambling you might struggle to get to it but it's definitely worth it when you're there. You have to walk through a bit of jungle or walk around a pile of rocks to enter this beach but once you're there you could spend hours there! It feels very secluded but also very safe. Locals and tourists go there and there's a little restaurant serving fresh juice and curries or chips etc. There are also sunloungers and because of the jungle there's sun and shade. Getting into the actual sea is hard as there's a bed of coral that smacks you in the ankles with every wave but if you get past it I saw lots of people swimming and enjoying themselves. If you're mad about swimming maybe go somewhere else but if you want a bit of a beach paradise for a day go here. I also saw they have parties and DJs every Tuesday.

Beautiful relaxing beach! Little peach of paradise! Great drinks but very quite. Apparently they have Djs on Tuesdays so if you are looking for a more upbeat day, research before going. Stop by the temple on the way down and take some photos.
Must to visit place, lots of flags from different countries (gonna bring Georgian flag next time to hang it there !) Not a bad bar with good fresh choice. WiFi is available !
A great hidden beach - not too busy. Great little bar/cafe with good food. The whole family swam in the sea - a memorable experience
Poor restaurant, not very clean. Not well lit at night. Toilets were disgusting. Staff were really nice.

This is a nice little spot to relax a bit out of Galle. Cost 500 slr for a tuk tuk from around the local spice market. Litte cafe to buy drinks and food from, coke was 200 slr, juice was about 300ish. There is a bit of dead coral as you walk in which comes as a shock, but push about a metre through and its soft sand. Water was very cloudy when we were there, but could have just been the time of year. Worth checking out!

Secluded and not too many people which was excellent! A walk down from the road through the jungle and you are greeted with the ocean. Unfortunately the water was a bit murky (maybe at this time of year??) But other than that, it was really nice.
The Trek down to the beach was nice, and beach was pristine. Recommend to go on a weekday to avoid local alcoholics. Avoid paying for parking - touts along the way.
Nice beach but you can find more beautiful beaches not so crowded on Sri Lanka. Here is a nice view you can make some pics.this beach is good for one day trip

We went to the beach in early morning and came back in evening, so you can guess that it was good. Its not a big beach like unawatuna beach but the place is nice to relax. There are washrooms near the beach but unclean and the locks are broken as well.
There was the old good "wild beach" a kind of "free rastaman republic". Now it`s a reasonable clean place with small caffes and a lot of different peoples of all ages.

This beach was recommend by advertisement and said to be a great small beach, quiet and with monkeys all around. Well the fact is, it was noisy based on the bar situated in the middle of the beach, Did not see any wildlife, but an overcrowded beach surrended by noisy russian tourists

We are going back to Unawatuna largely because of Jungle Beach, and we're taking friends to see the place for the same reason. I cannot give a better recommendation than that. You'll read other - probably better - reviews of the perfect, clear blue water in a secluded bay, you'll read about the free-flowing (strong!), reasonably priced cocktails, surprisingly (given the setting) good food, but I will just sum it up by saying it's like being on your own tropical paradise bar, even though you're just 10 minutes outside of the relative bustle of Galle. Getting here is by way of dirt road and then a walk. Make sure you arrange with your Tuk-Tuk driver to pick you up at a certain time as you won't be finding a taxi here later. But allow way more time that you think, you won't want to leave.

Amazing place to relax if you are going to galle or unwatuna side, a secluded beautiful beach where you have to climb down a small cliff which leads to a beautiful beach a small shack/restaurant .. Absolutely lovely

We walked to the beach, about 30 - 40 mins,  mostly along a small road, towards the end a some smaller path with a Creek crossing. From the main beach it is well sign posted. You can also go by tuk tuk if you don't want to walk... The beach was a bit more crowded than we expected, with a cafe and several sun chairs, but it was still nice and worth the walk. You can use the sun chairs for free if you buy something from the cafe which has reasonable prices. If you have spare time, definitely go for a few hours, but it's not a must see.
Bit disappointing. The 20 min walk from Una was quite nice but the beach itself was not all that. Swimming is better here than at Una though
Fantastic place. All you want from a beach. The restaurant and the folks running it are fantastic. Place to be, for sure.

The is by far the best beach I have been to in southern Sri Lanka. It had clear blue waters and was like a large pool with minimum waves. Even safe for children. The virgin forest around the beach adds value to it. It is getting popular by the day. An advice is to visit the place during a week day when the crowds are less.

We decided to walk there from the main Unawatuna beach and it was a really nice walk! You have to walk through the jungle for part of it, crossing over a few streams and up and down stone steps but it really adds to the experience. As we hadn't seen anyone during the walk we thought it'd be a lovely secluded hideaway....it isn't! It was SO busy! It's a pretty beach with a friendly beach bar but I didn't quite get the hype about it, maybe it's just because it was so busy. There is another small beach at the right side behind the rocks which is quieter but a bit tricky to get to unless you swim it. Still worth a visit but have realistic expectations!

Nice almost private beach near to busy Galle... We rent a scooter cause tuk tuk cost around 600ruppies to go there.. Beach is really small - 100m but it's great and calm place. You can buy some food or drinks in restaurant (juices 350r, cola 150r, meals 450+r). Great place for chill and relax

Went there in the evening and in the morning. Thoroughly enjoyed! There is a restaurant (hut like) where they serve juices and cocktails, they have areas to rest after the swim. Crowd was not bad as well.

This seemed to be a secret, as it was a very quiet and secluded beach. Beautiful clean beach with palms and a little mountain as a backdrop. There's a small shack there, where you get super affordable but fresh food, and drinks. They also have changing rooms, showers, toilets and beach/deck chairs.

Scootered up the hill on our way back from Galle. Lovely road, then sand bag steps down to the beach. Changing room was clean and lit, beers were 400 rupees, staff at bar watched our stuff. Had a lovely swim, and looking back at the beach it was very pretty. I dont like Unawatuna beach where dogs leave their mark everytime you turn around, this beach, by contrast was clean

My friends and I had a relaxing day snorkelling and enjoying the beautiful small beach of Jungle Beach. You can get there by land, using a Tuc Tuc or bike. But you can also do a snorkelling tour using a Dive club at Unawatuna Beach. The last thing is what we did, with Divers Land Dive Club. It costs more but we also enjoyed the boat ride. Our guesthouse was near to the dive club. The owner was honest to tell us, which is really fair, the sea was calm that day so we choose this way. There's also a small beach place which provides food and drinks... Some locals were playing music... Had a great time..
If you'll go to Unawatuna, you should visit Jungle Beach. You go from jungle, uphill and see pagoda, after you go down to Jungle beach
Hidden among the trees though not too far from the city is this really small piece of paradise. Great place to spend the afternoon though it can get a little crowded due to small beach area.
I never thought that the beach would be this small! It is not more than maybe 50-100m and there is a bar. Ok, there are a lot of trees around, but not really my idea of a jungle beach.

We stayed in Unawatuna for 3 nights out of season and decided that we wanted something other than the main beach to visit. We heard about Jungle beach from the lovely lady that ran our guesthouse (Moon Light Rest) and decided we would walk over a have a look. It was about a 30 minute walk through the jungle and the track was very good and well signposted all the way so no need to ask for any help from a local (that would likely ask for money afterwards). The beach was lovely, quite small but it had a nice chilled atmosphere with a beach bar and also very calm sea which was great for swimming. It was full of locals as it was a saturday and it was great fun watching them play cricket and rugby on the beach.

the guys that work at the bar and restaurant are really awesome. we didn't have enough money for our tab, told them we would leave our cell phone behind while we went back to the hotel to grab money... the guy said not to worry about leaving our hones, just to come pay the rest of the bill when we had time.. Super rad!!
One of Sri Lankas best kept secrets a really nice beach only 10 minutes by car from Unawatuna Beach Area.
A little dirty, and while with views of commercial marina and cement plant, surprisingly serene
Beautiful little beach. Only one (restaurant), wich means that this is more of an excurtion, rather than a whole day trip beach

Very nice little beach although it can be quite crowded now after the Unawatuna Beach "quick fix" (filled with new brown sand). Jungle Beach has a small restaurant and a bar. Beware that the toilet facilities on the beach are very limited
We went there twice on our trip, the first time it was sunny to chill out, we also went when it was stormy which was a very nice experience. A must visit location

Had quite high expectations for Rummassala and Jungle beach. However having waded thru a rocky downhill path thru a mildly dense jungle we came across a short stretch of beach with a lot of washed up corals, a small restaurant and no where to go. The beach area was covered by few sun beds and tables and chairs from the restaurant (have to pay to use them), there is hardly space to walk. Swimming is not recommended here. Waste of time really. Sri Lanka has much better options to offer than this.

This beach is located near by Rama Sulla where God Hanuman brings the Dronagiri mountain from himalaya. Water is so clean and there is no crowd at all. Isolated and love to go in the water. Must go and enjoy

The most wonderful feature is the thick foliage over the entire beach. It is quite an attraction for locals and foreigners as well, so holiday season must be uncomfortably crowded because the beach is not very long or wide and spacious. The beach is very small and covered by trees from all around, and is not so much of an "active" tourist zone. Not a beach I would feel comfortable being alone. I would recommend only carrying what is absolutely necessary to the beach.

We walked to the beach from our hotel, right the otherwise end of Unawatuna beach. It tok about 50 minutes, but felt longer bacause of the humidity. It was quiet before lunch, but more people gathered after lunch, and it could no longer be described as quiet. The little cafe provided reasonably priced dishes. Having had a bout of tourist stomach in our first week, we are always concerned with food hygiene, however, they seemed to be washing dishes nonstop behind the cafe, so nothing to worry about. Like Unawatuna, the waves are a bit strong, so little ones need to be looked after.
It was our favorite beach to go to. It was quiet, with plenty of shaded area, a bar with friendly staff. Would recommend as it is like being in a movie. A tiny bit of paradise.

One need to walk through the jungle about 20 mins to arrive this secret beach. It's nice and clean, unfortunately on the day we went it is raining and waves are strong. It's better to get a tuk tuk that waits you outside as the road outside is very quiet and has no tuk tuk passing by after sunset.

We probably picked one of the last good weather days for a while. Lazy, tropical place. We all had fried rice and cold beer on the beach. Sublime. I suspect during high season this place could be a nightmare, so we all enjoyed it more because it was less crowded (bit like Unawatana in high season). Almost like a postcard. Magical

there is tow jungle beaches one is near to the pagoda temple and the other one is about 500m after in rumassala road . To me definitely the one near to pagoda is the best one and I think it is one of the best beaches in lanka inspite that it is a small beach but you will feel the real lankan beach in this beach and there is a view point before you go into the jungle and it is so peaceful and there is another view point in the old hotel few steps before the second jungle beach and this on of the best view points you will ever see

This beach is like a  little paradise, though can be difficult to get to. Would definitely not recommend going there alone, especially if a female, I know I wouldn't feel safe there alone, however if with friends you would have nothing to worry about. The food in the small restaurant is freshly prepared, cheap and tasty, so are the fruit juices. They were very understandable when I explained I was a vegan, and even remembered this whenever I came back, and made sure not to add eggs in my vegetable fried rice.

this is a very secluded beach and sometimes it is not very safe to go. the autos will charge u a bomb and then there is 10 mins trek to the beach. if in a group then can be a fun place but also depends on the kind of people there are on the beach.
nice place for snorchling, nice place for photo on the rocks with waves, nice view to Galle - Fort. It is quit far away, but it is good place

A good walk from unuwatuna beach, this beautiful little beach was like finding a hidden gem. Granted we were here in low season so we only had to share it with a handful of people (could imagine it being very busy at peak times). Lovely secluded spot surrounded by jungle. The one restaurant on the beach had a good selection of food and drink, and gave us our meal for free because we found a caterpillar in it, even though we didn't say anything and ate the meal anyway (shows its fresh). Will definitely go back again.

I went during low season and bad weather and was thoroughly underwhelmed. Probably a spot to visit with a group of friends when its beautiful weather, otherwise you'll enjoy the main beach much more! The smoothies are cheap but the alcohol is expensive.

This is my favorite beach in Sri Lanka. Yes, it is crouded and small, but the surrounding nature is great (we walked from Unawatuna beach), and there were no waves, so you can swim as you like. I drank som smoothies at a bar, I liked them, as well as the fact that beach chairs are free of charge.

Small beach place in jungle beach.. I very silent place.near to Galle and unawatuna it's located . Compare with unawatuna beach jungle beach is excellent. Unawatuna some beach boys are very cheaters. And very dangers. But jungle beCh ppl are hlpfull any time. Only one restaurant in jungle beach....
A great please to pass away a day, especially at this time of year as it is very quiet, great for us oldies, food is very good and reasonably priced and the beer is cold!!

We enjoyed this beach and it's worth a visit. Low season it was quit and secluded. The cafe at the bottom is really nice and the staff friendly. We payed 300rupees from Unawatuna but you can walk as it's only 2k. We did however encounter an unpleasant scenario when we were walking back and passed a lot of young men. Somehow in that time my friends phone was pick pocketed from her bag. We went back down to search and ask around and the couldn't of been more attentive or helpful. A great little beach but be alert when walking back or leaving your stuff.

This is a great place to stop by when you are visiting Galle for a break from the heat and sightseeing Galle Fort. The sea is calm so we could easily swim with the kids, unlike in most of the other spots around Sri Lanka. Tuk tuk ride cost us 900 ruphiees return from Galle. There is a bar on the beach with basic food and cold beer.

Hard to find if driving.  Careful which road you take as some roads are tuk tuk accessible only.  Need to access from main road then turn off.  Still a little walk from where you park car, down hill, but shady on way up.  Small beach.  Not sure I would go again.  Not worth it.

I was nearly put off going by some bad reviews but I found it peaceful enough. I went on a Saturday in the off season and lots of locals were using it to party on but there is plenty of room for everyone. The one restaurant / bar keeps the beach very clean and there are lots of wooden beds to sunbath or lie under the many shady trees all free of charge. I could easily  imagine hoards of drunken tour groups from the northern climes ruining it for more sober users in the high season though.

We were told by local this was the "beach" to go to...it turned out to be true! Spent couple days there, only a short tuk-tuk ride from our hotel. Kids did a lot of snorkelling, and we just relaxed on the beach. Has a small cafe serving drinks and food.

Quite, calm waters, isolated and clean. Heard a lot about this beach. A short tuk tuk ride from Unawatuna and down a path from the a jungle. Stayed here for a good 6 hours and enjoyed every moment of it. Only one restaurant there and bit on the expensive side. If in Unawatuna, do visit Jungle beach.
We were on Sri Lanka in May and ocean always storms. So we spend whole day on Jungle Beach in the shade on palm. The place where you can quietly swim. I recommend you to spend one day on this beach.

Hiked from Thaproban hotel to this jungle beach.. It took about 30 minutes to reach there with path narrowing and through the jungle..  It was quite awesome walk early in the morning..  We were the first ones to arrive at this beach and the sign boards are very clear to take you there..  swam in the beach for sometime and there is a small hotel serving food and cocktails there..  A place not to be missed for early risers..
This is something that someone must do since is in the area!! Walk to jungle beach is the best all the walkway is in jungle!!! Not too long and not very difficult worth to do it!!!

We were looking forward to a peaceful untouched beach, especially considering the exciting walk through the jungle to get there. However, we were not alone, and the beach very quickly got busy, with a lot of quite rude tourists ( will not name the culture!) pushing in front of others to the little bar and talking noisily on the beach. The walk to the beach was great fun, but we were disappointed by the actual beach and it didn't live up to our expectations.

The place offers a nice view of light blue water and Galle fort, the path to the place is  a downhill climb sorrounded with huge trees, the entire place is actually put up in a very small segment of a rock and a jungle
I like the beach but sometimes its very crowded. Ideal for kids! I liked the way to go by foot to the beach, really jungles! Nice to visit if you are staying in unawatuna!

awesome place. but you need to go little early before 10 am to avoid rush. don't have too many options for food or drinks on the beach...the approach to the beach is also little difficult. but its a very nice beach. clean and lots of waves...
Spent a morning here. Amazing views and nice beaches. Go early and enjoy having the beach to yourself!
Lots of shade, a good swimming area, food on the beach. Delightful. Can catch a Tuk Tuk to the beach or walk through the forest. saw two great big goannas on the way.
