Jungle beach is one of the best beached you can ever be in the whole world and it is perfectly safe for families with even little kids. Access has made difficult by the nature itself to save the valuable place and therefore a walk through a narrow road is a must even if you park at the nearest car park. The view is spectacular and unique. Still this place has been ruined by the people how are running a restaurant and a sun bed renting place there. It seems like locals can not visit that place and it is only for foreigners, They would not let us rent a sun bed even after paying and they were not happy to let us have a shower again even after we offer to pay 100 each. They just rent sun beds and tables only to the drunken idiots who spoil and litter the whole surrounding and we saw many polythene and plastic litter just floating in the sea because of this people who only think about there income and nothing about sustaining the nature. We were disgusted by the way the locals were treated there and it was nice to have a small family up in the road who are running a car park and a bathing area so we could have freshen up and if not for them we would have to travel all the way back to out hotel to have a shower. Even though I've heard many times that down south is becoming more to foreigners only and decent locals are not welcome anymore, this was the first time with such a bad experience and It was a disaster. I don't think this is a good choice for decent foreigners even as it is only for the alcoholics and they are drinking and shouting to ruin the calm and quite holiday of every one around.
Very nice and calm waters for kids, but whistling and screaming from drunk russian tourists spoiled our experience

Few km away from highway exit.... lovely place and nice beach...can have safe sea bath comparing to other places in the vicinity of galle...you can have drinks and foods from restaurent from there...liquor too allowed to bring from outside....tables and beds are available on our request....
I liked nature around Jungle Beach. Clean water and not a lot people there. A lot of cute monkeys on trees. They don't go down to disturb people.

The beach is situated away from unnawantuna.  You need to trek down a jungle to reach this place. The view is just breathtaking. However I suggest not to try out the restaurant on the beach. Its just over priced and not good. Make sure you carry some food items and ample water.

We had high hopes after all the reviews but it was underwhelming. Perhaps because we had just arrived from mirissa and those beaches are much more unspoiled. Jungle beach seemed so small. With lots of tanning beds and a restaurant. It almost felt like a resort beach and not "jungle". Didn't stay very long as we found Unawatuna more fun. Also I got bitten a thousand times as I lay suntanning by an invisible mosquito which was no bigger than a gnat. The Sri Lankans said that its common there. So take bug spray. It is not a mozzie and bites during the day.
Perfect, little and quiet beach hidden away from the  traffic.  A must for anyone who wants to relax and enjoy the beauryful ocean away from the crowd.
Hard to get to but lovely. The sea is calm so nice to swimming. The sea is very clear so you get to see some fish.

A tuk tuk brought us to this beach from our resort early in the morning. It was quiet and tranquil and had lovely views towards Galle. The waters were warm to swim in and the beach area was extremely clean. Lounge chairs were available for lazing on and the cafe was open and ready for service. It was quiet whilst we were there. Jungle Beach was just a lovely, lovely spot to enjoy and cool off in the warm weather.

This bay is well worth the steep walk from the hill top where you're dropped by the Tuk tuk. The path is OK and part has handrails. The beach is beautiful; secluded with free sun beds and good facilities. There is one small bar selling divine milkshakes. It was spoiled somewhat by numerous bits of litter in the sea which made it off putting to swim in. Unawatuna was much larger and busier, but also cleaner.

Best place to stay if you are going to visit yala national park  which is only about 10 minutes away,,if you are looking for classy place with comfortable rooms and AC for a decent price this is where you should be heading .I would suggest to call before booking and get the best price from Mr. Viran. Service  was fast never kept us waiting and the staff was very friendly and help full.. Talking about the food is just amazing and tasty with different varieties both Sri Lankan and western..they also arrange safari jeeps apon request for very reasonable prices.. It is best to go early morning to see the Leopards otherwise it is just a waste of  time ...we found everything we need in Koragaha lodge  to enjoy our stay in yala,, we will definitely come Back here when we come to yala again...thank you :)
The scenery is beautiful and the walking trails around the beach are idyllic. But the beach itself is small, noisy and very crowded. The space for sunbathing is limited.
Lovely little secluded beach with food shack that served lunch fit for a prince with a lovely friendly owner

The small trek to arrive to the beach is lovely and when you are there it is like to be in the Cote d azur in France. the water is clean and so calm, the small bar serve very good pinacolada and fresh beers. Perfect place when it is not too crowded.

There are 2 beaches with the name Jungle. One is Jungle and is under Japanese Pagoda. Is bigger and little bit overcrowded. And second is White Jungle beach. The way on this beach  is cca 500 m befor  the Jungle. It is smaller but also with free sunbeds, toilet and small restaurant. Both are ideal for swimming.

Small beach with finer sand and much gentler waves than Unawatuna Beach. 9am and a handful of people there so very peaceful. Can imagine this place would get crowded easily.  I explored the nearby tracks and saw lizards, lots of birds, butterflies...and visited the Japanese Peace Pagoda. Very hot but very enjoyable walk. Be careful if walking in flip flops as the track is uneven.

Beautiful small beach located in the "jungle" - perfect for snorkelling and sunbathing during the day. There is a beach cafe/restaurant serving good food and cocktails. Every Wednesday there is a beach party from sunset to sunrise - amazing music and people of all ages - tourists and locals alike. Amazing night!
Nice beach close to Unawatuna, that can be reached by Tuktuk or by foot. Good restaurant on the beach with food and drinks for very amicable prices.

Spent a few hours on the jungle beach watching the sub set with a bottle of rum and a few beers. If you don't byob there is a bar on the beach that is owned by the rehab center nearby. So much of the profits go to fund a good service. Toilets available however you are better off finding a private area amongst the shrubbery and trees. Fantastic view of the city skyline. Remote. Beach loungers are available, I think for a small rental fee. However you need to be able to do a small hike up and down a beaten rock path on a hill to get there. It is a bit dangerous due to the branches and uneven rock. Make sure you have a flashlight if you plan on staying for the sunset.

We arrived here by boat after snorkelling along the shore which was well worth doing. The beach wasn't crowded and there were plenty of free beds with umbrellas available which we definitely needed for some well earned rest. A very basic toilet is available and you can buy drinks there. Walking up the beach we were disappointed to see quite a lot of rubbsh, however, this is hidden from the main beach area.
oyu will really enjoy this beach specially if you are a foreigner.. but usually the place is more crowded in weekends
Like: Clean, safe with toilets, food and drinks available! Dislike: Can be too crowded because of its popularity.

The beach is small, quiet and calm! Ideal for taking a rest. There are sunbeds in the sun as well as in the shadow. Water is transparent and much calmer than on other nearby beaches. A bar provides drinks and lunch. You can walk there from Unawatuna beach (takes about 30-40 mins) if you want to enjoy the nature and the views, or take a tuk-tuk (costs approximately 300lkr). You can also visit Japanese Pagoda up there. On Wednesday nights you can attend a Jungle Beach Party, which can turn out to be quite a wild one! Place is really worth paying a visit.

There are actually two beautiful jungle beaches both nice,isolated and very suitable for swimming,There is a restaurant- bar on each beach with free beach chairs.Beaches are accessible by boat or vehicle +5 minute walking.They  make parties once a week(wednesday or tuesday) there.
If you do one beach day, do it here. It is small and insular, however that is what is nice. Lovely sea and beach, matched with shaded areas, beer and good food.
Beautifull fish, fantastic view, clean see, free sun loungers, clean beach, the beach restaurant, disco in the evening, far from central beach

Small beach on a cove which means you can easily swim unlike other beaches in sri Lanka e.g. Unawatuna where the waves are too big. Little bar there to get a drink and food. Also rented mask and snorkel from them for 300 for an hour. Coral and fish not amazing. But at least you can swim the 15 meters from the beach to see. Nothing compared to what you might see in Thailand, Fiji, Aus, etc. Beach is clean and there are basic sunloungers which we didn't need to pay for. A welcome break from the larger beaches.

Beach is crowded. There is a bar on the beach, but the locals working there are really out to gouge tourists. Do not book their "fishing" tour. It consisted of a guy tying two lines directly on to the boat, and trolling for about an hour. Once we hooked a small fish, they brought it into the boat and handed it to us. Also for snorkeling, water is too murky and visibility too poor to have a good time. For a less crowded beach and for surfing stay at nearby Coco Bay resort.

it is very small and crowded. There are much better beaches around: Koggala & Unawatuna. There is a beach restaurant and beach chairs. Walking the jungle on the way to the beach is very nice and we enjoyed it. The views is beautiful. It is few kilometres from Unawatuna, so take a motorbike. There are some places where to leave it.
Several tuk-tulk drivers had mentioned this beacah but it turned out to be rather crowded when we were there and not what we had hoed for.
I loved the walk as you will see the Japanese pagoda from a distance and have a turn off to sunset point... Jungle beach was okay...
Jungle beach is a small but very clean beach. There are some restaurants but do not expect too much. Water is nice. Hardly any waves. Nice place for family with small kids.

My sister and I are 12, and we thought jungle beach was amazing the walk is ten minutes long, it's a nice walk through the jungle, the water is safe There's nice parts of shade on the beach for you to sit on wooden loungers.  We had drinks and lunch at the restraunt and it was very tasty and affordable

Small, with one bar, reasonable prices, decent food, free beds, lots of shade, safe beach, and nice walk to get too.  Plus you can see the Pagoda at the top first.  Lunch for four, 5 big beers, 2 fruit drinks....420 rupees.  Free bed in the shade on a nice beach, tough to beat.  Slightly crowded but the size dictates how many people can be there so not too bad at all.
Yuo could lay on the beach watching the nicest view of the Roomassala . The bar serves  nice smoothies and shakes.
Good: safe to swim, clean sand, snorkeling early morning (water gets cloudy later).   Pleasant beach bar. Good sun-beds free , adequate shade Can get crowded.
A very nice Little Beach, without too many tourists. Free beach chairs. No big waves. Perfect for children.

Great experience! The beach consists of two parts. If you leave tuk tuk earlier on your way, you'll get to the wild one. There could be dance music and illumination in the evening. Beware of underwater stones, sometimes they are very near the water surface, I hurt my foot. If you go to the very end of the road, near Japanese temple, there is the second part. It has cafes and it is much very cosy and comfortable. Tasty cocktails and fresh juices, nice people, shallow sandy entrance into clear water, no big waves, very safe, beautiful tropic fish swimming around you - great for adults and children. And awesome views! Must visit!
I must say Jungle Beach is the most beautiful beach in Sri Lanka for me, I went to there 1 time, but I fall in love with here.
came here several years ago before the tsunami,it was paradise but not anymore it has been commercialised.now its got 2 bars and very loud disco music.what a shame.
So secluded, only a few travellers. Right near the monument to the Tsunami which offers fabulous views looking  back on Galle. A beautiful panorama and clean crystal waters.

15 min hike through a rocky path, well marked trail. Make sure to wear comfortable hiking shoes.  We did see people walking in flip flops, but it is a very uneven rocky path.   Beautiful warm, calm, swimming beach.  Go early in the am if you want a lounge chair.

Its a nice beach tucked away in a corner, but its a popular beach so expect it to be crowded. We had a good time on the beach, the beach restaurant served some great fried prawns for a reasonable price and the beer was cold, nice crowd too. The beach was clean, the snorkeling decent, water calm for kids to jump in. Visited the beach twice during my stay at Galle. Its a good beach to spend time on, would love to visit again.

Very small beach and get crowded and hightide after lunch so come early. The water also gets very dirty during hightide! Free sunbeds, not so very comfy but free. Take a short walk around to the other beach, more quiet but no sunbeds. You can take the walk from Unawatuna Beach or go by tuctuc for around 400rp. Cute beach, just not during the afternoon.

we were advised by our hotel to arrive early and I'm very glad we did. The beach itself is about 50 m from end to end. This means that it does not take many people to make a crowd. You can very easily combine a visit to this beach with the Japanese peace monument up the hill. You can ask the tuk tuk driver to take you to the monument. You then  walk down the track and turn right to the beach. It is clearly marked. There is a pleasant Caribbean feel about it although in the distance you can see the town of Galle with various industrial chimneys and so on. The beach itself consists of two sections, the nearest one of which is used by the locals and the other for the tourists. There is an informal restaurant with seats and they offer fruit juice, coffee and meals throughout the day, though that is not obvious from the advertisements. You have to ask. Bearing in mind the captive audience the prices are reasonable, about Rs.300 for a nice fruit juice and here it is the real thing. Fresh juice freshly juiced. No bottled stuff here mate. The beach contains many loungers. They have actually fitted in 2 rows. Other half went for a snorkel and was excited by the fish that she did see though there was not a great variety. It is certainly safe. I will say about the sea in this part of the world that you can be lulled into a sense of safety in calm weather but once every so often you get a rogue wave which has quite a lot of power in it. A couple of hours was enough for us and we left at about 11:30 AM when people started to turn up in droves. There are taxis waiting so no need to request a return drive because it will cost you more. Taxi and by taxi I mean tuk tuk should set you back about Rs.600 maximum return that's three pounds to the Brits among you or four euros. Ladies, I nearly forgot to mention, there is a changing room. Take the morning and chill out folks it's a dead cert success. Read my other Sri Lanka reviews by clicking on my user name to the left of this page. Lots of useful hints and tips.

It takea you les than 20 min to walk to Jungle Beach from Unawantu. NOT hard to find, just follow the signs. The Beach was crowded when we where there on a sunday. I snorkled but visibility was pool and the corals is dead. Few fish. We like it better in Unawantu.

Went there to see Lord Hanuman statue. Being Indian, I cant miss it if I am in that part of Sri Lanka. Sea view is awesome. Clear water. Even if you are chest deep in water, you can steel see your feet.
snorkeling not too much crowded. To be reached by tuk tuk or hotel service. Very nice quite beach with snorkeling and a nice restaurant on the beach

I guess living in a country with the worlds best beaches (Australia) This was pretty disappointing No different to unawatuna beach You have to walk down a trail to get there - right next door to the peace pagoda too which is absolutely beautiful! I wouldn't waste my time heading here - you won't get a sun lounge anyways!! Head to Mirissa or Koggala if you like clear water to swim in not merky sandy water

walk there as we came across lovely locals as well as sunset point (another rocky beach before Jungle Beach). Jungle Beach is however very busy (we went during Feb) with both locals and tourists. because its so small we struggled to find a place to lie down, sand and sun loungers. worth going for an afternoon or morning.

This has now become one of the top beaches I love to visit. The beach starts soon after the jungle. I assume those kind of locations are very rare. The right side far end wasn't much clean. Those who like snorkeling, this is a place to begin as the waters are shallow.

One of the prettiest beach I have ever been. Sence of the beach with white sand will defenetly take your breath away. Its a must visit place for all the beach lovers. Don't forget the sun lotion though as its burning hot. Awesome location for a photoshoot too.

It is a little bit of trek to get to. But it is worth every minute of it. Quiet during the day, with a laze shack serving good cocktails. Given its cove like location you don't have to worry about being knocked about by the current and waves. You can just float and soak in the sun.

It's two small beaches with serene sea good for children's bathing. On the hill above the beach is Japanese pagoda of peace, you can also take a walk on the cape. Breaches crowded and not very beautiful.
After the peace and quiet of coco bay Jungle beach is great. It's lively and great bars. All different ages there too.

Well worth the walk to this lovely beach, don't be tempted to take a tuk tuk to the beach, the walk is beautiful walking through the jungle and seeing the monkeys swinging in the trees. Sunbeds and umbrellas are free. A small cafe on the beach which serves all sorts of meals and drinks including fresh juices. Fresh fish is bought to the cafe every day so you can take your pick of the days catch. The beach is split into two and we went for the quieter one which we walked to over the rocks, I'm sure there is probably another route to this. Beautiful to swim in the sea and look back towards the beach surrounded by the jungle. Definitely worth a day here.

Beach is rather long, but not too deep - about 4-5 rows of sunbeds that makes it quite. Sunbeds and umbrellas are free if you take at least something in any cafe (they are spread all over the beach line). Cafes are tasty, but menus are rather same in all of them. Waves are smaller vs other shores, so it fits families, not surfers. Beds are not available after sunset
We stayed nearby and walked down for a dip. Ended up getting a table on the sand and staying into the evening. Not a lot of food options, but you can make do and the beer is cold.
Small beach area.  It was a national holiday when we were there and the place was packed.  Just one bar there.  Average prices and a so so atmosphere.  Nothing special.
It is a beautiful and clean beach with a nice restaurant with friendly people. They serve good food and drinks. Their pineaapple juice was very tasty.

The place came highly recommended but given how hard it is to get there, it's really not worth all the efforts. It's a very small beach with calm water for a swim. The sand is actually rough, unlike the soft sands you find at some other beaches in South Sri Lanka.

The wording is too strong 'jungle beach'... We went there all the way and then came back straight away.... I thought I'll be alone swimming In a jungle beach but it was packed of people and locals....

It's a good 30 minute walk there, so leave early in the day. It's worth the walk for all the monkeys, peacocks & birds you see on the way! A very pretty spot, much quieter than the main beach in Unwatuna and better for swimming.
nice location,hidden in the jungle.small beautiful beach but not so wavy,quite deep so maybe not for small kids.nice bar with food service on the side.
Relaxing with cold beer, enjoying the catch of the day, swimming & enjoying the sun All while taking in the beautiful scenery...a little slice of heaven!

A cool and shady 15 min walk from unawatuna, and you are at the trendy and lively jungle beach. Lots of young people, lots of beer going around. restaurant is averagely priced, laid back and chilled out. We saw people getting tuks tuks if you don't fancy the walk there and back. We only went the once and felt that was enough, but overall we liked jungle beach. Maybe a little crowded, but high tide was on the way so it would probably have felt more spacious had it been low tide. Worth a visit if you are in unawatuna for a few days! I think this place would appeal more to backpackers than anyone else though! It's easy to find too just follow the wooden painted signs from the town.

Much smaller than the main beach but a really pretty little spot and especially good if you can get a sunbed. We saw a whole family of monkeys in the trees and coming down to take bits of banana from tourists (bought from the bar). Go and see the Japanese Peace Temple next door while you're there
We walked from Unawatuna,  takes about 30 min. Nice walk. Small beach gets busy so go early, before 10am to get a sunbed.  Nice bar for drinks and snacks.

Too many people know about this hidden beach that lives up to its name! Hard to get a nice spot if you are not an earlybird. Nice lunchcafe, pick the catch of the day. Realy miss a path to the next small beach, now it is too hard to reach.
The beach is nice and good for water sports.But difficult to reach by car.You need to walk for more than 2 kms in the hilly terrain.
Lovely little Beach sheltered by the reefs so safe swimming lots of sun-beds with great cafe excellent menu and some great drinks
great place to stay and its very good for swimming without big waves. nice restaurant. its interesting to walk across the beach to the little jungle beach near by.

It is a "must" to visit this nice beach.  You walk from Unawatuna and it is good description for the way until reach the small charming Jungle Beach. You find the very nice beach after walked through "the Jungle". The small restaurant serves good food, we asked for fish and were very satisfied.

Very nice hike in the jungle to the beach. Nice beach,  not too large. Staff very friendly. The lagoon behind the beach was impressive in terms of wildlife. Many pink lotus flowers have grown there, a mesmerizing view! Toilets could be better maintained (availability of soap and paper towels).

We stopped off here (at the Jungle Beach on the Galle side) on a hike from Galle to Unawatuna. It’s a pleasant little stretch of beach, but the walk down to it is by no stretch of the imagination through ‘jungle’. There’s a café and about a dozen tables and umbrellas. We would have had a drink here if it hadn’t been so expensive, but we decided to just have a dip in the sea and wait till we got to Unawatuna.
A small beach ,far away from tourist(better go with scooter) . A restaurant there.

After walking in the heat for almost an hour from Unawatuna beach we arrived at Jungle beach! It was not as we had expected but it was cool!. Its was really small and we where lucky to get some chairs! We stayed there for a couple of hours and went snorkelling which only cost 300 rupees for an hour.
hot, dusty walk down a steep track to a a small, busy beach was a disappointing waste of time. Water did not look inviting.

Yes its crowded, especially if you go on a Weds during peak tourist season. But thats the experience. Laughter, mingling, drinking and dancing on the beach under the moonlight! And its safe. Time flies by though... Be aware! All of a sudden its 5 am and you have to get a tuk-tuk home - don't let them charge you 1000 rupees either! You might not stay all night, but you can say you did it! Its fun during the day as well... Snorkeling isn't all they say it is because most of the reefs are dead or dying... But you will see fish! You can swim to the right, around the rocks and theres another little beach! Check it out!
Small beach, rubbish everywhere, but probably great party place at night. Access a bit adventureous, walking up the hill to get back makes you sweat.

The beach spot is a trek down hill through uneven steps and well as the name suggests "a jungle" What you get to is a small beach with beautiful waters. Bunch of umbrellas and chairs strewn around and some sun beds. There is coral pieces here and there in the sand. It's pretty as long as you are here for a swim or some such -  just about facing the water all the time. The cafe or restaurant is insanely over priced. And really crappy food. Avoid. There is pretty much no loo. There is a commode with an open door. So forget it. The serving guys seem strange loonies. Carry cash. No cards accepted. Supplies come in via a jetty. So you won't find the cafe open before 10-11 in any case. Wear sturdy shoes to go downhill.or climb back up. It's a short 15 mins. Overall. It's a nice spot. But really. Ruined fully by the supposed so called cafe. Would I go again? No maybe not.

Place is OK to go in a day you have not much to do near Unavatuna. There are steps going towards big Japanese temple, small bar on the beach and a not very clean place for snorkeling. This is about it.
Great little cove to swim in with kids and for adults and kids to snorkel. Lots of coral and fishes to see.
We went here because of the reviews about how undiscovered it was, but it is not secluded anymore, very windy, not very good swimming - skip it

This beach is very nice, it is covered with sand and look like a real tropical paradise. There is a cafe on the beach that provides longes as well. On the left in the ocean there is nice place for snorkling, so if you have mask, you can watch interesting underwater life.

Jungle beach is a real trek and the walk is half the fun! It is a nice beach, but it's pretty crowded and not really worth the walk unless you've got a lot of time. The water is calm and easy swimming for kids. You can also see the Galle fort from the water which is a fun novelty.

If you can avoid it, do this. the only "pro" of this place is low waves. All the rest are "cons" - plastic rubbish in water, rubbish in sand, bad way (beated uneven stairs) to reach the place, loud music...
It is a good scret hideout beach. It is right under the Peace Pagoda. You will enjoy going through the uneven terrain and little jungle. One two bars.
Jungle beach could be a wonderful place but there is a lot of litter placed in the jungle by the bar owners and visitors. This is not right and should have changed asap.
Nice cove like setting and far nicer than the main beach, but a little crowded, although we were there in high season, we preferred white jungle beach as it was quieter.

Did the trek to get there only to find that this tourist trap is a few meters of sand filled with cigarette buds and trash - oh, and a bar/shack serving tourist priced beverages. Save yourself the tuk tuk or walk and don't visit this final resting place for rubbish.
it was quite an adventure to climb down to the beach. it was also fun to walk along from this end to the other end
hidden away in the jungle. A peaceful Place to relax and enjoy if it is not raining heavily.I suggest you take your food and drinks even tough there are few restaurants.

I enjoyed the path (took about 30 minutes) to Jungel beach more than the actual beach, because it was crowded. Swimming there  though was nicer than at the bigger Unawatuna beach, because the waves were smaller.

Lovely small bay perfect for swimming only basic beach bar available in area but completely over run with Russian's who aren't the friendliest of fellows traveller's and are loud and rude which ruined our visit we had to leave to escape them.
Lovely little beach, off the beaten track, lovely to swim in the ocean and enjoy the gorgeous natural beauty this area has to offer.

Unawatuna beach is far from the Galle avenue, a quiet beach with many nice restaurants (fresh fish, Italian, indian etc) and bungaloes. We stayed in a room right at the beach, above "yellow cafe". The sunset was magnificent from our balcony: the whole sky was painted red and purple! Next to our room we could find foot massage, breakfast, and drinks in a bar which was oppened 10 years ago by a young guy from Switzerland. Unawatuna is the best place in Lanka to relax for 3-4 days...

We were driving to unawatuna beach but somehow missed the turn and end up in jungle beach. We park a car on a private parking (very cheap) and from there it was 300-400 meters down to the beach. We were amazed! A little beach with white sand, not so many people, beach bar and music on all the time. Fresh food, fresh juices, crystal clear water - called this place paradise.
This beach is nice, far away from traffic and people there want to sell you stuff that you don't need, where there a bit late and heard its best between 9am and 3 pm with the sun.
Just next to the pagoda the beach is well indicated and very  clean. There are toilets too. It is rather small but at the end of the afternoon it is a peaceful place to go for a swim.
The beach is beautiful for pictures but not clean enough to swim. That's why we didn't spend much time there but hurried back to Unawatuna.
It's a nice llittle beach which is a bit of a hike to get to, but it's quite busy nowadays as it becomes more known to tourists. Nice restaurant. We went there for an hour or so just for a drink.
lovely small beach, water beautiful, but dont expect to have it to yourself. Many people, not much room.
Not a nice beach - full of rubbish and it's tiny. Too many people crammed in and Unawatuna beach is much nicer to sit on.

I come from a country were going to the beach is a summer routine. I came to Unawatuna beach with high expectations yet my expectations were not only met but exceeded. Three horizontal ligns, green jungle, white sand and turquoise crystal clear water. Warm water, gentle waves, clean sands and minimal crowds. I highly highly recommend it. No trip to Srilanka would be complete without visiting this beach.

The second one was overcrowded, first one was oke, but nothing special. Better though then the spoiled beach of unawatuna. Locals were already busy with an old water scooter. So I guess this place won't be quiet for long anymore...
Very cosy little beach which is hard to get to. There is one bar and a few toilets. There are some chairs one can lie on and the place was filled with locals when we were there. Very nice!

We were yesterday in Jungle Beach having read that is one of the best places in Sri Lanka for snorkeling. In fact it is a good place to swim, because the sea shore is protected from the high waves of this area; but the water is murky and therefore you can not see almost anything: you can just glimpse the dead barrier and some colorful fish.
Great little beach, swimming and snorkelling is good,  not many sun beds so get there early if you want one.  Food was nice. Hard work getting the steps after a few cold beers.

It is a nice little hike to the beach with some fairly steep and rocky areas and through some lovely vegetation.  We enjoyed seeing some homes of the locals on the way.  The best decision we made was to get there early in the morning - at around 7am.  At this time it was empty and the restaurant which basically takes up the entire beach (beach is very small) wasn't operating yet.  The water is very nice to swim in, with gentle waves.  We didn't like the view of buildings in the distance.

Beautiful beach, easy to find down a steep rocky hill but not accessible to those with mobility issues. We walked from unawatuna which took about 30 mins and was a lovely walk through jungle, we got to see huge iguanas on the walk! Music however loud and beach crowded, we preferred white jungle beach a little further along.

Great entrance into the water. Clean, no dangerous stones and other traps in the water. Simple but pleasant restaurant. Quite public, no go-go music and "animation". Beatuful forest around it, with monkeys, apes, birds, fishes, pink lotuses
Stick to the main beach at Unawatuna - it's quiet at the end of the Peace Pagoda. Lots of fun meeting the locals in the sea there away from the tourists.
A lovely beach with a beautiful sunset view..  really great place ,Very quite, with an excellent little restaurant situated on the beach.

A happy find at the end of a short walk through the jungle!  A lovely natural beach - much less commercial than Unawatuna - with one beach hut where good food and smoothies are served by friendly, flirtatious staff!  Don't miss the impressive beach party on Wednesday night.

A very small and busy beach, but one of the few in tephe areas which doesn't have waves making it ideal for swimming and snorkelling. Much of the coral is sadly destroyed, but there are still some good marine life to see. Get there early to avoid the crowd. The restaurant is good value.

The beach itself is quite small, and you only need to spend an hour or so there. What makes it worthwhile is the trek to the beach which takes you through the jungle. Beautiful scenery and we even saw monkeys and other animals along the way.
Unless you get a hero tuktuk driver its a fair walk down. The beach is small, shaded and busy. The place feels like a tourist trap and there are so many better places to go.

We visited Jungle Beach just after New Year's (Jan 2014). The tuk tuk ride there was a bit expensive (most likely due to the dodgy road or the fact a second fare back from another tourist may not happen). It was a bit of a hike down to the spot through some pretty lush vegetation and once on the beach it was clear that the festivities from New Year's Eve had taken its toll because there was rubbish everywhere (in the water and on the beach). We were pretty disappointed and didn't stay long (note: we assumed it was dirty from NYE - I hope it's not like that all the time). VJ beach a bit further up is much, much better. Clear and pristine water with gorgeous palm trees dotting the waterline.
We had two nights stops at Unawatuna and happend to take the pleasure being in the Jungle Beach, though the weather was rainy and cloudy. We wished if we had the sun shine !
Make sure you wear trainers,  once the road runs out, it a ramble of dirt trail and a rocks to the top, well worth it though, we took some great photos of the bay and surrounding areas

I went there today on recommendation from some other travellers. It's OK in that it's a much quieter beach than the others I had seen. Accessible via a short bush track, it's seclusion is an asset. Unfortunately when I went there I found the water to be pretty dirty. So didn't want to spend any time in the water. There is a little cafe/bar at the beach as well as a bunch of beach chairs which are available for use without being a patron of the bar. If you want something a bit quieter it might be worth a visit... But honestly I reckon you could find a quiet spot somewhere on unawatuna main beach and enjoy that more, and the water would be at least clean.

I went there because information on the net tells that it is a excellent site for snorkelling. Don't believe it, it is a joke! Very few corals and fishes can be seen swimming out from the beach. You won't have use for your snorkelling gear there. Apart from this, the beach is worth a visit. The signposted footpath from Unawatuna is nice a nice 45 min. walk.

We went on a fairly treacherous trek to get to this beach from our hotel and were quite disappointed when we got there The beach itself is not that nice, the water is quite murky and there is only one little kiosk that looks a bit sad and I wouldn't really order anything there The main beach is much nicer and much more happening there
We used to go to this beach - It was quieter then the public Unawatunna beach, it has everything you need to enjoy the ocean.

I enjoyed the trek to the beach more than the beach itself. It's very small and can be quite busy. The views from the top of the road at sunset are very special. There are lots of monkeys swinging from tree to tree enroute which is good fun to watch.

Even in very tough and out of city conditions - guys are very gentle and smiling. They serve very good fresh food, of course with frequent mistakes in comparison with European restaurant... But I do not care, I am in Sri Lanka:)

Jungle beach is an excellent small beach on the opposite side of the headland from Unawatuna. A good forty minute walk takes you through a bit of jungle down to this beach. Very quite, with an excellent little restaurant situated on the beach. Free sun loungers

We swam at Unawatana beach in the morning. To break up the day we walked to the end of the beach and up to the Pagoda on top of the small hill. Walking back down we saw a small road and a somewhat hidden sign pointing way to Jungle Beach. A very pleasant 20 minute walk to the beach. Reasonably well sign posted (only one spot we had to guess - we followed the mainish small road). Last 10 minutes is walking thru reasonably thick bush on a well marked path - even crossed a very small stream. The beach itself is very pretty but oh so small. Nice to dip in the water - we didn't eat at the restaurant there (it looked like all the beach ones, all very same same). There is a larger beach around from jungle beach that you can either swim around the point or stumble across the rocks. Overall, worth it if you keep in mind it's a nice walk, with a refreshing dip and a cold beer at the end of it.

It's such a shame that some people keep dumping their rubbish in the sea there, otherwise it would have been quite nice. It's a very dirty beach and you can see a lot of rubbish when snorkelling there.

It was our first time on this great beach. It was hidden to local tourists while it was popular with foreigners... somehow accidentally we went there and it was mind blowing and calm... i would recommend this place to anyone who loves beaches...

A beautiful strip of sand hidden in a bay at the end of the jungle... very clean beach, crystal clear blue water.. Take a jet ski ride and discover the surroundings, you'll be surprise with the beautiful hidden Buddhist temples that are scattered around
it was heavily raining but a less crowded place compared to Unawatuna. can take you food and eat and enjoy the beach. Couples are not encouraged to go there.

We visited both Jungle Beach and White beach next door. You walk down the hill which can be a little steep. The beaches are set within the rainforest, with nice sand and clean water. Both have beach huts so you can grab some food or a beach. Definitely worth a visit!

Jungle Beach is on the other side of the bay from the Old Fort in Galle.   You can only drive so far, then must dismount and walk down a trail through the jungle until you come to Jungle Beach, which is about 100 meters long.  It has a white sand beach and the water is relatively clean. There is a restaurant there, but we did not eat.   Just enjoyed a chilled bottle of Lion Beer, the favorite beer in Sri Lanka.
the place is a one of a kind. The location  is exquisite. You have to walk through a jungle to get to the beach. It's one of the best place for snorkeling and have a relaxing sea bath.

We grabbed a tuk tuk from unawatuna beach and asked to go to Jungle beach. Now we were taken to the smaller one and when we got there were quite disappointed. However we went for a walk across the coast and from there we saw another larger beach. How do we get there? Well from the small beach I swam! My boyfriend walked the rocky walk and it was worth it for the 10 minute swim. A much larger beach with a small local bar, few tourists and a fantastic sunset. To leave, we walked up the hill in the dark (take a torch) and found ourselves on the main road. When getting there, ask the driver to take you to the 'larger' jungle beach where you will get a better experience and you won't have to swim to it!
Great beach for surfers, but if you're not into surfing, your beach experience will be a bit limited as it's quite rough / strong waves waters. Lovely sunset here in the evenings.

A small beach, just a few meters from Pagoda, is probably not worth a visit. Unawatuna beach is probably busier, but very nice. If you would like to explore beaches, you can find maany really good ones on your way to Mirissa or Tangalle.
It was run by quite young locals but all good natured & on till late every Wednesday, cocktails in that cheap but beautiful setting and normally really busy peak times, 8/10

Water was pretty cloudy and only real snorkelling is around the rocks at the left hand side of the bay.  Slightly more fish than in Mirissa but probably not worth leaving mirissa to come here purely for snorkelling as we did
Ok Beach and ok service. Probably more interesting for the younger generation. we went back to Unawatuna after a short time there.
a really great place to unwind with the locals and enjoy a cold beer in the cove in between snorkelling along the rocks
Lovely walk down but the water had so much rubbish floating in it.  Didn't even have a swim. Juice was fine but nothing special.

This review is for Unawatuna beach. Not sure if it is  different. Although to reach this beach, you have to drive through forest so I think this the one. Water activities, cafes, bars, expensive as well as medium budget hotels opening to beach.. You name it and I think this beach has it all. Having a big area to itself, it can accommodate large number of people and yet not feel crowded. It is an enjoyable beach to be in. For Indian tourist to relate, it felt like Calungute/Baga beach of Goa.

My review is on Unawatuna Beach, I am not sure if it is also called Jungle Beach. One of the top 3 locations In Sri Lanka for sea bathing. You have to find the correct place to swim, or else some areas have broken corals and rocks which hurt you. I would recommend the place next to a small guesthouse/hotel called Sun n Sea. Waters are amazingly calm and there is a nice beach stretch over there which is not extremely crowded.
secluded beach with a trek through the jungle to get to it.  lots of locals on this beach... kids having fun in the water and playing local music.
The drive to jungle beach was precarious to say the least, not for those with a faint heart in the tuk tuk. Once there, it was just a group of young travellers. We stayed for a beer and left

If you need a little, not too strenuous exercise, take the walk over the hill. Not recommended for the less physically able. On arrival though you will be confronted by a shallow little beach, rocks at both ends. Overpriced & not very good beach bar. We're you to miss it, you wouldn't be deprived of anything. Amazing what a name like "Jungle Beach" will do for the imagination.

After walking up a hill (Which you could take the tuk tuk as well), and walking down a rough jungle path (Which you can't take a tuk tuk or anything else that has a wheel) for 5-8min, then you end up in this tiny beach. Yes, technically it's hidden, but when 100 users looking for "hidden" at the same time, it's not really exclusive anymore is it... Adding up the fact that the water is not really clean, the beach is trashed, I really do not think it's worth visiting this place AT ALL.

Jungle beach is not hard to find, you just need to follow the signs and you'll be fine. The walk to jungle beach is a little up hill so the swim on the other side is very rewarding. The walk is probably around 25minutes. You can be dropped in two different spots by tuk Tuks. I would recommend walking the first time and seeing the route for yourself rather than being driven. The main jungle beach is where the jungle path leads you to it is busy with a little restaurant. If you walk around the rocks to the second beach it's a lot less crowded and it also has another restaurant. It's also nice break from the normal beach which is a lot smaller and more crowded.

This is a lovely beach with a nice little restaurant and bar. Free sun beds to those who are eating and drinking. We found that there were big groups of tourists beings brought here which spoilt it a bit, drunken Russian girls taking constant photos of each other in bikinis was a bit wearing. We did come here in the late afternoon a couple of times for a bite to eat and a drink and it was much more pleasant. Local kids playing in the see and the bus trips had gone back to their hotels! Party night was great for drinks and the track is lit up, so we could walk back to our hotel. We didn't stay long, just long enough for it to go dark and to see the sun set. I'm sure party animals would have made the most of it!
Is this place so popular....i really have absolutely no idea. Anyway...great marketing. The temple is worth a visit but.
Unawatuna beach is much better! So many people here in a small area. And the water is not so clean as in Unawatuna
It's good if you want to stay away from hustle and bustle of the main beach area.theres a small restaurant and its s great spot for snorkeling
Very small and cozy beach with a small snack bar in one corner. Exacting walked to the beach with a lot of monkeys who think they can eat your IPhone.
Sheltered spot so lovely swimming. Good food at the open air restaurant on the beach. Difficult decent and accent on a rough road

Very dirty - garbage all over. The water was of the weird color because of mix of mud/sand/garbage. There was a "Jungle beach restaurant" but the restaurant is just a little wooden hut but very pricey. No shower and bathroom of course. The only good memory about that beach was to watch after monkeys stealing bananas from that "restaurant"

Just beware there are two "Jungle Beaches"  next to each other and this one next to the Japanese Pagoda is the real deal, as we accidentally went to the other one by mistake and what a nightmare that was. No toilets, you just pee in the jungle, that along with a very steep rocky/steps to get there and back plus dogs fighting on the beach etc... So make sure you get the right one here, as for us we arrived on the back of a Tuk, Tuk which cost around 400 Rupees one way. You can either walk here in the 90 degree heat plus humidity if you want and arrive drenched in sweat with your tongue hanging out? Or take the easy way ?  Our Tuk, Tuk, driver upon seeing us attempting to walk there stopped and flung out the local Sri Lankan family he was carrying in the middle of nowhere, and ushered us in, it would seem us tourists pay more here talk about embarrassing.? Upon arriving you walk down a short rocky path and do wear sensible foot wear, and there is a real sense that tourism has began to flourish here out of a simple idea which is evident by the people visiting now which is a great shame. As for the restaurant well, it's slightly pricey but you'd expect that. We had some lunch and I had the best seafood cocktail I've ever had no kidding, this along with some beers went down a real treat and drowned out the screaming noise from some local lads below. Who were getting bored and were now attempting to drown each other, oh what joy.!   Thankfully they left later and we went on to the beach and the FREE wooden deck chairs which were quite empty, I did try the snorkelling but, the water was way too cloudy to see anything wrong time of year I think.?  There was also a bit of rubbish floating around too and there's nothing worse that makes me want to swim faster than when I see a half eaten sandwich or fag end floating past me.! Going to the toilet is also an education as it's a wooden cubicle with no running water just a bucket outside to wash with and flush, which begs the question just where exactly does the waste flow?  Oh yes, the beach water you're swimming in just remember to keep your mouth tightly shut.!    You might also have some company in here with the hermit crabs , chipmunks, monkeys, spiders etc, just look upon it as an experience. However, the beach area is really nice and you do get many photo opportunity's plus the views across to Galle are good, as for the restaurant staff they're all very friendly and they do have a really simple menu which suits all tastes and you can guarantee the fish is fresh here, as one of the guys actually asked me if I wanted to join him for a night fishing trip, looking at his dug out canoe held together with washing nylon and the thought of bobbing about in a shipping channel in the Indian ocean made me make my declining apologies and discreetly take a step back and rejoin the wife. You can also do boat trips from here which takes you around the bay if you get bored, and don't forget to visit the Japanese Pagoda on the way back before you jump into a Tuk, Tuk..!
500 rupees to get there by tuk-tuk from Unawatuna center, it is peaceful, like a lagoon. The snorkeling isn't good though.

Naomi Klein probably wouldn't like this place, becouse it's rather a beach bar than a regular beach. The place is deserted, quite small, in nice surrounding. Water a bit polluted: many plastic bags. A lot of coral residues on the shore. Restaurant is very overpriced. Prices of the food in the menu are not the actual prices.

Before you even get to the beach, you will enjoy the beautiful and breathtaking greenery that surrounds the road to Jungle Beach. The beauty of the scenery once you get to the beach was beyond description and I was able to take many amazing pictures down there. Worth a visit.

love the place. one of the best beaches I've visited in Sri Lanka. located between Unawatuna and Galle just at the foot of the Japanese peace pagoda in Rummassala. it lives up to its name have to go down a jungle to reach the beach. shallow ware, golden sand and all that follows for a blissful beach love affair. The beach is nice, it's swimmable, not rough and just the right size. When there are too many people, however, it becomes like any other crowded beach "crowded". :D one minus point is that people are taking the place for granted. the jungle around the area is ruined by people who have visited the place. plastic to alcohol bottles to cigarette buds it's getting ruined. over all a place to enjoy the sea. perfect!

Better go with a crowd. No offence, but most insanely drunk people freak me out and you get bunches of those here. But if you're with a group of people, it's ok. The hike towards it is pretty fun and if the people at the restaurant there tell you there's no water to have a wash after sea bathing, doesn't matter, you can still do a small hike to the top and have a wash for Rs. 40/ (Rs.100/ if you're a foreign tourist)

This hidden treasure was discovered by us about two years and visited there again this year January. It's hard to believe that not many locals go there but so many foreign tourist are at this beach. It's small but clean beach with no touts around unlike other places. A unique Sea food restaurant is located there but it is bit pricey. There is basic toilet there but best if you can avoid using it. The beach is surround by the jungle and waters are quite calm compared to Unawatuna beach which is on the other side of the bay. Lovely place to take a swim and rest under the shady tress which very close to the beach. There is a Japanese temple top of the hill where one can park the vehicle there and descend about 500 meters through the shady path. No wheel chair access.

I love this place, though I feel now it is a little too crowded some days. The beauty of the beach was in its secluded pristine quality. At least two methods of access, one which is not easy to navigate but much more fun. Good place to go discover and lounge around.

We came one morning and fell asleep on the chair in the shaded spot on the beach. We had a swim but be careful of the rocks they can be sharp underneath. You have to look out for dark spot and avoid it. We swim towards the right side and it was so pleasant. Water is not too cold. Really had a great time.

went here on a walk from our hotel (about 2km away).  Was a nice walk, though a bit steep.  On the way here we encountered a snake (big for us, because we come from NZ and have no snakes!) and a giant monitor lizard!  Both were a bit intimidating, but was pretty cool. There were monkeys down by the beach too which was cool.  Beach is pretty and looked inviting for a swim.  We bought a soft drink, sat down in the sun for 20 minutes then left as we were staying at a nice resort anyway.  Well worth the trip if you're in Galle/Unawatuna area

Loved hanging out at this beach surrounded by beautiful forest and palm trees. The bar there is quite nice with reasonably priced fresh juices and smoothies and they provide the sun loungers. They also have a restaurant. As the beach is literally in the forest there was even a group of monkeys showing up while we were sunbathing. Swimming at this beach was nice since it is protected by the bay and waves are not as intense. We walked there from Unawatuna following the signs which took about 20min through the forest. Would definitely come back for their all day DJ party on Wednesdays if we had time and dance on the beach.

The walk is about 1 1/2 hours and is hilly, alternatively take a tuk tuk,. Small quiet bay with a bar, we paid a tuk tuk to get there charged us 1000 rupee for return trip.  Not sure if it was worth it.

The beach has all the makings of a beautiful, quaint and exotic location. However, the herd of tourists smoking and eating packaged food made it quite off putting. Had a paddle in the sea and saw a lot of cigarette buts and general bits of rubbish. Stayed for an hour then went back to the main beach which I found to be much nicer.
Sheer beauty and isolation ! Just love this place ! The water is shallow enough to go a decent bit far out and  got lots of corals too... Great for quiet sun bathing !

I've been 2 times a jungle beach with family and friends. Very nice beach, very sheltered, soft sand, a great restaurant on the beach (fantastic prawns, fresh tropical fruit juices to scream), not crowded (March 10). The only drawback the lack of clarity of the water, which made it almost impassable snorkeling. In my opinion one of the best beaches in Southern Sri Lanka, especially the fact that it is sheltered from strong winds and high waves.
If you stay at Dionis Villa, this is a must, clean water, nice for snorkling and good restaurant with fresh fish every day.
Great fried rice! Friendly prompt service. Lovely setting, overlooking the beach. Relaxed atmosphere
Lots of tourists, many smoking, nothing to rave about! Still water, small beach, lots of deck chairs, litter in the water, not a fan!
The walk to the Jungle Beach is very nice, great views, the beach itself is mostly completely empty and wonderful.
Nice little beach with clear water away from the Unawatuna beach. It's a great place for relaxing. You can swim without a problem.

You can reach the beach by foot, NO need to pay for a tuk-tuk. You walk on a beautiful, small path through the jungle. The path is marked by several signs along the way. Unfortunately, snorkeling was not possible (mid September) due to bad visibility. The beach is very, very small and dominated by an overpriced snack hut. Even though there were not many people on the beach, it felt crowded. It's not possible to spread your towel in the sand, you can only use a few sunchairs which are quickly taken. We had expected more.
You have to take a three wheeler to get there, but the little beach is beautiful! I do not recommend the food at the restaurant on the beach...it was not bad but not worth the money.

The beach is tiny and the sea there is packed with people swimming absolutely everywhere even in low season... The walk there from Unawatuna is really nice though, follow the signs "jungle beach" but don't wear flip flops to walk there, you have to walk in the rocks uphill and then down to the other side so trainers might be a good idea. The walk is not that long at all but you might hurt your feet along the way. You'll be able to walk up to the Dagoba which is 5 min from the beach, this is a short but enjoyable walk and a great point of view. Just don't stay too long at jungle beach.
The little Beach is a great walk away from una. The Beach is beautiful,and a great place for relaxing - in the Winther it Might be great for snorkeling.

We spent a day at jungle beach which was a nice change from Unawatuna. It's a really lovely natural beach but make sure you go early as it's only tiny with limited lounges and places to sit. There is a food shack there for lunch and drinks selling fresh fish. Food was nice, best cup of tea so far in Sri Lanka!
The beech was ok - there was a restaurant which served very nice food and drink. However the water was very dirty, lots of rubbish and debris which the restaurant staff were cleaning up.
One if the amazing beach in Sri Lanka ❤️ bit hard to reach but thousand time worth to reach ❤️❤️❤️ No words have the experience 👍👍👍
Small beach near Unawatuna. It's a bit of a hike to get to it if on foot. There is a small cafe there too.
You had to walk for a bit, but there's directions all the way and the hike was a part of the adventure. Nice little beach with a beach resturant.
Some years ago was really a secret and hidden spot where to have a relaxing day on the beach, now is full of people, dirty, and noisy. Really pity.

I was positively surprised since there was no additional charge for the deckchairs. We enjoyed staying on the beach since it was not crowded. There is also a small cottage on the beach and you can have a meal or a cocktail. Once a week they organize beach party.

when you are walking arround Unawatuna, you always hear about this beach but most of the tourist don't get the chance to visit as it is a bit unreachable unless you want to try a small adventure. You can only reach that place by foot and going down th hill, walking in rivers and following small signs !! when you reach there it is totally different, the beach is amazging, clean, surrounded by trees and complete privacy with a small restaurant who can prepare you some delicious sea food !

This was the only beach we visited in the Galle area after it was recommended by our hotel.  It is a nice small beach with a cafe where you can buy food and juices.  They have a many wooden sun lounges that you can use, however the expectation is that you buy something from the cafe.  The beach was clean (for Ski Lanka) and located in the bay so the water was much calmer than other beaches we had driven past.
A great walk through Jungle to get to a perfect beach with palm trees and monkeys and a very nice cafe
This place of a piece of heaven  years back. Shallow lagoon. Great sandy beach.miniature of pasikuda today . But now beach is spoilt . too many shacks what they call restaurants.

Whilst it's a bit of a trek down the unkept jungle path it's well worth it. Wear sturdy foot ware to avoid a twisted ankle. My wife wore flip flops which made it more difficult. A bar on the beach gave quick & welcome relief and it's a tranquil spot. If you head back up the cliff after sunset then a torch would be useful.
So peaceful and adventurous. There are cafes by the beach as well. You can spend the day here. Take bug repellent when going through the jungle. Very nice experience.

That's a small beach in a Jungle. When we were there was full of locals. Easy to find if you have a scooter just pay attention and don't miss the turn from the main road (there is a sign). From the certain point you will need to walk through the pass. Nothing really special.

Tuk tuk driver went to a certain point and then you walked down the hill to discover a secluded beach.  Feels like only few people know about Jungle beach. So peaceful, great food (fresh fish of your choice), friendly staff. Great views and during peak season they throw great parties.
Very pretty! Take a tuk tuk to get there and walk back through the jungle path (ask around where it goes because it is not very evident) Note that it can get very crowded on this small beach.
a small beach off the beaten track. Take insect repellent and money as there is a shop which sells cold drinks. we walked there from Anwatuna beach.

Sea is nice here- no waves- you can swim without problems.here are sun benches on the beach free of charge. There is also a small restaurant threre where you can buy water- you don't have to carrry water all the way. The walk from Unawatuna is nice and easy to find.

it is a 15 min hike from the main beach and I believe it must be perfect early in the morning or later in the evening (though be careful to bring a torch or to leave before darkness). But during the day there were too many locals shouting and playing football and volleyball, which would be fine normally, but the beach is really very small, so it was a bit annoying. Overall nice but would not go there twice
Quiet and laid back with friendly café best approached on foot from hotel avoid weekend when local lads bongo away and booze. We went out of season.

We followed the signs from the end of Unawatuna Beach with little idea of just where we would end up. It was a hike up and over, then down fairly rough terrain. The views were stunning when we had them. The beach had a good food and beverage bar, with slow but worthwhile service. We had to wait for a table as lots of people had arrived by boats ahead of us. The swimming was good and we had chairs in the shade on the beach. We walked out to the main road in Unawatuna and that was another adventurous climb, though we could have chosen a yuk yuk ride down from the top.

Travellers always aspire to go to places where nobody have been before.  When a traveller carries a Lonely Planet, he or she has a sense of entitlement that they are about to come across something so rare or so forbidden.  However, whenever they get to those places and they see another person carrying a Lonely Planet book, you tend to feel like a fool.  And I suppose Jungle Beach is like that, a Fool's Paradise.  To be fair, on the record, I didn't find out about Jungle Beach from Lonely Planet book but from people that I met along the road, locals and foreign travellers alike.  You can either take a boat there from Unawatuna beach or that you could drive there or you could even get Tuk-Tuk there too.  Because I don't have any expectation of what Jungle Beach is supposed to be, I don't get underwhelmed when I saw the place.  Suffice to say that the journey there has been interesting, trekking through shrubs and rocks.  By the time you get to your destination, no doubt you would be drenched in sweat and right in front of you is a shack that sells beverages at a very inflated price.  For me, I didn't linger long apart from snapping pictures and off my merry way again.  I can't help but feeling that the whole thing is a cop out.  When you are at Galle, you are to see a white stupa on a high ground at a distance.  Jungle Beach is right underneath that.  In another three years time, these are the possibilities: Jungle Beach would become so commercialised that a proper road would be built there to service overseas tourists and that uncontrolled development would encroach upon the area and the beach is going to be gone forever.  It's already happening that way.  Sigh~commercialisation.

Please note that some guys have signposted to a second Jungle beach very close to the Japanese temple. Do not take that path. You end up in a beautiful beach with a shack and the water is very rough. There is a drunk/drugged guy who is selling drinks there and it is not very safe for females. The real Jungle beach is before you arrive at the temple. That is why you see different opinions on the Jungle beach on this site.

We spent a week here and every day was great. Staff is too friendly at first, but once they get to know you they are more relaxed and pleasant. We were very happy with rooms and territory, beach was also exceptional. The only cons I can think of is the prices at the restaurant, they seemed a bit too high when compared to local joints. A lunch for two at hotel restaurant would set us back 5000 rupees, while at Trincomalee center we were having a similar one for 700 rupees. Also there weren't enough fruits in the hotel, a plate of fruits (3 small slices of melon, 3 cubes of pineapple and 3 pieces of papaya) would cost us 1100 rupees, so we just went to Trincomalee and bought 3 pineapples, 4 mangos and 20 rambutans for the same 1000 rupees. Don't hesitate to take a snorkeling tour to Pigeon Island, our guide was Shamm and he was great. Showed us turtles, sharks and other tropical fish. Also, there is a good photo spot on the top of the island, Shamm will show you the way.

This place is like a little hidden paradise. The trek to get to the place makes it more interesting and feels like your in that film called the island. Once you get there this is a little paradise. Not even many locals know about this place or don't come here because of the access..but if your like me and like a bit of a trek..try this place it won't cost a penny...it's magical!

There are two ways to get to beach, try taking the one through the jungle. Once you get to the last sign for jungle beach going downwards, suggest going straight instead of downwards. Great views on the sea side rocks and then you can trek through a side path onto the beach. There is only one shack at the beach.

We came here after our trip to Galle to enjoy the beach and have lunch.  The lunch was average and the beach was a tropical paradise.  It truly is picture postcard perfect although the sea is very choppy with a massive undercurrent - do not go out of your depth!!!

one of the nicest beach in srilanka . the water was clean & cool, lot of shady spots so you can avoid the sun .Good place to have beer & swim with friends .& if you are looking for more adventure there is a hike road to the beach. simply loved it
When we went the beach bar was closed (New Year)and the beach was dirty and we felt uncomfortable. Stayed about 20 mins and got a small boat back

Pleasant enough cove, if it weren't for all the tourists, as the boat trips come here, and it's the secret place that EVERYONE knows. The little cafe is terrible service. The beach is okay but when the tide is in there's not that much sand to sit on. The snorkelling was almost non existent. Low visibility, hardly any coral. The few fish that were there were right in amongst the rocks on the left side. The tuk tuk drivers really sting you to come here, make sure you already have one organised to collect you.

This beach is nice, the central part is clean, there is a nice shadow so the sun wont burn you. It was not crowded and the toilet was suprisingly clean, but we were here in April. We came there with our tuk-tuk since it is quite a long way to walk when it is so hot. On the top of the road to the beach, there is huge Peace Pagoda, good place to see. The road to the beach was ok, a 5 minute walk through the jungle, it was not as bad as we read here, I think they reinforced it with sand bags, so it is not slippery. The restaurant staff offers sunbeds on the beach if you buy a few drinks there.

The best of Unawatuna beaches, hidden away in the jungle. A bit commercialized now, but still a must see. There is a small restaurant right at the beach where you can grab a beer while you chill. Snorkeling excursions are available for a nominal fee, not much coral to see, but plenty of coral fish.

You can easily get to this beach by boat or by tuk-tuk from Unawatuna where we stayed. The beach is clean, and every Tuesaday night there seems to be a beach party ( which we missed). We went there for snorkling. The variety of fish is fair enough, but due to rainfalls the previous days the water was pretty troubled and the sight wasn't that good. Since we snorkeled for a week around Pigeon Island we might be totally spoiled, anyway. It is well worth seeing and I would go there again if I stayed in Unawatuna or Galle.
Small beach area. Restaurant very good, fresh fish cooked to order. Ok but not amazing! Be prepared for local stray dogs wandering on the beach. They may lay under your snubbed, but won't bother you.
A hidden gem, tucked away but only a short tuk tuk ride. Feels like you are discovering a hidden beach

Easy and beautiful walk through the jungle on an easy pathway to a delightful little beach. Pure water, sunbeds available for the cost of a drink at the 'restaurant' good deal. Be warned the restaurant only serves juices, water and some spirits- no food!

After seing pictures of the beach we decided that we must see it - it looked fantastic - a patch of sand surounded by jungle. In reality it is a just a nice beach together with sunbeds, flags and restaurants and quite crowded, too. So much for expectations. You can come there by foot (about 30 minutes from Unawatuna - but beware it is not an easy trek in flip-flops - use common sense and wear decent shoes because it is not a walk in the park but it does offers beautifull vistas) or take a tuk-tuk.

We were escorted by friends to what was to be a magical beach destination and bar off the Rummassala hill just off the Galle highway entry point off the main road. It was easy enough to reach and a slight adventure too climbing down the well-worn jungle path to the bay. This place seems like you have landed in a truly secretive place. It was quite packed and as locals we were definitely a minority. There were kids of all ages as well. The water looked very welcoming and safe to swim and the numerous country flags posted on the rocks was a very neat touch I thought. I guess the wonder wore its welcome once you engage the Jungle Beach bar staff who looked at us like we were not welcome there. When we asked for a table they said it’s only available for lunch whereas numerous foreigners were camped sipping drinks sans lunch or any snacks for that matter and there were free tables… We shrugged this off as we were dying for a cool dip after a 6hr whale watching saga. We of course proceeded to order a hefty bunch of appetizers and beers. Noticeably outshining anyone else on the beach, and some of whom had obviously brought their own fruits and crisps along! Of course that could be due to the visibly poor conditions of the kitchen! Although one item the omelet was ultra salty the rest of the food was ok – the passion juice we got was watered down and wasn’t that great. They tried to sell us a small fish for 2000rupees and a massive prawn for 1200rs. Prices you’d get at much cleaner gallefort establishments for the same. Due to the poor service and the treatment we got we decided not to lunch there and move to the fort instead after the swim. I would discourage anyone from going to this place mainly due to a few reasons 1. Discriminatory practices 2. Poor hygiene of food prep 3. High prices 4. an utterly disgusting & unsafe toilet! If you end up there do enjoy the lovely beach and do take your own snacks!
It is a nice secluded beach, but it's quite crowded. Snorkeling is good with a huge variety of fish.

nice setting and very clear water, the bar on the beach is convenient and the staff frienfdly. A bit too crowded (it's one of the few beaches where you can swim) but alltogether a nice place to spend a day
Lovely beach. Free sun loungers , although no mattress or umbrellas Quite a hike from the town but Tuk-Tuks are available as you come up from the beach
Persevere and you will be glad you did.  This is a little oasis.  Long may it stay that way.  You can snorkel and chill out here.
Great place to hiking. also small restaurants there to refresh. very beautiful scenic view of galle city there
just ask your Tuktuk driver where to climb down. There are two paths leading either to the lonesome or to the 'crowdy' beach with small restaurant
Nice and scenic small beach, with calm and clear water but a bit crowded. Vegetation offers shade. There is a small restaurant, food was good.

Relatively less crowded beach, Few years back it was very empty and non commercialized, But we went there today (March 2014) it was way crowded than expected. Also you have beach beds , food and drinks available now in the beach. So it's not calm as it used to be but still worth a try. If you going there buy foods from somewhere else and come. You can buy lunch, drinks from there but it's overpriced and not tasty.

We walked over from Unawatuna beach for a change of location.  The beach is small, and on our visit just comfortably full with a mix of foreign adults and families with children. There are signs for toilets ( I didn't visit them) and a small restaurant. Prices did not seem excessive given the walk in only location. We didn't use the snorkel rental services because the mouth pieces looked very worn and dirty. There are a limited number of wooden lounge chairs. There is some litter along the paths ( along with some monkeys). We could all probably pitch in to help with this. We'll probably go back another day.

along trek for a small over crowded strip of beach,one shack offering overpriced food and drinks hard wooden sunbeds lots of rubbish nothing going for it ,after the long trek people put up with it rather than walk back straight away.
small rocky piece of sand in isolated position down rocky path - just not worth the effort of getting there.

Would have been a beautiful little beach... Unfortunately Sri Lankans don't feel the need of taking their picnic rubbish back with them. There are plenty of bottles (even broken glass!), plastic bags etc. The restaurant also doesn't bother about keeping it clean... They pile up the rubbish and burn it (and this is supposed to be a wildlife sanctuary). I have seen a  SL family having a very big picnic and then leaving everything behind :( I noticed that SL citizens don't care about keeping their coutry clean (they throw garbage from bus and car windows :/) SHAME SHAME SHAME on you Sri Lankans!!! Practical info: there are actually two Jungle beaches and two restaurants. You can access them by taking a rocky path. The JB closer to the pagoda is probably beter for snorkeling, but there are many urchins, so be carefull :)

Beautiful beach in a quiet cove and a snorkeling attraction, but the reefs are in a sad state. Dead and chrushed by guest walking all over and water scooters soaring thru them up on the beach. You can still see a lot of colorful fishes and the beach is wonderful. The walk there from the main road is nice thru the herbal mountain.

Nice beach with clear water and places with shadow. Cafe (note that they cook very slowly). But no toilet. Half an hour pleasant walk from Unawatuna. Advice: there are 2 beaches there, you'll need to go a few min further to the big beach.
the best beach we ' ve been in Sri Lanka in 3 weeks, nice walking to reach it but very nice could be busy because is not so big

Best thing about this beach is the walk to it on the track from unawatuna. Once there it is crowded and the least impressive view to the built up coast opposite. Overpriced tuk tuks on way back if you want to go by road. Avoid.

We were there about 10 am, and there were already too many people there. The beach in unawatuna is better. There were also rubbish and plastic both in the water and on the beach. Not a good experience.

I guess in the past the beach was remote and beautiful, but now it is not. Everybody in Unawatuna told us that we should go, so even after reading the mixed reviews we went. The tuk tuk drivers have a business there, so they charge good money for a short distance. We paid 700 LKR for a round trip. To get to the beach you need to go up a hill and there is not a lot of space for walking, so a tuk tuk is convenient. After walking down the hill from the tuk tuk parking lot and finally getting to the beach we were disappointed. The bay is very small, about 25 meters long, and there were dozens of people on the restaurant’s sun loungers, it was really crowded. We were already there, so we tried to enjoy our time swimming. There were a couple of boats that passed through the bay while we were there. A terrible gasoline smell came from the boats. I took my snorkel with me but there was no visibility, the few coral I saw was completely dead. There were only a few fish near the rocks.  I do not recommend spending money or time going to this beach. It is really an average place, far and crowded. The beach in Unawatuna is not very different and the beach in Mirissa or Hikkaduwa are much better.
Nice little beach away from the main Unawatuna beach. Much more sheltered than the main beach. Better for snorkeling although not great.

Getting to Jungle beach itself is an adventure. You can either trek all the way from unawatuna beach through jungles or you can get a tuk tuk to drop you off at a point from where you can walk to the beach via an easier trek. The beach was crowded but the warm water and the white sand made it up for that. You can rent a snorkel for around Rs. 300 for an hour from the tourist trap restaurant on the beach and go look at corals. There is a comparatively quieter jungle beach no. 2 on the other side of this beach that you can access by walking over the rocks that you see nearby. A nice place to spend the whole day if you don't mind the crowd or spending an overpriced meal for your lunch at the restaurant nearby.

Five years ago, this beach was a beautiful little hidden oasis away from the hustle and tourist trap that Unawatuna has quickly become. The road to the beach didn't exist, and only a small winding path could take you there, deterring most tourists while enticing those adventurous enough to make the effort. A few years ago however, the Sri Lankan man who owned this land was approached by a Russian investor, and so this beautiful beach became today's Russian disaster. The food is overpriced, the beach itself crowded to the brim by 11 and even the water, which is beautifully clean and has a great visibility most days, is filled with 2-4 glass bottom boats trying to coax tourists into a ride to 'see' fish you can see just snorkeling a few meters down the coast. The cafe has placed sun beds on every inch of beach, leaving nearly no room for those not willing to pay for a spot when you could just as easily spread your towel on the sand. To the right of jungle beach there is another stretch of sand only accessible by swimming or climbing over the rocks; for a while this was a welcome escape for tourists not willing to give in to the Russian monopoly. This 'secret spot' however, has, over the past year, also been inhabited by an equally overpriced cafe and on some days can closely resemble jungle beach.
