The continuous stream of tourists, especially families, is allowing this to continue happening, and soon these beaches will be just as ruined as those in unawatuna, so please, for the sake of preserving something beautiful, don't give them the satisfaction' and look elsewhere for your little piece of Sri Lankan paradise. I would reccomend getting a Tuk tuck and doing the cost to galle where you will find many small deserted beaches if you are looking right.
A bit too busy for my liking, but there are boat trips and a bar and restaurant.  Overall an interesting find

Nice way to spend half a day. Do try to walk from Unawatuna - only takes 15-20mins and not worth getting a tuk-tuk. One bar/restaurant on beach serves food/drink at same prices/quality as rest of Una beach bars. Snorkelling wasn't the best - low visibiloty, dead coral, minimal life. Some nice colourful fish.

There are 2 beaches here. We got a tuk tuk from Galle and were dropped off along from the Japanese pagoda, from where we walked down a jungly path to the main jungle beach. This was crowded (mostly Russians) and not great, with the usual litter lying around, some in the water. It wasn't easy to find a nice spot to sit, and the area next to the restaurant was unpleasant as the restaurant had smokey burners/ barbecues on the go (and that smell of paraffin). We were aware there was a second beach so, we decided to explore the other side of the rocks (west side) and found another that was much quieter, cleaner and nicer. There was a small cafe, but it was only just opening up for the day. There was still some litter here and there, but there seemed to be no getting away from that! Anyway, it was a pleasant spot to relax for an hour or so. We found a path leading up to the main road (track!) so we did not need to double back. We had a walk up to the Japanese pagoda, and then a stroll down to the main road. However, there were tuk tuks going up and down the track so transport was not a problem. The Sri Lankan authorities do not appear to care about keeping their beaches clean and rubbish free, as we found in many places.

Jubgle Beach is a tiny little beach next to Unavatuna. Not too bad, but services offered are fare from what's been promised and expected. We were assured about mind blowing unickness of the place and true "isolation". In fact, you can see Galle across the bay and there was some litter in the water.
Don't go there unless your Russian ! Awful little beach with a nice little bar that the Russians seemed to monopolise while I was there ! Really don't bother
We went on a Sunday, so lots of locals as well as tourists. The bar is very scruffy and none too clean. The water is great, though you need to watch out for the jet skis.
nice little beach hidden away from the masses. nice relaxed vibe to it and good snorkelling along the cliffs. however the view is not great, not a lot of space with only a few deck chairs.

Bit of a hike through the jungle and over the cliff but well worth the effort.  No hawkers on the beach.  Small but very clear, calm waters, sandy beach good for a snorkel. Popular with families. Has some sun loungers, the water comes up quite high at high tide so doesn't leave much of a beach or space! Has a restaurant which we decided would not be so great to eat at, also has extremely slow service.

Walking to jungle beach through the bushes expected the white isolated beach. There is a busy restaurant with russian signs and the beach is full of people. Next time I would rather travelled to Mirissa beach.
The beach was fine its not a moan but its only small but can get a bit crowded but great for a sheltered swim for children and adults alike.
Walked to this beach eraly in the morning before sun worshippers were up.  Very nice beech with a nice-looking beach bar
you can go by boat from Unawatuna beach or by tuk tuk up the hill and then walk the path down through the jungle. Very nice hidden beach.

Really nice place to go to! The food is especially good and well priced. The atmosphere is really nice. If you're going from Unawatuna to Jungle Beach by boat , try to go with a fellow named 'Sudu', he's the best man you'll meet in Sri Lanka, guaranteed.

Definitely worth making time to visit. A very nice, scenic hike via residential road and rocky trail leads to a wonderful spot to spend a few hours. The restaurant/bar offers everything you'd need from meals to drinks, even all-night dance parties if that's your thing. Great snorkelling, very few waves so great for kids.

We happened to go on Poya day when there are a lot of local families on the beach. While it certainly wasn't quiet it was quite fun to watch the children play! The beach is good for swimming and has a good amount of shade. I am not a fan of the restaurant. They just decided on the spot what they could not be bothered to make which happened to be all the things that I wanted. I then ended up with the tuna sandwich and that day was the only time I ended up with diarrhoea on the entire trip.

The jungle beach was an average experience. After trudging through the heat to get to the beach, we reached the beach and realized there was a lot of people there. The plus is that it was certainly not as busy as the main Unawatuna beach. It was quite small. I wouldn't rush back but I'm glad we made the effort.

This is a lovely little bay just to the West of Unawatuna, with a busy beach-bar and restaurant.  Loungers are plentiful and free to use if you patronise the bar or restaurant. However, the beach is very popular with groups of Russian tourists who are both noisy and aggressive in wanting to use the loungers even if you happen to be on them already - a most uncomfortable experience.  The restaurant food is well cooked and service efficient even when very busy. There is a lot of litter on the beach with discarded paper sweet wrappers and plastic bags finding their way into the waves to wrap around you when swimming.  The best snorkelling is around the rocks to the East end of the bay although the range of marine life is fairly unremarkable.
The beach is great for snorkelling and swimming. Best to head to the second quieter beach away from the crowds. Lovely snorkelling and the water is stunning :)

Nice beach for kids to swim at, but it gets crowded. Restaurant was nice and prices the same as the rest of Unawatuna - we got lunch for two adults and three kids in 20 minutes which was a first in SL!
can do a nice hike through roomassele..you can visit peace pagoda on the way.. spectacular view from there

Close to Galle but crowded and bit dirty, good to have a look but not a place for spending all day. nice hike to the beach, better than taking a Tuk Tuk, lots of monkeys in the trees as you walk up through the mountains.

This is really such a cool place to go swimming. You park on top of the mountain and trek through the jungle down to the hidden bay. Unfortunately on most days there are so many people it is too crowded. But if you pick the correct day, you have the entire beach to yourself!

Deserted is certainly NOT a word I would use to describe Jungle Beach. It might be better in the down season but in December it's completely overrun with tourists and sunbeds. That being said, the beach bar is nice and they rent out (slightly old and slightly broken) snorkeling material. The snorkeling is not amazing but you get to see a few nice fish. I would recommend going to the next beach. Follow the sign for "Jagle Bech" up on the road or just go through the "jungle" from Jungle Beach to your right when looking at the sea. It's much calmer, and has mainly locals.

Good walk over from Unawatuna, but rubbish increased over 3 weeks we were there. Our last visit was marred by aggressive Russians psyching us off the sun loungers. No idea if they were a tour party or individuals, but atmosphere spoilt. Gets very crowded at weekends.
Thought it would be quiet but packed with locals setting up a disco which was not what we expected after walking down a dirt track for 40 minutes to get to it.
Jungle beach was once a secret, nowadays it´s crowdy, and no hideaway. The Prices at the local Bar are very overpriced!!

Better than Unawatuna beach. Even it's a small beach, it's beautiful, more secluded and the road through the forest is beautiful. The little bar/restaurant is basic, but good enough to spend a few hours. The staff is very friendly. Simple dishes, fresh fish and seafood. They have also some fresh cocktails - the pina colada is a must.  Just perfect!

Tranquil and private. The trek to the beach makes it a great find! Love the waters here! Great for snorkelling. Try the approach road through the forest trek it's adventurous and worth the effort. If you are looking for a unique experience, this is the beach to visit!

This little beach around the point from Unawatuna was a great surprise.  We caught a tuk tuk there on what is a long and bumpy road only to find that it was packed - largely with locals having an absolute ball.  Such a beautful little bit of beach with a great vibe.  Definitely worth a visit.
Great beach and good little restuarant A must visit  within the area but beaches in mirissa and tangalle are better

This is a perfect small beach with free sunbeds and a great cafe/bar. We got here by Tuk tuk, but there is a walk down a rough path for the last part. You can walk from Unawatuna in about 15 - 20 mins.

Hike from Unawatuna town was about 30min and was pleasant.  Beach had good shade areas but even at fairly low tide no much of beach area.  Very crowded with mostly foreign but also some local visitors when we went.  Around the rocks there is another beach area much quieter.  There is a restaurant cafe serving food and drinks right there.

The walk from Unawatuna to Jungle beach is truly beautiful and not difficult if you're mobile. However, on our visit the beach was totally crammed with large parties of Russian tourists and it was effectively 'full'. There is not a lot of beach unless you catch it just at low tide, and if you do, and it's quiet it must be an really nice place. There are two small cafe places with a few chairs, but even there the first signs you see are in Russian. it was rather like Moscow-on-Sea, and one persons music filled the beach area. My advice, if you want a beautiful beach is to walk away from Unawatuna, away from the Galle direction, and you'll find three beautiful beaches, much better and virtually empty.

Lovely little beach and you might find monkeys playing in the trees. 30 minutes on foot, 15 by tuk tuk and depending on which cafe owner the driver's related to will determine which beach you get to as there are 2, about 300 yards apart.

We followed the signs from the west end of Unawatuna beach and walked up over the hill to jungle beach. This tool about 20 to 30 mins slow walking. The roads we ok and there were sign posts at all the junctions. Once there we found a small, clean and tidy beach which was busy but not over-crowded. There is a small cafe selling drinks and basic food. Prices were reasonable. There tide was nearly all the way in so the beach was not that big but the water was clean and reasonably clear and we had a good swim. Some others have said there beach is dirty and littered. These reviewers either went to the wrong beach or they locals have done a good clean up because I did not see one piece of litter. Nice beach to get away from the crowds at Unawatuna
Smaal beach. Have to walk there. Not many sunbeds, nice for snorkling. A few wild dogs.Not recommended for elderlt people.

I'm not quite sure why people bother going a long way just to get to the Jungle Beach. If your accomodation is right there, that's fine - the beach is pretty and surrounded by its namesake. The waves are not as strong as elsewhere if you stay close to the beach. It is very small, however, and the water is not what I'd call clear and clean, though it is not dirty either. What I liked most, actually, is the small adventure in climbing down to the beach when you start walking from the Unawatuna tourist area. Make sure you know how to get back, though, as the climb back up is more tiring and you will get lost easily if you try a different way. There is a main road where you can catch a tuk-tuk back. Personally, I prefer Unawatuna beach or any other beach that you can reach on a day trip.

You could take a tuk tuk ride or hike across the hills from unawatuna, or take a short boat ride. LOVELY PLACE FOR SNORKELLING ! and spending a quiet day away from the hustle bustle of unawatuna beach.
We climbed over the mountain to reach it from our hotel and found it both crowded and dirty. Over-hyped and hardly worth the effort.

it is a must see beach too small but very clean and private if not on a weekend , highly suggested to bring your own food like fruit or sandwiches as the only restaurant providing cooked food there is horrible, dirty and no one has a clue of how to cook a dish also fish is never fresh there,
I had a nice day there. Less people then at Unawatuna bay, but somebody told mу that during the weekend it`s really crowded with locals.
This is a beach that is not easy to reach from the hotels area in Unawatuna, which is fine. The worse thing, as this is the norm in Sri Lanka, is the poor manteined and dirty sands and waters.

We (me, my wife, our 12 year old daughter) loved Jungle Beach. More relaxed and laidback than the main Unawatuna beach, it's just a twenty minute walk away over the headland via the Peace Pagoda. Did a little snorkelling and saw some some quite groovy fish, but if you are a hardcore snorkeller I imagine it's nothing to write home about. Not a bad little place to eat. And so much less busy. Plus we loved the walk over from the Birdhouse in Unawatuna which is where we stayed and a place I'd definitely recommend.
Easy walk away from the town, lovely beach overlooking Galle.  A nice bar serving drinks and decent food at reasonable prices.  Much better than the main beach in Unawatuna.

Ask your tuktuk driver to take the jungle road. You see what's behind all the tourism of Unawatuna and were the villagers live. It is an easy way to get lost if you go on your own and you don't always see a lot of locals to ask the way, so maybe more clever to take tuktuks there before you go on you own by scooter or bike. The beach itself is a nice little place! I visited jungle beach on my second day in Sri Lanka and then it takes your breath away!

loved the food, view and relaxed atmosphere, no hawkers which is great Tuck Tuck from Unawatuna took five minutes, got there at lunch time, chose a lobster, noodles, and cold beer. Views are amazing, sea rushes in from time to time under your sun bed so make sure you don't put your bag, or book on the sand, and make sure your flip fops are on the ledge. take a towel. great afternoon out.....

This beach is a very famous tourism spot in Sri Lanka. This is about 5 km from Galle, a city in the southern part of the country. The water is crystal clear. You can see the sand at the bottom of the water very clearly. The beach is very clean and tidy - no littering. Lots of restaurants are available nearby. However parking is usually very tight during weekends. Be prepared to walk some distance. However the sight at the end of the road is worthwhile. During weekends you always find someone with a guitar belting out sweet music or skimpily dressed tourists playing beach volleyball. The Unawatuna beach resort offers a fantastic cuisine. Or you can visit the Light House - a star hotel in Galle.
It is in the nature, nice small beach, with no big waves, so you can swim. There is a restaurant with fresh fish and seafood. Very nice and relaxing!
As this was a close location to where we stayed we tried it and didnt like it much though, the sea was rough at the time and it was crowded. So didnt stay for a long time....
It was a short trek and worth it. The Beach bar really isn't much but the beach is nice. I don't think they serve food.

It really is a trek to get down to jungle beach after parking your car on top of the Rumassala hill near the temple. But the place is like something out of a movie.  Unfortunately there are far too many people there on most weekends so that feeling of having the entire beach to yourself is gone. Try going on a week day when there arent too many people.  There is a makeshift bar/cafe that serves beer and food as well as rent beach beds. But a really cool place to go go snorkelling and to chill.
was told secluded beach, it was for all of us tourists there, not that many only about 10 others nice, everywhere is nice anyway

Really can't rate this beach enough! Favourite in Sri Lanka. Lovely walk there through the jungle. Awesome snorkelling from the beach - a calm water cove with beautiful jungle backdrop. Lovely for a swim. Really friendly guys at the restaurant down there .. and delicious fresh fish ... Devilled fish and fresh fish with chips n salad ... Highly recommend. As I say - favourite beach in Sri Lanka!!

We had visited many beaches in Lanka and we found this one to be the best. First, its nested in teh middle of a small jungle, availability of food, water is the prettiest and cleanest. We spent a lot of time in the water and loved it. Must visit better than other beaches in Unawatuna region.

we took a day trip from Unawatuna to have a change of scenery. The beach was sheltered and the sea was very calm for swimming when we visited. There was no obvious sign of pollution and the beach appeared clean. It was worth visiting for a change of scenery but personally I am very contented with Unawatuna beach! I imagine that in peak season this small beach could get busy.
It takes us only 15-20 min walk to come in Jungle beach from Unawatuna beach. On the back way we saw wonderful temple (Pagoda) and statue of Budda. On back way we take tuk tuk for 200 rupiy

Its a nice walk down to Jungle beach. Once you're there you can relax on a small but cosy beach with wooden loungers, surrounded by palmtrees. You can also have a few drinks and some food at the local 'restaurant'. I don't really get the raving reviews, for us it was just okay, nothing special and nothing to rave about. Just a plain old okay if you want to go somewhere different.

Polluted beach--plastic bags, bottles and a lot of other rubbish, hence what was once a beautiful little beach is now a rubbish heap littered with garbage and strewn with dead coral--very depressing. Unbelievable how no one seems to care about this irreversible damage to the precious fragile coral.

Lovely little beach with a nice restuarant serving food and drinks. Great for swimming if the sea elsewhere is a bit rough. It can get a bi crowded though as it is rather small. And as there is only one place to buy food and drink its more expensive than other places (although still pretty cheap).

Love the peace and tranquility here, only a few tourists and locals about.  Had the best ever fried noodles from the food shack here - simply the best!!  Definitely worth a visit, remember to wear sensible shoes as there is only a rough footpath down a hill to this beach.

The beach is actually a very long stretch of sand, but we found our little paradise at the most left-hand corner. It is a lovely little secluded place with soft sand, blue sea and hot sun and nobody else. Just perfect. However, be careful when going swimming, as there are rocks underwater and the strength of waves can easily push you over. Also take plenty of sunscreen and your own supplies for the beach.
Took a tuk tuk to this beach which was clean with cafe & beer. Mix of locals and tourists, good for families, see a bit rough but ok for a shallow swim. Grab a sunbelt and chill
good view,keep all your valuables at hotel go by tuk tuk or boat spend the day with joy,remarkably good place.

Best to go there by Tuk Tuk but it's well worth a visit. The beach is small and secluded and there is a small beach restaurant which does good food and drinks. It's worth taking a walk along the path leading from the left of the beach along the seafront to the headland. You get a very good view across to Fort Galle and of local fishing boats coming back to the harbour.

Poor visibility for snorkelling, and you will risk having your belongings stolen by thuggish youths hanging around in the bushes. Also note that there is little shade in the afternoon so bring adequate sunscreen.

You can rent masks and snorkels on this seculded beach for great snorkeling on the left hand side. water is clean and lots of fish. You can walk up the hill to the Japanese dogoba after, good stop for sunbathing and reading. You can get there by tuk tuk or by boat from Unawatuna

We took a tuk tuk from our hotel (Jetwing Lighthouse) and then walked around 10 minutes. It is tucked away and seems to be popular with European tourists, so it seemed okay to be in your bikini. We originally had gone there for snorkeling, but in August the sea is a but murky. It is plenty good enough for a paddle and a swim though. Apparently, November/ December time is better for snorkeling as the sea is calmer.
Great beach with beach bar serving food & drinks, golden sand and good snorkeling. 20 minute walk from Coco Bay Hotel.
An OK little beach , nowhere to sit when the tide is high , leering fishermen , and rubbish strewn everywhere. Was a nice walk there , but hard to see what all the fuss is about.

This is a beautiful beach,from where you can also go snorkelling.We had asked a boatman at the Unawatuna beach and he agreed to take us there for  LKR 2000 each the next morning at 10am. Quite happy with the agreement we just shared our plan with the Dunes owner Gayan.He then guided us how to go because its very near. Walking would be a little tiring. You can hire a Tuk Tuk. Since we had a hired car we went there in the afternoon.Then there is a trail which you have to walk. A little further there is also a sign  board of Jungle Beach  which makes it easier to follow the right track.A little further  down and after  a few steps is this lovely beach.There is a small restaurant where you can eat and drink. To our surprise we met the same boat man who was serving there.We were happy that we saved LKR 4000.There were many tourists and locals enjoying the golden sand and the cool water. This is the best beach to go in Unawatuna and we loved it.
Great small beach , deserted with a cool shack on the beach grilling fresh seafood and serving cold beers, enjoy!

Loved jungle beach as it was isolated but I doubt it will be the same isolated place in the future as it is growing in popularity. The beach was really nice and the small shop that was on the beach had lion beer which we really enjoyed. Lots of tourists were there few locals but the atmosphere was great! Before going to jungle beach we visited the Temple which was an amazing sight and the view from the temple is great!
fab walk through the jungle to get there and clear sea and fishermen to watch. Bit rough monsoon time.
Beautiful Place and best time to visit at sunset. We went around 6 0' clock in the evening to watch a wonderful sunset.

Diane, a girl from the group I was traveling with, suggested we should go to the Jungle beach and I am really glad that she did. I had not heard of it and I was not that enthusiastic, as we only had an hour and half gap and we staying four minutes away from Unawatuna beach and that place was a little bit far, but I decided to go with her anyway. We took a tuk-tuk, you can actually walk trough the forest if you know the track, the tuk-tuk dropped us next to the Peace Pagoda and then we walk down to the beach. It is a small bay and can't see until you are actually there, we were even wondering whether we took the wright direction. I loved the Jungle Beach! There was only one couple there plus the guy, who is keeping the small coffee shop. He is the one who told us that it not always that quiet, as sometimes local guys come to drink arak there. However for the short time we were there nobody else came and for me it felt as if you were on a private beach. It is good for swimming and with a great view, as it is surrounded by the mountains. You can have a great photo session there too. I highly recommend to visit it, if you staying in Unawatuna. I am certainly glad that I did.
Nice beach. Not too easy to get (take tuk-tuk) but worth to see. Have little cafe. There is Japanese Buddhistic Temple near Jungle Beach - interesting place.
Lovely, quiet, picturesque. A great place for a romantic stroll or sunset as it was totally deserted during off season. Beautiful!
Loved the quaint charm of the area that seemed untouched by time and modernisation. The locals were laidback and the entire area was calm and serene despite the intense monsoon season sun.

it was a small jungle and small beach. but still, it was beautiful. a guy in Unawatuna told me that there are pink elephants and many iguanas in the jungle, but that was not true..that guy was so seriously joking! and i was so naive to believe what he said. haha...anyway..there are no elephants, only some butterflies and trees - the medical and herbal plants, that's what the local people say. but still, i was able to see one iguana that was disappearing into the bush. at the entrance of the jungle beach there is the japanese temple, which is also worth visiting.
Nice beach a tuk tuk ride away from unawatuna.  Try the lunch there.  We selected from catches of the day and they prepared it on site.  Fantastic.

This place is a little isolated and its good for snorkelling , interesting place where you can enjoy the beautiful blue calm water . There is only one place to eat at the beach with serves pretty decent food and drinks.
Clean, private, idyllic spot. You can walk here if local or get a tuk tuk easily either. Sheltered for swimming

Jungle Beach is less known to manny tourists who visit Unawatuna  and not accessible from  Unawatuna Beach by foot .Only way to reach jungle beach from Unawatuna beach is by boat and due to same reason its hidden from many who visit the area. The best way to reach Jungle beach is via Rumassala hil (Bonavista hil).Access lies about 4KM from galle and 2,5 km from Unawtuna on Galle/Matara road from right in front of Cement factory. Its an intresting climb about 3 km up the Bonavista hil and you climb down to the Jungle beach for a fantastic view of the Galle city.Road up the hil is motorable and you may get there by ,taxi or tuk tuk (Tree Wheeler) if you dont feel like tracking and save time and energy becaus climb can be too steep for people who are not used to. This beach is special for its location, beach imediately next to the jungle.Clean and sandy beach provides a fantstic panaromic view of the city of Galle and ideal place to watch sunset in the evenings. Clear and safe waters provides very good conditions for snorkling and swimming.
Great Bar at night time,  it really rocks even when its not busy.  Excellent service,  great food and drinks. Awesome beach front Bar.

had a great fun with my friends this was my last trip in Sri Lanka before i came to Saudi Arabia its the best place to have a safe sea bath in Unawatuwa area Its free of charge Its near the Wijaya beach Hotel in Unawatuwa cool and calm area where no much crowded playing only descent crowd are coming to this place
I met ellie In this place.. so i will never forget this place.. very romantic u should go but dont spoil its beuty ppl ...

Not easy to get there, requiring tuk-tuk and walk down a hill or by boat, but very pleasant for a beach day.  Beautiful ocean beach with jungle vegetation nearby for shade, kept well by someone and enjoyed by locals and tourists alike.  Nice and quiet, too.

We took a tuk-tuk to the top of the hill by the white pagoda and then had a short walk down a path to the beach. We arrived about 10.30 am and it wasn't crowded and we found sun loungers without any problem. Maybe it gets crowded in peak season but it was fine when we went. Had lunch at the one cafe that's there, which was much better than we expected. A toilet is also available which we found to be quite ok. The beach was clean and the water clear and we enjoyed our time there and would go back again, perhaps trying to follow the path from Unawatuna next time.

If you have time to kill its a nice walk there but we enjoyed the walk more than the beach itself. It is very pretty and secluded but there's so many great beaches in the south that its not a stand out.

A forty minute walk from Unawatuna past the new Peace Pagoda and down the jungly path and you come to this beach of dreams. It's sheltered and the sea is crystal clear. There's one ramshackle cafe/restaurant that provides a nice selection of snacks, meals and drinks - sometimes offering ocean fresh seafood. You can rent snorkels or shell out for diving trips and the wooden loungers on the beach are free to visitors who use the cafe.  When we were there there were no more than twenty five people on the beach. It is a place to smile and daydream about on dark winter nights in more northerly climes.

Jungle Beach is the place to head if you like snorkelling. It's a small bay just beyond Unawatuna towards Galle. There is an over-priced boat ride available from Unawatuna beach or a cheap five min tuc-tuc ride and a little walk down a path. The sand is soft and the water crystal clear making it the perfect place to see some fish. There are the standard wooden sun beds there although they don't have any cushions at present (something they said they were going to do for the next tourist season); they being the guys who run the beach cafe. You can get a reasonable selection of drinks here and an adequate food menu. We even saw some wild monkeys in the trees trying to steal the limelight!

We hiked to Jungle Beach from Unawatuna Beach.  We followed the signs and sometimes relied merely on our common sense and were there within 30 minutes.  The hike was great as we began on a paved road which became a small pathway winding through the Rumassala Jungle.  Soon we could see the stupa of the Peace Pagoda which sits directly above the beach.  We had some great views of the India Ocean before walking downward to Jungle Beach.  Many others had found the beach also.  In fact it is nearly accessible by moped or tuk tuk via a different pathway.  There is a beach shack there which serves cold beer and other drinks and some food.  The beach is small and it was pretty packed by 10:00 (people took boats to get there also).   I tried snorkeling but the water clarity is not good and there isn't much to see.  In short, the journey was much better than the beach!

This was the first time I went to Unawatuna and had a wonderful time there. We stayed at Happy Mooh Hotel next to Happy Banana and room was ok. The beach is clean and enjoyable. Night life is good met some new friends. Went on a small hiking trip and the view was awesome from the top of the rock.
Interesting but not a lot to do after you have seen it. The jungle does indeed go down right to the sea. I ran there early one morning from Unawatuna but would guess it is just an 1/2 hour walk.

This is the best beach I have seen in southern part of Sri Lanka. Can access both from boat and vehicle. If going by a vehicle you have to park it near Unawatuna Peace Temple and have a 5 minute walk to the beach. If use public transportation, have to get down near Unawatuna Cement factory and get a tuk tuk. I do not advise to go by foot because you have to walk a lot and same time the road have some steeps to climb. Beach is bit developed now and have good restaurant. But I don't know if it function on non tourist seasons (other than Nov - Mar). We could not find any changing rooms so have to search for the bushes close by. This is very good place if you are a good diver. Lots of sea creatures to see with lots of corals. Please bring your swimming gears and goggles because no one there to rent them. Please bring your garbage back with you. This is still a very clean beach.
Very clean, secluded beach. Ideal for snorkelling. Beautiful surroundings. Facilities available. Refreshments available.

Just a quick review - the toilet was clean WITH loo paper as well ! The food was better than average & it was very peaceful only about 20 people there.  It's worth an afternoon snorkeling as we saw some lovely fish on the coral.
but no real coral . plenty of fish and pretty enough good beach for kids because there is no swell great view of Galle from the Pagoda nearby and worth a look itself

This tiny little bay was mobbed with travellers/tourists/locals/dogs/cats etc...you name it, it was there. Its hardly serene or picturesque. Dont take your kids as just behind the sun loungers is a 'toilet' which can only be described as rancid. There are pebbles on which you can stand to save you wading  through human waste, to reach a small hut hidden in the trees..  I didnt get further than peering across and turned back! We left shortly afterwards to find somewhere cleaner.

Nice beach with a coffee & restaurant where you can lunch or snack. Prices are reasonable : 100 Rpees a coke, 450 for noodles (beware one portion is enough for 2 people!!) You can easily reach the beach by walking (15 mn from the center), the path is quite difficult to find. Ask locals!! A bit crowded at lunch time, better to go after 4:00 pm or before midday. Enjoy!!

Getting there was fun and a stop off at the temple made it worth our while. The beach is very nice but can get a bit crowded with boat trips. We stayed at Unawatuna and despite close proximity only visited the once.

It may not be the easiest place to find, but if you're near Galle and want a quiet, secluded beach to relax at, this is by far the pick of the area! There's a little restaurant / kiosk on the beach so you don't have to worry about packing your own food.

Jungle beach is just 15 minutes walking from the center of Unawatuna but you can also reach it easily by Tuk Tuk. The little beach is so beautiful and pure and the servie provided by Ajith and his staff is amazing!! They have daily fresh fish, probably the best we've had in Sri Lanka so far... the menu changes depending of what the fishermans bring in the morning (they deliver the fish straight on the beach!!!). Very nice also juices and cocktails freshly prepared with the local fruits. TO TRY !!!
Stunning beach and clean water. Not as deserted as would have liked but certainly isolated...a 20 minute trek from Unawatuna but well worth it.

Located a short Tuk Tuk ride, or a boat trip away from Unawatuna, Jungle beach offers beach location, snorkelling, swimming, crabbing within the rocks as well as a nice beach restaurant set in the palm trees. The walk down from where the Tuk Tuk drops you needs attention but is less than a 5 min walk. Free sun beds are available but not plentiful so you may have to wait your turn, it seemed that when we were there people were coming and going every few hours so beds became free on a regular basis. Well worth a trip to lounge in a wonderful beach paradise.
Not a long ride - but the beach is nothing particular...small beach, close to the forrest and a bit more people than perferable...

Great secluded beach, though can still be crowded. There is a hike to get there but it is a natural filter- it would be ten times busier. Bring snorkelling gear if you have it, the coral is bleached but there are still some colourful fish not far from the water's edge. BUT Don't both with the food unless you love REALLY average service. Calamari and chips has taken almost an hour and a half - still waiting. The guys at the restaurant seem more interested in chatting to foreign girls in bikinis, I know, they were very at tentative until my husband sat at the table.

The sea here is lovely and calm and delightful to swim in. This is a small beach and it gets very busy so be advised that you might not have a bed. There is only 1 place to eat here and even though the food is quite good it's a little pricey compared with some other places. But I would still recommend at least a day here!
We went here for the afternoon.  It was a nice beach as the locals used it and the sea was calm so we were able to swim out.
lovely sea and sand  and a lovely walk to get there  beautiful views  reasonable priced drinks but diesel from boats spoiled it as they keep going to and fro smell gets down your throat

You can get a tuktuk to take you to the top of the cliff, it is then quite a climb down a sort of path, not very good if you have walking difficulties, or like my husband recovering from a broken leg. The beach when you get to it is quite small with not many sun beds.

Our Tuk Tuk driver informed us of this beach and took us to it. It is a bit of a climb down to the beach, but well worth it. The crystal clear water is perfect for bathing and lovely golden sand. The small restaurant does a roaring trade and the food is very good. I expect this place was heaven a few years ago when it was not so well known, but it was not too crowded and a lovely place to stop and have a swim and chill for a few hours

We went there for around 2 hours by boat. We rented the boat for 2 hours for around $40 also on our way to the jungle beach we saw the fishes through the glass in the bottom of the fishing boat. also we saw the Japans temple on the way. it was really great beach with the white sand and very quit beach for relaxing and tanning.

It is a small place, luckily not too accessible. Come in the morning and be sure to bring your snorkling equipment to see all the beautiful tropical fish over the corals. You may choose to have your lunch at the one and only restaurant.

Unfortunately the day we went we had bad weather and it rained quite a lot on and off.  But it is a gorgeous little spot, secluded and quiet with just a few sun beds.  The little restaurant there does lovely cold lions and great seafood at lunch time.  Will return.

We walked here from our hotel. As we where walking we meet an elder from the area and he took us over the hill and through the bushes. What a fantast experience. We saw wild monkeys in the trees, rice fields and local homes. Everyone friendly and our guide was a lovely older gentleman. I paid him 2,000 Rupee which I know is alot but he was worth it.We where thrilled with the experiance my husband and i had.

Very small beach that would be very cool if only a few people there, but it was filled to near capacity the day we were there.  I'd check it out if staying in Galle or Unawatuna, but not worth a further trip to go.

Nice short walk to the Peace Pagoda where you can get a great view of Unawatuna bay.  The best snorkeling can be found around the rocks opposed to just off the beach.  Little restaurant that serves meals & cold drinks.

Fellow travellers had been telling us how nice Jungle beach was so on our last day (Saturday) in Unawatuna we took the bumpy 500 ruppee ride up and over the hill from Galle to Jungle Beach. I am sure people will rave about something there but I am blessed if I can see it. The small beach was packed with tourists and locals as was the limited swimming area and it was rocky underfoot too. We sat for a while after our swim but it was so crowded it became unpleasant so after an overpriced drink we left and walked half a kilometre up hill before we chanced upon a Tuk Tuk to take us back to Unawatuna.
perfect colour of the sea and very nice place for children's, good meal there - we tried a fresh lobster - wonderful taste and good price

It is a chalenginng location. You have to follow the main road (presently there is only one in Unavatuna) till it comes to a dead end. Then you have to get some exercise: climb down the rocky path, cross a creek and go up (same rocky path). Then finally you get to a flat passage: some teen minutes more and you'll be there... The Jungle Beach is in fact two beaches: in the nearest to you entrance point you will be offered sun beds and snacks (there is the one and only cafe working there). The other part of the beach is located across the rocks (it is not a difficult path, but still), and there are no facilities at all. It is a more relaxed place than the main Unavatuna's beach, less crowded and more laid-back, even during national holidays (which are plenty in January). There is only one spot where you may eat - that is a disadvantage. The advantage is that you have no annoying vendors of souvenirs. There are no big waves there - at least every time I went there, the water was alsolutely calm. My advise: if you want to go there, wear something better than flip-flaps: spare your ankles, the rocky path is rather challenging.

We were recommended to visit this beach by fellow hotel guests (long-stay).  Our three wheeler driver would only take us to the Peace Pagoda; from then on, a short walk to the beginning of the path down (look out for colourful centipedes on the road).  Bit of a scramble next to shrubs with wonderful aerial roots, down to the beach.  Clean, small, perhaps a dozen other people there, on deck chairs; later, a group of local students with a taste for arrack. What was unexpected was a beach cafe, plus another one (same owner) under construction.  The owner, who said he owns the land but is afraid of corrupt officials who might object to his current building, is having another one built - on outriggers.  So, if he is instructed to remove it, he can tug it away by sea! After this story, we could not resist eating here; we were shown the fish on offer (apparently locally caught), and chose a superb coral fish, served with salad and chips (unfortunately cold when they arrived), with as much Lion Lager as we wanted, all at a very reasonable price. The beach dogs all appear to be friendly, and are appreciative of scraps! After a couple of hours, back to Galle. This time, the (different) three wheeler driver was more adventurous, and had driven to the top of the track.
Beatiful but plenty of other tourists. Acces is not very easy but lovely beach, think worth a side trip from Unawatuna, especially if you are not going to other undeveloped beaches.

The walk to the Jungle Beach sets expectations high and on reaching the beach we weren't dissappointed. I'm glad we arrived early as there are limited beds and space generally. Tried to snorkel but the water was very murky. The only thing is, that this lovely little spot is not a well kept secret so by the afternoon it was chocca and we had to wait over an hour for a sandwich from the little beach shack. Still, worth a visit.

Almost reluctant to write this review as I have been enjoying Jungle Beach's remote beauty for decades and it is now getting quite busy. The beach itself has gone full circle from a sandy bay to being strewn with dead coral as a result of illegal blasting for fish and then being swept wonderfully clean again by the tsunami - well it had to do some good. Over the last couple of years the path down ha been made bigger/easier and a cafe has opened up and provided sun beds. The sand and sea here are beautiful and with the main Unwatuna beach suffering erosion in recent years it's no wonder more people are using it.  The second beach which is a clamber over the rocks or requires a boat trip is still very quiet.
tiny, overcroweded, and trash floating in the water.  Don't bother with this beach.  Take a tuk tuk south to Mirissa.
The easy way to get there is by tok tok.there is no wawe and almost no people. nice.Remember to bring somthing to drink.

Such a long trip down bumpy roads to this beach.. Also, not the cleanest of beaches I thought, and the toilets available on the beach were pretty grim. Only the one restaurant, the staff were very friendly and helpful, and assisted us ordering a tuk tuk to get us OUT of Jungle beach. It was raining the day we went which probably didn't help. Nicer sea and views from Unawatuna, stay there!!
Beautiful beach and clear ocean water... worth to visit! Great and safe snorkeling! We got there by Tuk-Tuk ride and it was definitely worth it.
Fantastic food freshly caught and cooked on the beach. Catch a tuk tuk or boat as it is quite a walk to get to it.

Have been there only once and really sorry we didn't manage to come back at least once again while staying in Sri Lanka. The place is great. I would say it is better that Unawatuna beach. Jungle beach is not big but the beach is great and water is clear. They have beds there and a restaurant. We ordered vegetable which turned out to be really tasty. I would definitely recommend to visit this place to everyone.

Jungle beach is a stunning little hidden beach. Only a 20 minutes walk from the busy centre of Unawatuna, up the hill with a wonderful view of the sea. It's also possible to take a tuktuk up to the hill. This beach is a very good alternative for the more busy beach in the centre, which is full of restaurants. Jungle beach only has one small restaurant which serves tasty fresh fish and has a very nice staff.

A joyous moment is even more so when it comes unexpectedly! This beach was being visited as an afterthought since we had time on our hands. We spotted a medium sized monitor lizard crossing the road on the way to the pagoda. You need to walk down from the pagoda and take a right at the first footpath/trail you get to reach the beach down below. We broke a flip flop on the way and the staff at the small resto-cafe there bought us a new one from the market!!! We ordered a grilled fish in lemon butter sauce. It was super fresh, caught monutes ago from the corals slightly up ahead in the sea. Snorkelling was great in the cam waters, spotted the same kind of fish we ate and a few others. some tiny rock crabs as well. Water was clear, visibility only hampered by the setting sun. Make sure you go for 2-3 hours, within sunlight time. They have a very scary loo. Beware! Relieve yourself before you visit here.
One of the more secluded beaches if you want to get away from the rush and crowd of Unwatuna. Excellent trek down and if you are lucky you get to see the monitor lizard in the wild.

We spend a couple of hours snorkling at Jungle Beach in Unawatuna. It was nice but the water was not that clear. There are many corals and fish. We saw Octopus, Pufferfish and lots of other small fishes.

Unfortunately this beach is no longer the hidden gem the travel guides claimed it to be.  It's now pretty much on the visit list for anyone who's even remotely intrepid which means you won't get away from the crowds. The beach does have a nice relaxed feel to it however, with very tranquil waters which are perfect for wading or swimming, especially with young kids.  There's a small cafe/restaurant which serves fresh fruit and seafood and has a friendly staff.

Had read online and in my guide book that jungle beach are suppose to be a secluded beach. It's not. At least not if your coming to the beach after nine in the morning. But it's so much betterr than Unawatuna beach wich is lacking places to sit on the beach without getting wet. The beach is perfect for kids though, the waves are much smaller than those at Unawatuna beach. This in addition to the rocks make it perfect for snorkelling. There's a restaurant on the beach. Make sure you reserve a table and order your food at a certain time or else your risking to gave to wait for an hour and a half to get the food. To get here you can either trekk in the jungle for 45 minutes or take a tuktuk.There is no toilet on the beach, at least if you don't want to be part of ruining the beach (everything that goes in the toilet goes straight in to a nasty smelling lake right beside it).

We took a boat to Jungle Beach but I'd suggest you just make your own way on foot/tuk-tuk.  Peaceful and good for a snorkel although visibility was not great.  Great place to kick back for a few hours but try and go in the morning before most of the crowd gets there.

A pretty secluded beach that has calmer waters than Unawatuna. The beach itself is pretty small and the toilet is very "interesting" but you don't have to worry about any currents. There were more people snorkelling there than what I saw at Unawatuna but I can't speak for the snorkelling itself.
The path to reach jungle beach is nice..very quite and calm place. spend almost 5 to 6 hours chilling out there..!!

This little beach was off the beaten track but was well worth it.  You walk through rough terrain for about 20 minutes to emerge onto a beautiful beach with clear water lapping at the shore.  The walk itself is stunning and we came across monkeys and other animals on the way.  There are no shops or refreshments there so if you're making a day of it, bring your beers with you!

We just walked to Jungle beach through a bit of scrub land round the back and spent the morning there. I didn't find it polluted at all, the water was clear and the sand was beautiful. The sea was calmer for swimming in here, so I really enjoyed that as I wouldn't swim on Una beach. It isn't a very big beach and because all the local tuk tuk drivers are touting it as a trip out, its getting busier, but it was still nice and worthwhile making the effort to get there.

Coming from a country with hundreds of amazing beaches it was hard to get excited about this one which faces a cement works.  As 2 females on a beach with approx 15 male fishermen we did not feel at all comfortable and left after a few minutes.  By contrast the Peace Temple at the top is utterly stunning and a very special place.
After a 15 min rickshaw drive and a short walk we reached this somewhat secluded beach between Unawatuna and Galle. Unfortunately the beach and surroundings are quite polluted.
If you don´t know what to do, this is a nice little walk. The bay itself is not very spectacular but still.

It is a quiet small stretch of beach with few people, and blissfully calm waves. We took a catamaran out for a snorkel - it was a big waste. the corals are all dead and there are just a few fish. Not worth it at all. its better to just laze in the water or swim. However - there was a bit of litter in the water - wish it could be cleaned up...
nice little beach away from the main Unawatuna beach. Much more sheltered than the main beach. better for snorkeling although not great.

Walked in flip flops the wrong and long way. To where the road ended. The path got more and more narrow and we where in jungle land. Then it opened up. A beach like no other. No people. No shops. Just a handful of fishermen in a corner and some blue sunchairs. Very cool. Only accesible by foot or boat.

It is a nice place but definitely no secret place. We had some 25 local people leaving the beach when we arrived and 3 more - smaller groups - around and a couple of foreigners. Not really silent but different and good for swimming.
An enjoyable and in comparison quiet/remote beach.   Snorkelling not as good as they say but plenty of fish near the rocks on the left.

Beautiful, virgin beach...best for snorkling and relaxing. There are 2 choices to reach the place. 1. with car/tuk tuk/motor bike. It will take you until the Chinese temple, then you have to walk trough the jungle to get to the beach. 2. with boat from unawatuna beach (quite expensive) my suggestion, take a bit of adventure to cross the jungle :-)

A bit of a hike from where the car can park on a hot day but well worth it..gorgeous little cover surrounded by coconut trees. Very unspoilt but with sun loungers and a juice bar. Much better than Unawhatuna Beach. Unfortunately it rained on the day we went.
The place where you can meet the locals, we didn't see any tourists at all. The ocean is not as wild as at Unawatuna beach. The sun beds are free of charge and the drinks cheap. Go there!

lovely beach, but polluted by building and shacks. The sea is shallow, and its perfect for relaxing and swimming. Safe for children for swimming. But one part of the beach is overcrowded and a bit dirty. And there are two many tiny huts which have been built two close to the shore without proper planning. This has taken away the beauty from the beach.
Beautiful beach - a bit of a treck from the village (Unawatuna) - but well worth it.
